verses.after: The moon’s light will be like the sun’s, and the sun’s light seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, when the **LORD** binds his people’s fracture and heals the wound from his blow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound they were struck with.

verses.rationale: Retain coming name and difficult burden expression.
verses.before: Look, the name of the LORD comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire.
verses.after: Look! The name of the **LORD** comes from afar, his anger burning, his burden heavy. His lips are full of indignation, his tongue like devouring fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the name of the LORD comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire.

verses.rationale: Keep three judgment images and misleading bridle.
verses.before: His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.
verses.after: His breath is like a flooding stream rising to the neck, sifting nations in a sieve of destruction; a bridle that leads astray is on the peoples’ jaws.
verses.tsw_comparator: His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.

verses.rationale: Preserve festival-night setting and divine Rock.
verses.before: You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to the LORD's mountain, to Israel's Rock.
verses.after: You will have a song as on a night when a festival is consecrated, and gladness of heart like those who go with a flute to the **LORD**’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to the LORD's mountain, to Israel's Rock.

verses.rationale: Keep arm action and weather catalogue.
verses.before: The LORD will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
verses.after: The **LORD** will make his majestic voice heard and show his arm descending, with furious anger and devouring flame, cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.

verses.rationale: Keep divine strike and named target.
verses.before: For through the voice of the LORD the Assyrian will be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.
verses.after: At the **LORD**’s voice Assyria will be shattered; he will strike with the rod.
verses.tsw_comparator: For through the voice of the LORD the Assyrian will be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.

verses.rationale: Preserve him/them shift following read-form plural.
verses.before: Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which the LORD will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.
verses.after: Every stroke of the appointed staff that the **LORD** brings down upon him will be accompanied by tambourines and lyres; with swinging blows he will battle them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which the LORD will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.

verses.rationale: Retain prepared burning place and sulfur breath.
verses.before: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is made ready. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. the LORD's breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
verses.after: Topheth has long been prepared; it is made ready even for the king. Its fire pit is deep and wide, with fire and wood in abundance. The **LORD**’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, sets it ablaze.
verses.tsw_comparator: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is made ready. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. the LORD's breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.

verses.rationale: Keep military abundance contrasted with unasked divine help.
verses.before: Woe to people who go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they do not look to the Holy One of Israel, and they do not seek the LORD!
verses.after: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, leaning on horses, trusting chariots because they are many and horsemen because they are very strong, but not looking to Israel’s Holy One or seeking the **LORD**!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they do not look to the Holy One of Israel, and they do not seek the LORD!

verses.rationale: Preserve ironic wisdom and culpable helpers.
verses.before: Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evil-doers, and against the help of people who work iniquity.
verses.after: Yet he too is wise; he brings disaster and does not take back his words. He will rise against the house of evildoers and against the helpers of those who do wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evil-doers, and against the help of those who work iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keep flesh/spirit contrast and both parties’ failure.
verses.before: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, both the one who helps will stumble, and the one who is helped will fall, and they all will be consumed together.
verses.after: The Egyptians are human, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the **LORD** stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble and the helped will fall; together they will all perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, both the one who helps will stumble, and the one who is helped will fall, and they all will be consumed together.

verses.rationale: Retain lion resolve and open force of on/for/against Zion.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD to me, "As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds is called together against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them, so the LORD of Hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
verses.after: For the **LORD** said this to me: “As a lion, a young lion, growls over its prey, though a whole band of shepherds is called against it, not frightened by their voices nor subdued by their uproar, so the **LORD** of hosts will descend to fight on Mount Zion and its hill.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD to me, "As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds is called together against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them, so the LORD of Hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.

verses.rationale: Keep bird metaphor and passing-over verb.
verses.before: As birds hovering, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it. He will pass over and preserve it."
verses.after: Like birds in flight, the **LORD** of hosts will shield Jerusalem; shielding, he will deliver it; passing over, he will rescue it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As birds hovering, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it. He will pass over and preserve it."

verses.rationale: Make addressed people explicit within return appeal.
verses.before: Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.
verses.after: Return to the one against whom you Israelites have rebelled so deeply.
verses.tsw_comparator: Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep human manufacture and paired metals.
verses.before: For on that day everyone will cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold—sin which your own hands have made for you.
verses.after: On that day each of you will reject the silver idols and gold idols your own hands made for you as a sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: For in that day everyone will cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold—sin which your own hands have made for you.

verses.rationale: Preserve nonhuman sword and enslavement aftermath.
verses.before: "The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of humanity, will devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will become subject to forced labor.
verses.after: “Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; a sword not of humanity will devour him. He will flee before the sword, and his young men will become forced laborers.
verses.tsw_comparator: "The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of humanity, will devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will become subject to forced labor.

verses.rationale: Keep uncertain rock metaphor and divine furnace.
verses.before: His rock will pass away by reason of terror, and his princes will be afraid of the banner," says the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.
verses.after: His rock will pass away in terror; his officials will panic at the signal,” declares the **LORD**, whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: His rock will pass away by reason of terror, and his princes will be afraid of the banner," says the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep righteous rule and distinct governing roles.
verses.before: Look, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule in justice.
verses.after: Look! A king will reign in righteousness, and officials will govern with justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule in justice.

verses.rationale: Retain four protective comparisons and distributive man.
verses.before: A man will be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
verses.after: Each will be like a shelter from wind, a refuge from a storm, like streams in a dry place, like a great rock’s shade in a weary land.
verses.tsw_comparator: A man will be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.

verses.rationale: Preserve sensory reversal of earlier hardening.
verses.before: The eyes of people who see will not be dim, and the ears of people who hear will listen.
verses.after: The eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will pay attention.
verses.tsw_comparator: The eyes of those who see will not be dim, and the ears of those who hear will listen.

verses.rationale: Keep haste transformed into ready speech.
verses.before: The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.
verses.after: Impulsive minds will understand and know; stammering tongues will speak readily and clearly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.

verses.rationale: Retain social misnaming corrected.
verses.before: The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.
verses.after: A fool will no longer be called noble, nor a scoundrel be described as generous.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

verses.rationale: Connect false speech with concrete hunger and thirst.
verses.before: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practice profanity, and to utter error against the LORD, To make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
verses.after: For a fool speaks folly and plots wrongdoing in his heart: practicing godlessness, speaking error about the **LORD**, leaving the hungry empty and depriving the thirsty of drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practice profanity, and to utter error against the LORD, To make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.

verses.rationale: Follow poor read-form and preserve judicial harm.
verses.before: The ways of the scoundrel are evil. He devises wicked devices to destroy the humble with lying words, even when the needy speaks right.
verses.after: The scoundrel’s tools are evil. He devises schemes to ruin the poor with lying words, even when the needy plead a just case.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ways of the scoundrel are evil. He devises wicked devices to destroy the humble with lying words, even when the needy speaks right.

verses.rationale: Keep threefold noble repetition.
verses.before: But the noble devises noble things; and he will continue in noble things.
verses.after: But the noble person devises noble things and stands by noble things.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the noble devises noble things; and he will continue in noble things.

verses.rationale: Preserve specifically female audience.
verses.before: Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice! You careless daughters, give ear to my speech!
verses.after: Rise, women at ease, and hear my voice! Confident daughters, listen to what I say!
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice! You careless daughters, give ear to my speech!

verses.rationale: Keep stated interval and two failed harvests.
verses.before: For days beyond a year you will be troubled, you careless women; for the vintage will fail. The harvest will not come.
verses.after: In a year and some days you confident women will tremble, for the grape harvest will fail and no fruit gathering will come.
verses.tsw_comparator: For days beyond a year you will be troubled, you careless women; for the vintage will fail. The harvest will not come.

verses.rationale: Retain exposure and mourning garment supplied contextually.
verses.before: Tremble, you women who are at ease! Be troubled, you careless ones! Strip yourselves, make yourselves naked, and put sackcloth on your waist.
verses.after: Shudder, women at ease! Tremble, confident women! Strip yourselves bare and tie sackcloth around your waists.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tremble, you women who are at ease! Be troubled, you careless ones! Strip yourselves, make yourselves naked, and put sackcloth on your waist.

verses.rationale: Follow breasts rather than emend fields in first phrase.
verses.before: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
verses.after: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,
verses.tsw_comparator: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.

verses.rationale: Keep land and urban joy losses together.
verses.before: Thorns and briars will come up on my people's land; yes, on all the houses of joy in the joyous city.
verses.after: for my people’s soil, overgrown with thorns and briers, for every joyful house in the jubilant city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thorns and briars will come up on my people's land; yes, on all the houses of joy in the joyous city.

verses.rationale: Preserve forever even before until-next-verse tension.
verses.before: For the palace will be forsaken. The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;
verses.after: The palace is abandoned, the noisy city deserted. Citadel and watchtower become caves forever, a delight for wild donkeys, pasture for flocks,
verses.tsw_comparator: For the palace will be forsaken. The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;

verses.rationale: Retain spirit/wind openness and landscape echo29:17.
verses.before: Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.
verses.after: until a spirit is poured on us from on high. Then the wilderness becomes fruitful land, and fruitful land is regarded as forest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.

verses.rationale: Keep paired moral qualities inhabiting changed land.
verses.before: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness will remain in the fruitful field.
verses.after: Justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness live in fruitful land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness will remain in the fruitful field.

verses.rationale: Preserve righteousness causing peace and security.
verses.before: The work of righteousness will be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
verses.after: The work of righteousness will be peace, its effect quietness and confidence forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: The work of righteousness will be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.

verses.rationale: Keep three habitation descriptions.
verses.before: My people will abide in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
verses.after: My people will live in a home of peace, in secure dwellings and restful places free from fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: My people will abide in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.

verses.rationale: Retain difficult hail/city interruption as concessive.
verses.before: Though hail flattens the forest, and the city is leveled completely.
verses.after: Though hail brings the forest down and the city is brought very low,
verses.tsw_comparator: Though hail flattens the forest, and the city is leveled completely.

verses.rationale: Keep sowing and unrestrained working animals.
verses.before: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.
verses.after: happy are you who sow beside every water, letting ox and donkey roam free.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.

verses.rationale: Preserve mirrored actions and consequences.
verses.before: Woe to you who destroy, but you were not destroyed; and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have made an end of betrayal, you will be betrayed.
verses.after: Woe, destroyer who has not been destroyed, betrayer whom no one has betrayed! When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; when you end your betrayal, they will betray you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you who destroy, but you were not destroyed; and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have made an end of betrayal, you will be betrayed.

verses.rationale: Retain source their/our shift without harmonization.
verses.before: O LORD, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
verses.after: **LORD**, show us favor; we wait for you. Be their arm each morning, our salvation in a time of distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.

verses.rationale: Keep divine rising and scattered nations.
verses.before: At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled. When you lift yourself up, the nations are scattered.
verses.after: At the sound of tumult peoples flee; when you rise, nations scatter.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled. When you lift yourself up, the nations are scattered.

verses.rationale: Retain collective scavenging comparison.
verses.before: Your spoil will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.
verses.after: Your plunder is gathered as the locust gathers; as locusts rush, people rush upon it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your spoil will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.

verses.rationale: Repeat paired civic virtues.
verses.before: The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
verses.after: The **LORD** is exalted, for he dwells on high; he fills Zion with justice and righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.

verses.rationale: Preserve your/his shifts and treasury metaphor.
verses.before: There will be stability in your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is your treasure.
verses.after: He will be the stability of your times, a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the **LORD** is his treasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: There will be stability in your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is your treasure.

verses.rationale: Keep uncertain valiant-one term and failed envoys.
verses.before: Look, their valiant ones cry outside; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
verses.after: Look, their valiant ones cry outside; messengers of peace weep bitterly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, their valiant ones cry outside; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.

verses.rationale: Retain pinned cities rather than witnesses emendation.
verses.before: The highways are desolate. The traveling man ceases. The covenant is broken. He has despised the cities. He does not regard man.
verses.after: Highways lie desolate; travelers have stopped. He has broken the covenant, despised cities, and has no regard for anyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: The highways are desolate. The traveling man ceases. The covenant is broken. He has despised the cities. He does not regard man.

verses.rationale: Preserve four named regions and desert comparison.
verses.before: The land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is confounded and withers away. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.
verses.after: The land mourns and droops; Lebanon is ashamed and withers. Sharon has become like the Arabah; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is confounded and withers away. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.

verses.rationale: Keep threefold now and elevation.
verses.before: "Now I will arise," says the LORD; "Now I will lift myself up. Now I will be exalted.
verses.after: “Now I will rise,” says the **LORD**. “Now I will be exalted; now I will be lifted high.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Now I will arise," says the LORD; "Now I will lift myself up. Now I will be exalted.

verses.rationale: Retain failed pregnancy and self-consuming breath.
verses.before: You will conceive chaff. You will bring forth stubble. Your breath is a fire that will devour you.
verses.after: You conceive dry grass and give birth to stubble; your breath is a fire that consumes you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will conceive chaff. You will bring forth stubble. Your breath is a fire that will devour you.

verses.rationale: Keep lime-burning and cut-thorn comparisons.
verses.before: The peoples will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.
verses.after: Peoples will be burned to lime, like cut thorns set ablaze.
verses.tsw_comparator: The peoples will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.

verses.rationale: Preserve paired geographic audiences.
verses.before: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and, you who are near, acknowledge my might."
verses.after: You far away, hear what I have done! You nearby, acknowledge my might!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and, you who are near, acknowledge my might."

verses.rationale: Keep fearful questions and fire as divine presence context.
verses.before: The sinners in Zion are afraid. Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?
verses.after: Sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the godless: “Who among us can live with devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The sinners in Zion are afraid. Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?

verses.rationale: Preserve six ethical actions and embodied refusals.
verses.before: the one who walks righteously, and speaks blamelessly; the one who despises the gain of oppressions, who gestures with his hands, refusing to take a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from looking at evil—
verses.after: The one who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, rejects profit from oppression, shakes off a bribe from his hands, stops his ears against talk of bloodshed, and closes his eyes against evil—
verses.tsw_comparator: the one who walks righteously, and speaks blamelessly; the one who despises the gain of oppressions, who gestures with his hands, refusing to take a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from looking at evil—

verses.rationale: Keep bread/water sufficiency and rocky height.
verses.before: he will dwell on high. His place of defense will be the fortress of rocks. His bread will be supplied. His waters will be sure.
verses.after: that person will dwell on high; rocky strongholds will be his refuge. His bread will be supplied; his water will be secure.
verses.tsw_comparator: he will dwell on high. His place of defense will be the fortress of rocks. His bread will be supplied. His waters will be sure.

verses.rationale: Retain unnamed king and expansive land.
verses.before: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty. They will see a distant land.
verses.after: Your eyes will see a king in his beauty; they will see a land stretching far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty. They will see a distant land.

verses.rationale: Preserve officials’ unnamed functions and three questions.
verses.before: Your heart will meditate on the terror. Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?
verses.after: Your heart will recall the terror: “Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your heart will meditate on the terror. Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?

verses.rationale: Keep intimidating unintelligible language.
verses.before: You will no longer see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that you cannot comprehend, with a strange language that you cannot understand.
verses.after: You will no longer see the insolent people, the people whose speech is too obscure to understand, whose stammering tongue makes no sense.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will no longer see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that you cannot comprehend, with a strange language that you cannot understand.

verses.rationale: Keep secure tent metaphor and festival identity.
verses.before: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that will not be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
verses.after: Look at Zion, city of our appointed festivals! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful home, a tent that will not be moved, whose stakes will never be pulled up, whose ropes will never be snapped.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that will not be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.

verses.rationale: Preserve protective waterways without military ships.
verses.before: But there the LORD will be with us in majesty, a place of broad rivers and streams, in which no galley with oars will go, neither will any gallant ship pass by there.
verses.after: There the majestic **LORD** will be for us a place of rivers, broad waterways, where no rowing ship goes and no mighty vessel passes.
verses.tsw_comparator: But there the LORD will be with us in majesty, a place of broad rivers and streams, in which no galley with oars will go, neither will any gallant ship pass by there.

verses.rationale: Retain three full divine names and roles.
verses.before: For the LORD is our judge. the LORD is our lawgiver. the LORD is our king. He will save us.
verses.after: For the **LORD** is our judge, the **LORD** our lawgiver, the **LORD** our king; he will save us.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is our judge. the LORD is our lawgiver. the LORD is our king. He will save us.

verses.rationale: Preserve abrupt ship address and weak sharing plunder.
verses.before: Your rigging is untied. They could not strengthen the foot of their mast. They could not spread the sail. Then the prey of a great spoil was divided. The lame took the prey.
verses.after: Your ropes hang loose; they do not hold the mast firm or spread the sail. Then abundant plunder will be divided; even the lame will take the spoil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your rigging is untied. They could not strengthen the foot of their mast. They could not spread the sail. Then the prey of a great spoil was divided. The lame took the prey.

verses.rationale: Keep sickness and forgiveness linked but not explained causally.
verses.before: The inhabitant will not say, "I am sick." The people who dwell in it will be forgiven their iniquity.
verses.after: No inhabitant will say, “I am sick.” The people living there will have their guilt forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The inhabitant will not say, "I am sick." The people who dwell in it will be forgiven their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Retain widening summons to creation.
verses.before: Come near, you nations, to hear! Listen, you peoples. Let the earth and all it contains hear; the world, and everything that comes from it.
verses.after: Come near, nations, and hear; peoples, pay attention! Let the earth and all that fills it listen, the world and all that springs from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come near, you nations, to hear! Listen, you peoples. Let the earth and all it contains hear; the world, and everything that comes from it.

verses.rationale: Preserve herem destruction and military scope.
verses.before: For the LORD is enraged against all the nations, and angry with all their armies. He has utterly destroyed them. He has given them over for slaughter.
verses.after: The **LORD** is angry with all nations, furious with all their armies. He has devoted them to destruction, handed them over for slaughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is enraged against all the nations, and angry with all their armies. He has utterly destroyed them. He has given them over for slaughter.

verses.rationale: Keep graphic bodily aftermath and hyperbolic landscape.
verses.before: Their slain will also be cast out, and the stench of their dead bodies will come up; and the mountains will melt in their blood.
verses.after: Their slain will be thrown out; the stench of their corpses will rise, and mountains will melt with their blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their slain will also be cast out, and the stench of their dead bodies will come up; and the mountains will melt in their blood.

verses.rationale: Retain cosmic host and scroll plus leaf comparisons.
verses.before: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.
verses.after: All heaven’s host will decay, and the heavens roll up like a scroll. All their host will wither, like a leaf withering on a vine, like one withering on a fig tree.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.

verses.rationale: Preserve first-person divine sword and Edom target.
verses.before: For my sword has drunk its fill in the sky. Look, it will come down on Edom, and on the people of my curse, for judgment.
verses.after: “My sword has drunk its fill in heaven. Look! It descends on Edom, on the people I have devoted to destruction, for judgment.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For my sword has drunk its fill in the sky. Look, it will come down on Edom, and on the people of my curse, for judgment.

verses.rationale: Keep sacrificial anatomy and two divine names.
verses.before: The LORD's sword is filled with blood. It is covered with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
verses.after: The **LORD** has a sword filled with blood, smeared with fat— the blood of lambs and goats, the fat of rams’ kidneys. For the **LORD** has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in Edom’s land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD's sword is filled with blood. It is covered with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

verses.rationale: Retain larger animals and gruesome fertility metaphor.
verses.before: The wild oxen will come down with them, and the young bulls with the mighty bulls; and their land will be drunken with blood, and their dust made greasy with fat.
verses.after: Wild oxen will fall with them, young bulls with mighty bulls. Their land will drink its fill of blood, and their dust be enriched with fat.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wild oxen will come down with them, and the young bulls with the mighty bulls; and their land will be drunken with blood, and their dust made greasy with fat.

verses.rationale: Keep day/year and judicial cause.
verses.before: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
verses.after: For the **LORD** has a day of vengeance, a year of repayment for Zion’s cause.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.

verses.rationale: Clarify land referent while retaining burning substances.
verses.before: Its streams will be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, And its land will become burning pitch.
verses.after: Edom’s streams will turn to pitch, its dust to sulfur; its land will become burning pitch.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its streams will be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, And its land will become burning pitch.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated unending desolation.
verses.before: It will not be quenched night nor day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. No one will pass through it forever and ever.
verses.after: Night and day it will not go out; its smoke will rise forever. From generation to generation it will lie waste; no one will pass through it forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will not be quenched night nor day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. No one will pass through it forever and ever.

verses.rationale: Keep uncertain fauna and tohu/bohu creation reversal.
verses.before: But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it. The owl and the raven will dwell in it. He will stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness.
verses.after: Pelican and hedgehog will possess it; owl and raven will live there. He will stretch over it the measuring line of emptiness and the plumb stones of waste.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it. The owl and the raven will dwell in it. He will stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness.

verses.rationale: Render compressed kingship collapse and retain uncertainty in note.
verses.before: They will call its nobles to the kingdom, but none will be there; and all its princes will be nothing.
verses.after: Its nobles—there is no one there to proclaim king; all its officials will be nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will call its nobles to the kingdom, but none will be there; and all its princes will be nothing.

verses.rationale: Preserve abandoned power centers and returning fauna.
verses.before: Thorns will come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it will be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.
verses.after: Thorns will rise in its palaces, nettles and brambles in its strongholds. It will become a home for jackals, an enclosure for ostriches.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thorns will come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it will be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.

verses.rationale: Retain named night being rather than silently zoologize.
verses.before: The wild animals of the desert will meet with the wolves, and the wild goat will cry to his fellow. Yes, the night creature will settle there, and will find herself a place of rest.
verses.after: Desert creatures will meet hyenas; a goat-demon will call to its fellow. There Lilith will settle and find herself a resting place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wild animals of the desert will meet with the wolves, and the wild goat will cry to his fellow. Yes, the night creature will settle there, and will find herself a place of rest.

verses.rationale: Keep nesting sequence and uncertain owl identification.
verses.before: The arrow snake will make her nest there, and lay, hatch, and gather under her shade. Yes, the kites will be gathered there, every one with her mate.
verses.after: There an owl will nest and lay eggs, hatch them and gather her young in her shade. There the kites will gather, each with its mate.
verses.tsw_comparator: The arrow snake will make her nest there, and lay, hatch, and gather under her shade. Yes, the kites will be gathered there, every one with her mate.

verses.rationale: Retain pinned my/his shift and paired animals.
verses.before: Search in the book of the LORD, and read: not one of these will be missing. none will lack her mate. For my mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered them.
verses.after: Seek in the **LORD**’s scroll and read: not one of these will be missing; none will lack its mate. For my mouth has commanded it, and his spirit has gathered them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Search in the book of the LORD, and read: not one of these will be missing. none will lack her mate. For my mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered them.

verses.rationale: Keep land-allotment language for animals.
verses.before: He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them with a measuring line. They will possess it forever. From generation to generation they will dwell in it.
verses.after: He has cast the lot for them; his hand has divided it for them with a measuring line. They will possess it forever, live there from generation to generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them with a measuring line. They will possess it forever. From generation to generation they will dwell in it.

verses.rationale: Keep personified landscape and uncertain flower identification.
verses.before: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.
verses.after: The wilderness and dry land will rejoice; the desert plain will celebrate and bloom like a meadow flower.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.

verses.rationale: Repeat glory/splendor and restore three named landscapes.
verses.before: It will blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Lebanon's glory Lebanon will be given to it, the excellence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the LORD's glory, the excellence of our God.
verses.after: It will bloom abundantly, celebrate with joy and singing. Lebanon’s glory will be given to it, Carmel’s and Sharon’s splendor. They will see the **LORD**’s glory, our God’s splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Lebanon's glory Lebanon will be given to it, the excellence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the LORD's glory, the excellence of our God.

verses.rationale: Retain bodily encouragement.
verses.before: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
verses.after: Strengthen slack hands; make trembling knees firm.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.

verses.rationale: Keep vengeance as part of rescue announcement.
verses.before: Tell people who have a fearful heart, "Be strong. Don't be afraid. Look, your God will come with vengeance, God's retribution. He will come and save you.
verses.after: Tell those with anxious hearts, “Be strong! Do not fear! Look, your God will come with vengeance, with God’s repayment. He himself will come and save you.”

verses.after: Through your servants you have insulted the Lord. You said, ‘With my many chariots I climbed the highest mountains, Lebanon’s farthest reaches. I cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses; I reached its remotest heights, its luxuriant forest.
verses.tsw_comparator: By your servants, have you defied the Lord, and have said, "With the multitude of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon. I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice fir trees. I will enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field.

verses.rationale: Retain hyperbolic water mastery without importing foreign waters.
verses.before: I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt."
verses.after: I dug and drank water; with the soles of my feet I dried up all Egypt’s streams.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt."

verses.rationale: Preserve divine prior planning versus king’s boast.
verses.before: Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning them into ruinous heaps.
verses.after: Have you not heard? Long ago I did it; in ancient days I formed it. Now I have brought it about: you turn fortified cities into ruined heaps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning them into ruinous heaps.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult field text rather than silently scorched grain.
verses.before: So their inhabitants had little power. They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.
verses.after: Their inhabitants, powerless, were terrified and ashamed, like plants in a field, tender grass, grass on rooftops, a field before it stands ripe.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore their inhabitants had little power. They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.

verses.rationale: Retain ordinary movements and rebellion under divine knowledge.
verses.before: Yet I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me.
verses.after: I know when you sit, when you go out and come in, and how you rage against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me.

verses.rationale: Preserve bodily coercion and reversed journey.
verses.before: Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, therefore will I put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.
verses.after: Because your rage against me and your arrogance have reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your lips, and turn you back by the way you came.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, therefore will I put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

verses.rationale: Retain three agricultural years and imperative read-form.
verses.before: This will be the sign to you. You will eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from the same; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
verses.after: “This will be your sign: This year eat what grows by itself, and in the second year what springs from that. In the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: This will be the sign to you. You will eat this year that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from the same; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.

verses.rationale: Keep below/above renewal image.
verses.before: The remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
verses.after: The surviving remnant of Judah’s house will again take root below and bear fruit above.
verses.tsw_comparator: The remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.

verses.rationale: Preserve parallel remnant locations and divine zeal.
verses.before: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will perform this.'
verses.after: For a remnant will come out of Jerusalem, survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the **LORD** of hosts will do this.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will perform this.'

verses.rationale: Keep four denied siege actions.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, 'He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.
verses.after: Therefore the **LORD** says about the king of Assyria: “He will not enter this city, shoot an arrow there, approach it with a shield, or heap up a siege ramp against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, 'He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.

verses.rationale: Repeat denied entry and return route.
verses.before: By the way that he came, by the same he will return, and he will not come to this city,' says the LORD.
verses.after: By the way he came he will return; he will not enter this city,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the way that he came, by the same he will return, and he will not come to this city,' says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep two stated reasons for protection.
verses.before: 'For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake.'"
verses.after: “I will shield this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: 'For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake.'"

verses.rationale: Preserve exact number and observer perspective without implied resurrection.
verses.before: The angel of the LORD went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, look, these were all dead bodies.
verses.after: The **LORD**’s angel went out and struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. When people rose early in the morning, there lay all the dead bodies.
verses.tsw_comparator: The angel of the LORD went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, look, these were all dead bodies.

verses.rationale: Retain multiple departure verbs and destination.
verses.before: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went away, returned to Nineveh, and stayed there.
verses.after: Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp, left, and returned to Nineveh, where he stayed.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went away, returned to Nineveh, and stayed there.

verses.rationale: Preserve all names, patricide, escape, and succession.
verses.before: It happened, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.
verses.after: As he worshiped in the house of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword. They escaped to Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: It happened, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain stark prediction without adding conditionality.
verses.before: In those days was Hezekiah sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, "Thus says the LORD, 'Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.'"
verses.after: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came and told him, “The **LORD** says: Put your household in order, for you will die; you will not recover.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days was Hezekiah sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, "Thus says the LORD, 'Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.'"

verses.rationale: Keep bodily gesture and prayer.
verses.before: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
verses.after: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserve personal appeal and intense tears.
verses.before: and said, "Remember now, the LORD, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done what is good in your sight." Hezekiah wept bitterly.
verses.after: “Please, **LORD**,” he said, “remember how I have walked before you faithfully, with a whole heart, and done what is good in your sight.” Hezekiah wept bitterly.
verses.tsw_comparator: and said, "Remember now, the LORD, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight." Hezekiah wept bitterly.

verses.rationale: Retain new prophetic speech introduction.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
verses.after: Then the **LORD**’s word came to Isaiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,

verses.rationale: Keep heard/seen pairing and exact extension.
verses.before: "Go, and tell Hezekiah, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father, "I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Look, I will add fifteen years to your life.
verses.after: “Go and tell Hezekiah: The **LORD**, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I am adding fifteen years to your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Go, and tell Hezekiah, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father, "I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Look, I will add fifteen years to your life.

verses.rationale: Retain king/city rescue and repeated city.
verses.before: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
verses.after: I will rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria’s hand, and I will shield this city.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.

verses.rationale: Preserve two full divine names and sign function.
verses.before: This will be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has spoken.
verses.after: This will be your sign from the **LORD** that the **LORD** will do what he has spoken:
verses.tsw_comparator: This will be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has spoken.

verses.rationale: Retain steps rather than assume dial; preserve sun/shadow shift.
verses.before: Look, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun returned ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down."'"
verses.after: I will make the shadow cast by the sun on Ahaz’s steps go back ten steps.” And the sun went back ten steps on the steps it had descended.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun returned ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down."'"

verses.rationale: Keep literary heading inside verse.
verses.before: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and had recovered of his sickness.
verses.after: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, after his illness and recovery:
verses.tsw_comparator: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and had recovered of his sickness.

verses.rationale: Retain disputed midst expression and lost years.
verses.before: I said, "In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I am deprived of the residue of my years."
verses.after: I said, “In the midst of my days I must go through Sheol’s gates; I am deprived of my remaining years.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, "In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I am deprived of the residue of my years."

verses.rationale: Keep doubled YAH and difficult inhabitants-of-cessation phrase.
verses.before: I said, "I will not see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world.
verses.after: I said, “I will no longer see **YAH**, **YAH** in the land of the living. I will no longer look on human beings among those who inhabit this passing world.
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, "I will not see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world.

verses.rationale: Preserve tent/weaving images and I/he/you shifts.
verses.before: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.
verses.after: My dwelling is pulled up and carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. Like a weaver I have rolled up my life; he cuts me from the loom. From day to night you bring me to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

verses.rationale: Follow waited reading with note; repeat exact refrain.
verses.before: I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day even to night you will make an end of me.
verses.after: I waited until morning; like a lion he breaks all my bones. From day to night you bring me to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

verses.rationale: Retain birds and legal guarantor appeal.
verses.before: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security."
verses.after: Like a swallow or crane I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak from looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed; stand surety for me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security."

verses.rationale: Keep difficult reflective response and humbled walking.
verses.before: What will I say? He has both spoken to me, and himself has done it. I will walk carefully all my years because of the anguish of my soul.
verses.after: What can I say? He has spoken to me, and he has done it. I will walk humbly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: What will I say? He has both spoken to me, and himself has done it. I will walk carefully all my years because of the anguish of my soul.

verses.rationale: Retain unspecified these and restoration petition.
verses.before: Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of them: you restore me, and cause me to live.
verses.after: Lord, by these things people live; in all these is the life of my spirit. Restore me and let me live.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of them: you restore me, and cause me to live.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated bitterness and bodily forgiveness image.
verses.before: Look, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.
verses.after: Look, bitter bitterness became my well-being. In love you kept my life from the pit of destruction, for you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

verses.rationale: Retain stark death claims without doctrinal harmonization.
verses.before: For Sheol cannot praise you. Death cannot celebrate you. People who go down into the pit cannot hope for your truth.
verses.after: Sheol cannot thank you, death cannot praise you; those going down to the pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Sheol cannot praise you. Death cannot celebrate you. Those who go down into the pit cannot hope for your truth.

verses.rationale: Preserve doubled living and specific paternal transmission.
verses.before: The living, the living, he will praise you, as I do this day. The father will reveal your truth to the children.
verses.after: The living, the living thank you, as I do today; a father makes your faithfulness known to his children.
verses.tsw_comparator: The living, the living, he will praise you, as I do this day. The father will make known your truth to the children.

verses.rationale: Keep my/we shift and both divine names.
verses.before: The LORD will save me. Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The **LORD** will save me! We will play my songs on strings all the days of our lives in the **LORD**’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will save me. Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain retrospective practical treatment after song.
verses.before: Now Isaiah had said, "Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he will recover."
verses.after: Isaiah had said, “Bring a cake of figs and spread it on the boil, so he may recover.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Isaiah had said, "Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he will recover."

verses.rationale: Preserve retrospective question in original chapter position.
verses.before: Hezekiah also had said, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
verses.after: And Hezekiah had asked, “What is the sign that I will go up to the **LORD**’s house?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezekiah also had said, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"

verses.rationale: Keep name, father, gift, and occasion.
verses.before: At that time, Merodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he heard that he had been sick, and had recovered.
verses.after: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, having heard that he had been ill and had recovered.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time, Merodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he heard that he had been sick, and had recovered.

verses.rationale: Follow his treasury read-form and full display inventory.
verses.before: Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not show them.
verses.after: Hezekiah welcomed them gladly and showed them his treasury—the silver, gold, spices, fine oil, his whole armory, and everything in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in his entire domain that Hezekiah did not show them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not show them.

verses.rationale: Keep unanswered first question and explicit Babylon answer.
verses.before: Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah, and asked him, "What did these men say? Where did they come from to you?" Hezekiah said, "They have come from a country far from me, even from Babylon."
verses.after: The prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked, “What did these men say, and where did they come from?” Hezekiah answered, “They came to me from a distant land, from Babylon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah, and asked him, "What did these men say? Where did they come from to you?" Hezekiah said, "They have come from a country far from me, even from Babylon."

verses.rationale: Repeat comprehensive display without editorial judgment.
verses.before: Then he asked, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah answered, "They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them."
verses.after: Isaiah asked, “What did they see in your palace?” Hezekiah said, “They saw everything in my palace. There is nothing in my storehouses I did not show them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he asked, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah answered, "They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them."

verses.rationale: Retain prophetic authority and addressee.
verses.before: Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts:
verses.after: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the **LORD** of hosts:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts:

verses.rationale: Keep all/nothing totality and deportation destination.
verses.before: 'Look, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,' says the LORD.
verses.after: ‘Days are coming when everything in your palace, everything your ancestors have stored up until today, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will remain,’ says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: 'Look, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,' says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain kinship and bodily/status ambiguity of eunuchs.
verses.before: 'They will take away your sons who will issue from you, whom you will father, and they will be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.'"
verses.after: ‘Some of your own sons, born to you, will be taken away and become eunuchs in the king of Babylon’s palace.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: 'They will take away your sons who will issue from you, whom you will father, and they will be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.'"

verses.rationale: Keep limited temporal relief without supplying moral verdict.
verses.before: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "the LORD's word which you have spoken is good." He said moreover, "For there will be peace and truth in my days."
verses.after: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The **LORD**’s word you have spoken is good.” For he said, “There will be peace and stability in my days.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "the LORD's word which you have spoken is good." He said moreover, "For there will be peace and truth in my days."

verses.rationale: Preserve doubled command and collective belonging.
verses.before: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
verses.after: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult double recompense and military-service image.
verses.before: Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and cry to her that her warfare is ended, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received from the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.
verses.after: “Speak to Jerusalem’s heart and call to her: her hard service is complete, her guilt has been accepted as paid; she has received from the **LORD**’s hand double for all her sins.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and cry to her that her warfare is ended, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received from the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.

verses.rationale: Locate road preparation in wilderness while noting alternative punctuation.
verses.before: A voice cries: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
verses.after: A voice calls: “In the wilderness clear a way for the **LORD**; make a straight highway through the desert for our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: A voice cries: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.

verses.rationale: Retain comprehensive landscape preparation.
verses.before: Every valley will be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground will become level, and the rough places a plain.
verses.after: Every valley will be raised, every mountain and hill brought low; uneven ground will become level, and ridges a plain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain.

verses.rationale: Keep all flesh and both divine names.
verses.before: And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all flesh will see it together, for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
verses.after: The **LORD**’s glory will be revealed, and all flesh will see it together, for the **LORD**’s mouth has spoken.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”

verses.rationale: Follow pinned third-person reply and retain hesed ambiguity.
verses.before: A voice says, “Cry!” And I said, “What will I cry?” All flesh is grass, and all its loyalty is like the flower of the field.
verses.after: A voice says, “Call out!” And he says, “What shall I call?” “All flesh is grass, and all its faithfulness like a field’s flower.
verses.tsw_comparator: A voice says, “Cry!” And I said, “What shall I cry?” All flesh is grass, and all its loyalty is like the flower of the field.

verses.rationale: Keep divine breath and explicit human comparison.
verses.before: The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of the LORD blows upon it; surely the people are grass.
verses.after: Grass dries up, a flower withers, when the **LORD**’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are grass.
verses.tsw_comparator: The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of the LORD blows upon it; surely the people are grass.

verses.rationale: Repeat exact withering phrase and lasting word.
verses.before: The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.
verses.after: Grass dries up, a flower withers, but our God’s word stands forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.

verses.rationale: Choose feminine city as herald with alternative noted.
verses.before: Get yourself up to a high mountain, O herald of good news to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, O herald of good news to Jerusalem. Lift it up, do not fear; say to the cities of Judah, “Look your God!”
verses.after: Climb a high mountain, Zion, bearer of good news! Raise your voice with strength, Jerusalem, bearer of good news! Raise it; do not fear. Say to Judah’s cities, “Look, your God!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Get yourself up to a high mountain, O herald of good news to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, O herald of good news to Jerusalem. Lift it up, do not fear; say to the cities of Judah, “Behold your God!”

verses.rationale: Retain repeated look and royal reward language.
verses.before: Look, the Lord GOD comes with might, and his arm rules for him; look, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
verses.after: Look, the Lord **GOD** comes with might; his arm rules for him. Look, his reward is with him, his recompense before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and his arm rules for him; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

verses.rationale: Keep shepherd arm echo and nursing animals specifically.
verses.before: He will tend his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms; he will carry them in his bosom, and gently lead those that are with young.
verses.after: Like a shepherd he tends his flock; with his arm he gathers the lambs and carries them against his chest. He gently leads those nursing their young.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will tend his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms; he will carry them in his bosom, and gently lead those that are with young.

verses.rationale: Preserve ancient measuring tools and cosmic rhetorical question.
verses.before: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the heavens with a span, and enclosed the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance?
verses.after: Who has measured the waters in his palm, marked off the heavens with a handspan, held earth’s dust in a measure, weighed mountains on a balance and hills on scales?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the heavens with a span, and enclosed the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance?

verses.rationale: Keep repeated measure verb and spirit rather than import Greek mind.
verses.before: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or as his counselor has instructed him?
verses.after: Who has measured the **LORD**’s spirit, or instructed him as his counselor?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or as his counselor has instructed him?

verses.rationale: Preserve teaching repetition and unanswered questions.
verses.before: With whom did he take counsel, and who made him understand? Who taught him the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
verses.after: Whom did he consult for understanding? Who taught him the path of justice, taught him knowledge, or showed him the way of understanding?
verses.tsw_comparator: With whom did he take counsel, and who made him understand? Who taught him the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?

verses.rationale: Keep repeated look and insignificant weights.
verses.before: Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are accounted as the dust on the scales; look, he takes up the islands like fine dust.
verses.after: Look, nations are like a drop from a bucket, regarded as dust on scales. Look, he lifts islands like fine dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are accounted as the dust on the scales; behold, he takes up the islands like fine dust.

verses.rationale: Preserve inadequate forest and animal offering.
verses.before: Lebanon would not suffice for fuel, nor are its beasts enough for a burnt offering.
verses.after: Lebanon does not have enough wood for the fire, nor enough animals for a burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lebanon would not suffice for fuel, nor are its beasts enough for a burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Retain stark national comparison without softening.
verses.before: All the nations are as nothing before him; they are accounted by him as less than nothing and emptiness.
verses.after: All nations are as nothing before him; he regards them as less than nothing and emptiness.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the nations are as nothing before him; they are accounted by him as less than nothing and emptiness.

verses.rationale: Keep two comparison questions.
verses.before: To whom then will you liken God, or what likeness compare with him?
verses.after: To whom, then, will you compare God? What likeness can you set beside him?
verses.tsw_comparator: To whom then will you liken God, or what likeness compare with him?

verses.rationale: Retain material production of supposed deity.
verses.before: An idol! A craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts for it silver chains.
verses.after: An idol? A craftsman casts it, a goldsmith plates it with gold and fashions silver chains.
verses.tsw_comparator: An idol! A craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts for it silver chains.

verses.rationale: Choose poor-offering reading and note uncertain term.
verses.before: He who is too poor for an offering chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not move.
verses.after: Someone too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not wobble.
verses.tsw_comparator: He who is too poor for an offering chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not move.

verses.rationale: Preserve four rebuking questions.
verses.before: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?
verses.after: Do you not know? Have you not heard? Were you not told from the beginning? Have you not understood earth’s foundations?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?

verses.rationale: Keep circle and tent as ancient imagery, not modern cosmology.
verses.before: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them like a tent to dwell in;
verses.after: He sits above earth’s circle, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers. He stretches the heavens like a thin curtain, spreads them like a tent to live in.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them like a tent to dwell in;

verses.rationale: Retain parallel political demotion.
verses.before: who brings princes to nothing, and makes the rulers of the earth as emptiness.
verses.after: He reduces rulers to nothing, makes earth’s judges emptiness.
verses.tsw_comparator: who brings princes to nothing, and makes the rulers of the earth as emptiness.

verses.rationale: Preserve three scarcely clauses and sudden removal.
verses.before: Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the earth, when he blows on them, and they wither, and the tempest carries them off like stubble.
verses.after: Scarcely planted, scarcely sown, scarcely has their stem rooted in the earth, when he blows on them and they wither, and a tempest carries them off like stubble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the earth, when he blows on them, and they wither, and the tempest carries them off like stubble.

verses.rationale: Keep direct divine challenge without naming comparison.
verses.before: To whom then will you compare me, that I should be like him? says the Holy One.
verses.after: “To whom will you compare me, that I should be his equal?” says the Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: To whom then will you compare me, that I should be like him? says the Holy One.

verses.rationale: Retain counted celestial host and individual naming.
verses.before: Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is missing.
verses.after: Lift your eyes on high and see: who created these? He brings their host out by number and calls each by name. Because of his great vigor and mighty strength, not one is missing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is missing.

verses.rationale: Keep paired people-names and judicial claim.
verses.before: Why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over by my God”?
