verses.after: Why do you say, Jacob, and declare, Israel, “My way is hidden from the **LORD**; my claim escapes my God’s notice”?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over by my God”?

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated questions and unlimited divine endurance.
verses.before: Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable.
verses.after: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The **LORD** is the everlasting God, Creator of earth’s farthest reaches. He does not grow weary or tired; his understanding cannot be searched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable.

verses.rationale: Keep strength supplied to powerless rather than capable.
verses.before: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.
verses.after: He gives strength to the weary, and increases the power of those who have none.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.

verses.rationale: Retain specifically young male strength failing.
verses.before: Even youths will faint and be weary, and young men will fall exhausted;
verses.after: Even youths grow weary and tired; young men stumble and fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even youths shall faint and be weary, and young men shall fall exhausted;

verses.rationale: Keep waiting and three movement/endurance clauses.
verses.before: but people who wait for the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not be weary; they will walk and not faint.
verses.after: But those who wait for the **LORD** will renew their strength. They will rise on wings like eagles, run and not grow tired, walk and not grow weary.
verses.tsw_comparator: but those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint.

verses.rationale: Keep courtroom summons and strength echo40:31.
verses.before: "Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let's meet together for judgment.
verses.after: “Islands, be silent before me! Let peoples renew their strength. Let them approach, then speak; let us come together for judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let's meet together for judgment.

verses.rationale: Preserve unnamed conqueror and difficult righteousness subject.
verses.before: Who has raised up one from the east? Whom called him to his foot in righteousness? He hands over nations to him, and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.
verses.after: Who stirred up one from the east, whom righteousness summons to its feet? He hands nations over to him and brings kings low; he makes them dust before his sword, driven stubble before his bow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has raised up one from the east? Whom called him to his foot in righteousness? He hands over nations to him, and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.

verses.rationale: Retain novel route and safety.
verses.before: He pursues them, and passes by safely, Even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.
verses.after: He pursues them and passes safely on, by a path his feet have never traveled.
verses.tsw_comparator: He pursues them, and passes by safely, Even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.

verses.rationale: Keep first/last and emphatic self-identification.
verses.before: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am he."
verses.after: Who has worked and done this, calling generations from the beginning? I, the **LORD**, am first, and with the last I am he.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am he."

verses.rationale: Preserve global fearful response.
verses.before: The islands have seen, and fear. The ends of the earth tremble. They approach, and come.
verses.after: The islands see and fear; earth’s ends tremble. They draw near and come.
verses.tsw_comparator: The islands have seen, and fear. The ends of the earth tremble. They approach, and come.

verses.rationale: Keep mutual encouragement in idol-making context.
verses.before: Everyone helps his neighbor. They say to their brothers, "Be strong!"
verses.after: Each helps his neighbor, saying to his brother, “Be strong!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone helps his neighbor. They say to their brothers, "Be strong!"

verses.rationale: Retain coordinated workmanship and comic unstable idol.
verses.before: So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. the one who smoothes with the hammer encourages the one who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, "It is good;" and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter.
verses.after: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, the one who smooths with a hammer the one who strikes the anvil. He says of the soldering, “It is good,” and secures the idol with nails so it will not wobble.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. the one who smoothes with the hammer encourages the one who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, "It is good;" and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter.

verses.rationale: Keep named servant and active loving participle.
verses.before: "But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,
verses.after: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I chose, offspring of Abraham who loved me—
verses.tsw_comparator: "But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,

verses.rationale: Repeat servant/choice and explicit nonrejection.
verses.before: You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, 'You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;'
verses.after: I took hold of you from earth’s ends, called you from its farthest corners. I said, ‘You are my servant; I have chosen you and have not rejected you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, 'You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;'

verses.rationale: Keep three divine support verbs and right-hand image.
verses.before: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
verses.after: Do not fear, for I am with you. Do not look around in dismay, for I am your God. I strengthen you; I help you; I uphold you with my righteous right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.

verses.rationale: Preserve hostile rage and reduced-to-nothing fate.
verses.before: Look, all people who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. People who strive with you will be like nothing, and will perish.
verses.after: Look, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced. Those who contend with you will become nothing and perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be like nothing, and will perish.

verses.rationale: Keep search without finding and intensified nothing.
verses.before: You will seek them, and will not find them, even people who contend with you. People who war against you will be as nothing, as a non-existent thing.
verses.after: You will look for your opponents and not find them. Those who fight you will become nothing, nothing at all.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will seek them, and will not find them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as nothing, as a non-existent thing.

verses.rationale: Retain divine grasp of people’s right hand and repeated assurance.
verses.before: For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; I am the one who says to you, “Do not fear; I will help you.”
verses.after: For I, the **LORD** your God, hold your right hand and tell you, ‘Do not fear; I help you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; I am the one who says to you, “Do not fear; I will help you.”

verses.rationale: Keep humiliating worm metaphor and redeemer identity.
verses.before: Don't be afraid, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I will help you," says the LORD, "and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: Do not fear, worm Jacob, people of Israel. I help you,” declares the **LORD**; your Redeemer is Israel’s Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: Don't be afraid, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I will help you," says the LORD, "and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve violent transformation from worm to agricultural tool.
verses.before: Look, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff.
verses.after: “Look, I make you a new threshing sledge, sharp and double-edged. You will thresh mountains and crush them, make hills like chaff.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff.

verses.rationale: Retain dispersal and contrasted celebration.
verses.before: You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in the LORD. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: You will winnow them; wind will carry them off, and a tempest scatter them. But you will rejoice in the **LORD**, and glory in Israel’s Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in the LORD. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep material need and two assurances.
verses.before: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none. Their tongue fails for thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
verses.after: The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the **LORD**, will answer them; I, Israel’s God, will not abandon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none. Their tongue fails for thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

verses.rationale: Retain four water/land reversals.
verses.before: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs among the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
verses.after: I will open rivers on bare heights, springs within valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, dry land sources of water.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the midst of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.

verses.rationale: Keep seven trees while noting uncertain species identifications.
verses.before: I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I will set fir trees, pine, and box trees together in the desert;
verses.after: I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil tree in the wilderness; in the desert I will set cypress, plane, and pine together,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I will set fir trees, pine, and box trees together in the desert;

verses.rationale: Preserve four cognitive responses and creative agency.
verses.before: that they may see, know, consider, and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
verses.after: so they may see and know, consider and understand together that the **LORD**’s hand has done this, that Israel’s Holy One has created it.
verses.tsw_comparator: that they may see, know, consider, and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.

verses.rationale: Keep courtroom language and distinct title.
verses.before: Produce your cause," says the LORD. "Bring forth your strong reasons," says the King of Jacob.
verses.after: Present your case,” says the **LORD**. “Bring forward your strongest arguments,” says Jacob’s King.
verses.tsw_comparator: Produce your cause," says the LORD. "Bring forth your strong reasons," says the King of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserve former/future evidentiary challenge.
verses.before: "Let them announce, and declare to us what will happen. Declare the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come.
verses.after: Let them come forward and tell us what will happen. Tell us what the former things were, so we may consider and know their outcome; or announce to us what is coming.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Let them announce, and declare to us what will happen. Declare the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come.

verses.rationale: Follow see read-form and retain provocative good/harm challenge.
verses.before: Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and see it together.
verses.after: Tell us what will happen afterward, so we may know you are gods. Do good or do harm, so we may be dismayed and see it together!
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and see it together.

verses.rationale: Render rare work-description cautiously and retain severe verdict.
verses.before: Look, you are of nothing, and your work is of nothing. the one who chooses you is an abomination.
verses.after: Look, you are less than nothing, and your work is worthless. Whoever chooses you is an abomination.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you are of nothing, and your work is of nothing. the one who chooses you is an abomination.

verses.rationale: Keep north/east descriptions and unnamed agent.
verses.before: "I have raised up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name; and he will come on rulers as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay.
verses.after: “I stirred up one from the north, and he came; from the rising sun he calls on my name. He comes upon rulers like clay, like a potter trampling mud.
verses.tsw_comparator: "I have raised up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name; and he will come on rulers as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay.

verses.rationale: Retain triple absence of predictive witness.
verses.before: Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know? And before, that we may say, 'He is right?' Surely, there is no one who declares. Surely, there is no one who shows. Surely, there is no one who hears your words.
verses.after: Who announced it from the beginning so we could know, in advance so we could say, ‘He is right’? No one announced it, no one made it heard; no one heard your words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know? And before, that we may say, 'He is right?' Surely, there is no one who declares. Surely, there is no one who shows. Surely, there is no one who hears your words.

verses.rationale: Make compressed first-person claim readable with supplied tell.
verses.before: I am the first to say to Zion, 'Look, look at them;' and I will give one who brings good news to Jerusalem.
verses.after: I was first to tell Zion, ‘Look, here they are!’ I give Jerusalem a bearer of good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the first to say to Zion, 'Look, look at them;' and I will give one who brings good news to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain failed consultation and absent answer.
verses.before: When I look, there is no man; even among them there is no counselor who, when I ask of them, can answer a word.
verses.after: I look, but there is no one; among these there is no counselor who can answer a word when I ask.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I look, there is no man; even among them there is no counselor who, when I ask of them, can answer a word.

verses.rationale: Keep threefold worthlessness and wind image.
verses.before: Look, all of them, their works are vanity and nothing. Their molten images are wind and confusion.
verses.after: Look, all of them are emptiness; their deeds are nothing, their cast images wind and waste.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, all of them, their works are vanity and nothing. Their molten images are wind and confusion.

verses.rationale: Preserve unnamed servant, divine delight, and nations’ justice.
verses.before: Look, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom my soul delights. I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
verses.after: “Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one, in whom I delight. I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring justice to the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom my soul delights. I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.

verses.rationale: Keep triple refusal of loud public force.
verses.before: He will not cry out or raise his voice or make it heard in the street.
verses.after: He will not shout or raise his voice, or make it heard in the street.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will not cry out or raise his voice or make it heard in the street.

verses.rationale: Retain fragile objects and faithful justice.
verses.before: A bruised reed he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not extinguish; faithfully he will bring forth justice.
verses.after: A bruised reed he will not break; a dimly burning wick he will not put out. He will faithfully bring justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: A bruised reed he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not extinguish; faithfully he will bring forth justice.

verses.rationale: Preserve wordplay linking servant’s endurance to reed/wick.
verses.before: He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice in the earth, and the islands will wait for his law."
verses.after: He will not burn dim or be crushed until he establishes justice on earth; the islands wait for his instruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice in the earth, and the islands will wait for his law."

verses.rationale: Keep breath/spirit parallel and universal creation.
verses.before: Thus says God the LORD, the one who created the heavens and stretched them out, the one who spread out the earth and what comes out of it, the one who gives breath to its people and spirit to people who walk in it.
verses.after: Thus says God, the **LORD**, who created the heavens and stretched them out, spread the earth and all that springs from it, gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk upon it:
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says God the LORD, the one who created the heavens and stretched them out, the one who spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, the one who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk in it.

verses.rationale: Preserve servant as covenant, not merely covenant messenger.
verses.before: "I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;
verses.after: “I, the **LORD**, called you in righteousness; I will take your hand and guard you. I will give you as a covenant for the people, a light for the nations,
verses.tsw_comparator: "I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;

verses.rationale: Retain concrete sight and release images.
verses.before: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and people who sit in darkness out of the prison.
verses.after: to open blind eyes, to bring prisoners out of confinement, those dwelling in darkness out of prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.

verses.rationale: Keep divine name claim and exclusive glory.
verses.before: "I am the LORD. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images.
verses.after: I am the **LORD**; that is my name. I will not give my glory to another or my praise to carved images.
verses.tsw_comparator: "I am the LORD. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images.

verses.rationale: Retain organic sprouting metaphor for announced events.
verses.before: Look, the former things have happened, and I declare new things. I tell you about them before they come up."
verses.after: Look, the former things have come to pass; now I announce new things. Before they sprout, I make them known to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the former things have happened, and I declare new things. I tell you about them before they come up."

verses.rationale: Keep seafarers, sea contents, islands as praise audience.
verses.before: Sing to the LORD a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, the islands and their inhabitants.
verses.after: Sing the **LORD** a new song, his praise from earth’s ends— you who go down to the sea, and all that fills it, islands and those who inhabit them!
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to the LORD a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, the islands and their inhabitants.

verses.rationale: Preserve named desert communities and heights.
verses.before: Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Let them shout from the top of the mountains!
verses.after: Let wilderness and its towns lift their voices, the settlements where Kedar lives. Let Sela’s inhabitants sing for joy, shout from the mountaintops.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Let them shout from the top of the mountains!

verses.rationale: Keep islands refrain and glory.
verses.before: Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare his praise in the islands.
verses.after: Let them give glory to the **LORD** and proclaim his praise in the islands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare his praise in the islands.

verses.rationale: Retain male warrior simile before female labor simile.
verses.before: The LORD will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies.
verses.after: The **LORD** goes out like a warrior; like a man of battle he stirs his zeal. He cries out, raises a battle shout, shows his might against his enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine maternal bodily metaphor without qualification.
verses.before: "I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a laboring woman. I will both gasp and pant.
verses.after: “For a long time I have kept silent, kept still and restrained myself. Now I cry out like a woman in labor; I gasp and pant together.
verses.tsw_comparator: "I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a laboring woman. I will both gasp and pant.

verses.rationale: Keep destructive landscape counterpart to restoration.
verses.before: I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs. I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.
verses.after: I will lay mountains and hills waste and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn rivers into islands and dry up pools.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs. I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.

verses.rationale: Repeat unknown paths and resolve final them as people with note.
verses.before: I will bring the blind by a way that they do not know. I will lead them in paths that they do not know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
verses.after: I will lead the blind by a way they do not know, guide them on paths they do not know. I will turn darkness before them into light, and rough places into level ground. These things I will do; I will not abandon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring the blind by a way that they do not know. I will lead them in paths that they do not know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.

verses.rationale: Retain misplaced trust and emphatic shame.
verses.before: "People who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, 'You are our gods' will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed.
verses.after: Those who trust in carved images, who tell cast idols, ‘You are our gods,’ will be turned back, deeply ashamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, 'You are our gods' will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed.

verses.rationale: Preserve paradoxical commands.
verses.before: "Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.
verses.after: Listen, you deaf! Look and see, you blind!
verses.tsw_comparator: "Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult meshullam epithet and servant indictment.
verses.before: Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as the one who is at peace, and as blind as the LORD's servant?
verses.after: Who is blind but my servant, as deaf as the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one committed to me, blind like the **LORD**’s servant?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as the one who is at peace, and as blind as the LORD's servant?

verses.rationale: Follow infinitive read-form and preserve second/third-person shift.
verses.before: You see many things, but do not observe. His ears are open, but he does not listen.
verses.after: Seeing many things, you pay no attention; with ears open, he does not hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: You see many things, but do not observe. His ears are open, but he does not listen.

verses.rationale: Retain divine purpose and Torah’s honor.
verses.before: It pleased the LORD, for his righteousness' sake, to magnify the law, and make it honorable.
verses.after: The **LORD** desired, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify instruction and make it glorious.
verses.tsw_comparator: It pleased the LORD, for his righteousness' sake, to magnify the law, and make it honorable.

verses.rationale: Preserve captivity and absent restitution command.
verses.before: But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become a prey, and no one delivers; and a spoil, and no one says, 'Restore them!'
verses.after: But this is a people robbed and plundered, all trapped in holes, hidden in prisons. They have become prey, with no rescuer, plunder, with no one saying, ‘Give them back!’
verses.tsw_comparator: But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become a prey, and no one delivers; and a spoil, and no one says, 'Restore them!'

verses.rationale: Keep future-oriented appeal without assigning audience.
verses.before: Who is there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?
verses.after: Who among you will listen to this, pay attention and hear for the time to come?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?

verses.rationale: Preserve we/they shift and divine responsibility.
verses.before: Who gave Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn't the LORD, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not walk in his ways, and they disobeyed his law.
verses.after: Who handed Jacob over to plunder, Israel to robbers? Was it not the **LORD**, against whom we sinned? They would not walk in his ways and did not listen to his instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who gave Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn't the LORD, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not walk in his ways, and they disobeyed his law.

verses.rationale: Keep singular collective target and unlearned destruction.
verses.before: So he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle; and it set him on fire all around, but he did not know; and it burned him, but he did not take it to heart."
verses.after: So he poured on him his burning anger and the violence of war. It blazed around him, but he did not understand; it burned him, but he did not take it to heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle; and it set him on fire all around, but he did not know; and it burned him, but he did not take it to heart."

verses.rationale: Retain reassurance after judgment and paired created/formed.
verses.before: But now, this is what LORD says, he who created you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: "Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; you are mine.
verses.after: But now the **LORD** says, he who created you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by name; you are mine.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now, this is what LORD says, he who created you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: "Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; you are mine.

verses.rationale: Keep passage through danger rather than avoidance of it.
verses.before: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned; the flame will not set you ablaze.
verses.after: When you pass through water, I am with you; through rivers, they will not sweep you away. When you walk through fire, you will not be scorched; the flame will not burn you.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned; the flame will not set you ablaze.

verses.rationale: Retain three nations and consequential exchange claim.
verses.before: For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.
verses.after: For I am the **LORD** your God, Israel’s Holy One, your Savior. I give Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.

verses.rationale: Preserve costly human substitution without softening.
verses.before: Since you are precious and honored in my sight, and because I love you, I will give people in exchange for you, nations in exchange for your life.
verses.after: Because you are precious in my eyes, honored, and I love you, I give people in your place, nations in exchange for your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Since you are precious and honored in my sight, and because I love you, I will give people in exchange for you, nations in exchange for your life.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated assurance and two gathering directions.
verses.before: Do not fear, for I am with you; I will bring your offspring from the east, and from the west I will gather you.
verses.after: Do not fear, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not fear, for I am with you; I will bring your offspring from the east, and from the west I will gather you.

verses.rationale: Preserve north/south commands and both gendered children.
verses.before: I will say to the north, 'Give them up!' and to the south, 'Do not withhold!' Bring my sons from far away, and my daughters from the ends of the earth—
verses.after: I will tell the north, ‘Give them up!’ and the south, ‘Do not hold them back!’ Bring my sons from far away, my daughters from earth’s ends—
verses.tsw_comparator: I will say to the north, 'Give them up!' and to the south, 'Do not withhold!' Bring my sons from far away, and my daughters from the ends of the earth—

verses.rationale: Retain three creation verbs and purpose.
verses.before: everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made."
verses.after: everyone called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed, whom I made.”
verses.tsw_comparator: everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made."

verses.rationale: Keep paradoxical witness audience.
verses.before: Lead out people who have eyes but are blind, who have ears but are deaf.
verses.after: Bring out the people who are blind though they have eyes, who are deaf though they have ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lead out those who have eyes but are blind, who have ears but are deaf.

verses.rationale: Preserve courtroom proof and witness response.
verses.before: All the nations gather together, and the peoples assemble. Which of them declared this and proclaimed to us the former things? Let them bring in their witnesses to prove they were right, and let them hear and say, 'It is true.'
verses.after: All nations gather together, and peoples assemble. Who among them can announce this and tell us the former things? Let them bring witnesses and prove themselves right; let others hear and say, “It is true.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the nations gather together, and the peoples assemble. Which of them declared this and proclaimed to us the former things? Let them bring in their witnesses to prove they were right, and let them hear and say, 'It is true.'

verses.rationale: Keep witnesses/servant collective and temporal exclusivity.
verses.before: "You are my witnesses," declares the LORD, "and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, nor will there be one after me.
verses.after: “You are my witnesses,” declares the **LORD**, “and my servant whom I chose, so you may know and trust me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, and after me none will be.
verses.tsw_comparator: "You are my witnesses," declares the LORD, "and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, nor will there be one after me.

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic I repetition and saving exclusivity.
verses.before: I, even I, am the LORD, and apart from me there is no savior.
verses.after: I, I am the **LORD**; apart from me there is no savior.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, even I, am the LORD, and apart from me there is no savior.

verses.rationale: Keep three first-person acts and witness refrain.
verses.before: I have revealed and saved and proclaimed—I, and not some foreign god among you. You are my witnesses," declares the LORD, "that I am God.
verses.after: I announced, I saved, I made it heard; no foreign god was among you. You are my witnesses,” declares the **LORD**, “and I am God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have revealed and saved and proclaimed—I, and not some foreign god among you. You are my witnesses," declares the LORD, "that I am God.

verses.rationale: Preserve difficult temporal claim and irreversible action.
verses.before: Yes, and from ancient days, I am he. No one can deliver out of my hand. When I act, who can reverse it?"
verses.after: From the day’s beginning I am he; no one can rescue from my hand. I act—who can turn it back?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, and from ancient days, I am he. No one can deliver out of my hand. When I act, who can reverse it?"

verses.rationale: Choose fugitives reading and note difficult bars/ships syntax.
verses.before: This is what LORD says—your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: "For your sake I will send to Babylon and bring down as fugitives all the Babylonians, in the ships in which they take pride.
verses.after: The **LORD**, your Redeemer, Israel’s Holy One, says: “For your sake I have sent to Babylon and brought them all down as fugitives, the Chaldeans in the ships they rejoiced in.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what LORD says—your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: "For your sake I will send to Babylon and bring down as fugitives all the Babylonians, in the ships in which they take pride.

verses.rationale: Keep four linked divine designations.
verses.before: I am the LORD, your Holy One, Israel’s Creator, your King."
verses.after: I am the **LORD**, your Holy One, Israel’s Creator, your King.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the LORD, your Holy One, Israel’s Creator, your King."

verses.rationale: Retain exodus imagery without inserting Egypt name.
verses.before: This is what LORD says—he who makes a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,
verses.after: The **LORD** says, he who makes a way through the sea, a path through mighty waters,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what LORD says—he who makes a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,

verses.rationale: Keep martial catalogue and extinguished-wick image.
verses.before: who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the warrior together, they lie down, they cannot rise, they are extinguished, quenched like a wick:
verses.after: who brings out chariot and horse, army and warrior— they lie down together, never to rise, extinguished, put out like a wick:
verses.tsw_comparator: who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the warrior together, they lie down, they cannot rise, they are extinguished, quenched like a wick:

verses.rationale: Retain memory reversal beside explicit remembered exodus.
verses.before: "Forget the former things; do not dwell on the past.
verses.after: “Do not remember the former things or dwell on things of old.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Forget the former things; do not dwell on the past.

verses.rationale: Keep new growth and transformed exodus route.
verses.before: See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I am making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland.
verses.after: Look, I am doing something new; now it sprouts—do you not recognize it? I will make a way in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I am making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland.

verses.rationale: Retain animals’ honor and human thirst addressed.
verses.before: The wild animals honor me, the jackals and the owls, because I provide water in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland, to give drink to my chosen people,
verses.after: Wild animals will honor me, jackals and ostriches, for I give water in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland, to give my chosen people drink,
verses.tsw_comparator: The wild animals honor me, the jackals and the owls, because I provide water in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland, to give drink to my chosen people,

verses.rationale: Keep formation purpose and narrated praise.
verses.before: the people I formed for myself that they may proclaim my praise.
verses.after: the people I formed for myself to recount my praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: the people I formed for myself that they may proclaim my praise.

verses.rationale: Retain direct accusation and paired names.
verses.before: Yet you have not called upon me, Jacob, you have not wearied yourselves for me, Israel.
verses.after: Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; you have grown weary of me, Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you have not called upon me, Jacob, you have not wearied yourselves for me, Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve contrasting human failure and divine nonburdening.
verses.before: You have not brought me sheep for burnt offerings, nor honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings nor wearied you with incense.
verses.after: You have not brought me sheep for your burnt offerings nor honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with grain offerings nor wearied you with frankincense.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have not brought me sheep for burnt offerings, nor honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings nor wearied you with incense.

verses.rationale: Repeat burden/weary reversal and concrete offerings.
verses.before: You have not bought any fragrant calamus for me, nor lavished on me the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened me with your sins and wearied me with your offenses.
verses.after: You have not bought fragrant cane for me with silver nor satisfied me with your sacrifices’ fat. Instead, you have burdened me with your sins and wearied me with your guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have not bought any fragrant calamus for me, nor lavished on me the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened me with your sins and wearied me with your offenses.

verses.rationale: Keep emphatic I and divine motive, not earned pardon.
verses.before: I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions, for my own sake, and remembers your sins no more.
verses.after: I, I am the one who wipes away your rebellions for my own sake; your sins I will not remember.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions, for my own sake, and remembers your sins no more.

verses.rationale: Preserve judicial invitation, not a devotional command.
verses.before: Review the past for me, let us argue the matter together; state the case for your innocence.
verses.after: Remind me; let us argue our case together. You tell your story, so you may be proved right.
verses.tsw_comparator: Review the past for me, let us argue the matter together; state the case for your innocence.

verses.rationale: Keep unidentified first ancestor and mediating officials.
verses.before: Your first father sinned; your spokesmen rebelled against me.
verses.after: Your first father sinned, and your interpreters rebelled against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your first father sinned; your spokesmen rebelled against me.

verses.rationale: Preserve severe ending after forgiveness announcement.
verses.before: So I disgraced the dignitaries of your temple; I consigned Jacob to destruction and Israel to scorn."
verses.after: So I profaned the sanctuary’s officials and handed Jacob over to destruction, Israel to insults.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I disgraced the dignitaries of your temple; I consigned Jacob to destruction and Israel to scorn."

verses.rationale: Repeat named servant and chosen relation.
verses.before: Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
verses.after: “But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.

verses.rationale: Retain womb formation and alternate Israel name.
verses.before: This is what the LORD who made you, and formed you from the womb, who will help you says: "Don't be afraid, Jacob my servant; and you, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
verses.after: The **LORD**, who made you and formed you from the womb, who will help you, says: Do not fear, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what the LORD who made you, and formed you from the womb, who will help you says: "Don't be afraid, Jacob my servant; and you, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.

verses.rationale: Keep double pouring and water/Spirit parallel.
verses.before: For I will pour water on the one who is thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your seed, and my blessing on your offspring:
verses.after: I will pour water on thirsty ground, streams on dry land. I will pour my Spirit on your offspring, my blessing on your descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will pour water on the one who is thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your seed, and my blessing on your offspring:

verses.rationale: Preserve pinned among-grass wording rather than emend.
verses.before: and they will spring up among the grass, as willows by the watercourses.
verses.after: They will sprout among the grass, like willows beside flowing water.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they will spring up among the grass, as willows by the watercourses.

verses.rationale: Retain three acts of identification and hand-writing ambiguity.
verses.before: One will say, 'I am the LORD's;' and another will be called by the name of Jacob; and another will write with his hand 'to the LORD,' and honor the name of Israel."
verses.after: One will say, ‘I belong to the **LORD**’; another will call himself by Jacob’s name. Another will write on his hand, ‘The **LORD**’s,’ and take the name Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: One will say, 'I am the LORD's;' and another will be called by the name of Jacob; and another will write with his hand 'to the LORD,' and honor the name of Israel."

verses.rationale: Preserve both divine names and exclusive first/last claim.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel and Israel’s Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts: “I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no God.
verses.after: The **LORD**, Israel’s King and Redeemer, the **LORD** of hosts, says: I am first and I am last; apart from me there is no God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel and Israel’s Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts: “I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no God.

verses.rationale: Keep ancient-people phrase and challenge’s number shift.
verses.before: Who is like me? Who will call, and will declare it, and set it in order for me, since I established the ancient people? Let them declare the things that are coming, and that will happen.
verses.after: Who is like me? Let him call out, declare it and set it before me, since I established the ancient people. Let them declare what is coming and what will happen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is like me? Who will call, and will declare it, and set it in order for me, since I established the ancient people? Let them declare the things that are coming, and that will happen.

verses.rationale: Retain witnesses and Rock as divine designation.
verses.before: Don't fear, neither be afraid. Haven't I declared it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? Indeed, there is not. I do not know any other Rock."
verses.after: Do not be frightened or afraid. Have I not long ago made you hear and told you? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? There is no other Rock; I know of none.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Don't fear, neither be afraid. Haven't I declared it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? Indeed, there is not. I do not know any other Rock."

verses.rationale: Preserve witnesses’ uncertain referent and failed perception.
verses.before: Everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses do not see, nor know, that they may be disappointed.
verses.after: All who form idols are emptiness; their treasured objects bring no benefit. Their witnesses neither see nor know, and so they are put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses do not see, nor know, that they may be disappointed.

verses.rationale: Keep rhetorical exposure of useless making.
verses.before: Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing?
verses.after: Who would form a god or cast an idol that brings no benefit?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing?

verses.rationale: Retain collective challenge and human makers.
verses.before: Look, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together.
verses.after: Look, all its companions will be ashamed; its craftsmen are only human. Let them all gather and stand forward: they will tremble and be ashamed together.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together.

verses.rationale: Keep tools and maker’s bodily dependence.
verses.before: The blacksmith takes an axe, works in the coals, fashions it with hammers, and works it with his strong arm. He is hungry, and his strength fails; he drinks no water, and is faint.
verses.after: The smith works with a cutting tool over the coals, shaping it with hammers and working it with his strong arm. But he grows hungry and loses strength; without water to drink he becomes faint.
verses.tsw_comparator: The blacksmith takes an axe, works in the coals, fashions it with hammers, and works it with his strong arm. He is hungry, and his strength fails; he drinks no water, and is faint.

verses.rationale: Preserve four tools and constructed human likeness.
verses.before: The carpenter stretches out a line. He marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with planes. He marks it out with compasses, and shapes it like the figure of a man, with the beauty of a man, to reside in a house.
verses.after: The woodworker stretches a line, marks the shape with a stylus, works it with planes, and outlines it with a compass. He makes it in a man’s shape, with human beauty, to live in a house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The carpenter stretches out a line. He marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with planes. He marks it out with compasses, and shapes it like the figure of a man, with the beauty of a man, to reside in a house.

verses.rationale: Keep tree growth before manufacture and uncertain species names.
verses.before: He cuts down cedars for himself, and takes the cypress and the oak, and strengthens for himself one among the trees of the forest. He plants a fir tree, and the rain nourishes it.
verses.after: He cuts cedars, takes a holm oak or an oak, and lets it grow strong among the forest’s trees. He plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.
verses.tsw_comparator: He cuts down cedars for himself, and takes the cypress and the oak, and strengthens for himself one among the trees of the forest. He plants a fir tree, and the rain nourishes it.

verses.rationale: Retain one material’s mundane and cultic uses.
verses.before: Then it will be for a man to burn; and he takes some of it, and warms himself. Yes, he burns it, and bakes bread. Yes, he makes a god, and worships it; he makes it an engraved image, and falls down to it.
verses.after: It becomes fuel for someone. He takes some and warms himself; he lights a fire and bakes bread. He also makes a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows before it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then it will be for a man to burn; and he takes some of it, and warms himself. Yes, he burns it, and bakes bread. Yes, he makes a god, and worships it; he makes it an engraved image, and falls down to it.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated half and satisfied maker’s speech.
verses.before: He burns part of it in the fire. With part of it, he eats meat. He roasts a roast, and is satisfied. Yes, he warms himself, and says, "Aha! I am warm. I have seen the fire."
verses.after: Half he burns in the fire. Over that half he cooks meat, roasts it and eats his fill. He also warms himself and says, “Ah! I am warm; I can see the fire!”
verses.tsw_comparator: He burns part of it in the fire. With part of it, he eats meat. He roasts a roast, and is satisfied. Yes, he warms himself, and says, "Aha! I am warm. I have seen the fire."

verses.rationale: Keep rest-of-wood deity and helpless rescue appeal.
verses.before: The rest of it he makes into a god, even his engraved image. He bows down to it and worships, and prays to it, and says, "Deliver me; for you are my god!"
verses.after: With the rest he makes a god, his idol. He bows and worships it, prays to it and says, “Rescue me, for you are my god!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The rest of it he makes into a god, even his engraved image. He bows down to it and worships, and prays to it, and says, "Deliver me; for you are my god!"

verses.rationale: Retain obscured eyes/hearts without supplying agent.
verses.before: They do not know, neither do they consider: for he has shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.
verses.after: They do not know or understand, for their eyes are smeared shut so they cannot see, and their hearts so they cannot discern.
verses.tsw_comparator: They do not know, neither do they consider: for he has shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.

verses.rationale: Preserve long self-questioning that never occurs.
verses.before: No one thinks, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, "I have burned part of it in the fire. Yes, I have also baked bread on its coals. I have roasted meat and eaten it. Will I make the rest of it into an abomination? Will I bow down to a tree trunk?"
verses.after: No one takes it to heart or has the knowledge and understanding to say, “Half I burned in the fire; I baked bread on its coals, roasted meat and ate it. Shall I make the rest an abomination? Shall I bow before a block of wood?”
verses.tsw_comparator: No one thinks, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, "I have burned part of it in the fire. Yes, I have also baked bread on its coals. I have roasted meat and eaten it. Will I make the rest of it into an abomination? Will I bow down to a tree trunk?"

verses.rationale: Keep ash-feeding and grasped lie.
verses.before: He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has turned him aside; and he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, "Isn't there a lie in my right hand?"
verses.after: He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has led him astray; he cannot rescue himself or say, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has turned him aside; and he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, "Isn't there a lie in my right hand?"

verses.rationale: Retain doubled servant and passive nonforgetting.
verses.before: Remember these things, Jacob and Israel; for you are my servant. I have formed you. You are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.
verses.after: “Remember these things, Jacob, Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you; you are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember these things, Jacob and Israel; for you are my servant. I have formed you. You are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.

verses.rationale: Keep cloud imagery and redemption preceding return.
verses.before: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
verses.after: I have wiped away your rebellions like a thick cloud, your sins like a cloud. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.

verses.rationale: Retain entire creation chorus and two names.
verses.before: Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of your trees, for the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.
verses.after: Sing, heavens, for the **LORD** has acted! Shout, depths of the earth! Burst into song, mountains, forest, and every tree in it! For the **LORD** has redeemed Jacob and displays his glory in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of your trees, for the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.

verses.rationale: Follow by-myself read-form, noting written who-with-me question.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, and the one who formed you from the womb: "I am the LORD, who makes everything; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself;
verses.after: The **LORD**, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb, says: “I am the **LORD**, maker of everything, stretching out the heavens alone, spreading the earth by myself,
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, and the one who formed you from the womb: "I am the LORD, who makes all things; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself;

verses.rationale: Keep three defeated rival claims to knowledge.
verses.before: who frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; who turns wise men backward, and makes their knowledge foolish;
verses.after: frustrating liars’ signs and making fools of diviners, turning the wise back and making their knowledge foolish,
verses.tsw_comparator: who frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; who turns wise men backward, and makes their knowledge foolish;

verses.rationale: Preserve servant singular, messengers plural, and restoration promises.
verses.before: who confirms the word of his servant, and performs the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, 'She will be inhabited;' and of the cities of Judah, 'They will be built,' and I will raise up its waste places;'
verses.after: confirming my servant’s word and fulfilling my messengers’ counsel; saying of Jerusalem, ‘She will be inhabited,’ and of Judah’s cities, ‘They will be rebuilt; I will raise her ruins,’
verses.tsw_comparator: who confirms the word of his servant, and performs the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, 'She will be inhabited;' and of the cities of Judah, 'They will be built,' and I will raise up its waste places;'

verses.rationale: Keep divine command to deep and rivers.
verses.before: who says to the deep, 'Be dry,' and 'I will dry up your rivers;'
verses.after: saying to the deep, ‘Dry up! I will dry your rivers,’
verses.tsw_comparator: who says to the deep, 'Be dry,' and 'I will dry up your rivers;'

verses.rationale: Keep explicit Cyrus, shepherd designation, and temple-address shift.
verses.before: Who says of Cyrus, 'He is my shepherd, and will perform all my pleasure,' even saying of Jerusalem, 'She will be built;' and of the temple, 'Your foundation will be laid.'"
verses.after: saying of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd! He will fulfill all my purpose,’ and saying of Jerusalem, ‘She will be rebuilt,’ and of the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Who says of Cyrus, 'He is my shepherd, and will perform all my pleasure,' even saying of Jerusalem, 'She will be built;' and of the temple, 'Your foundation will be laid.'"

verses.rationale: Retain foreign king as anointed and bodily conquest image.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD to the LORD’s anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped, to subdue nations before him and loosen the belts of kings, to open doors before him so that gates will not be shut:
verses.after: The **LORD** says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to loosen kings’ belts, to open doors before him so gates cannot be shut:
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD to the LORD’s anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped, to subdue nations before him and loosen the belts of kings, to open doors before him so that gates will not be shut:

verses.rationale: Follow straighten read-form and retain uncertain terrain word.
verses.before: "I will go before you, and make the rough places smooth. I will break the doors of brass in pieces, and cut apart the bars of iron.
verses.after: “I will go ahead of you and straighten the rough places. I will shatter bronze doors and cut through iron bars.
verses.tsw_comparator: "I will go before you, and make the rough places smooth. I will break the doors of brass in pieces, and cut apart the bars of iron.

verses.rationale: Keep hidden wealth and purpose of naming.
verses.before: I will give you the treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, that you may know that it is I, the LORD, who call you by your name, even the God of Israel.
verses.after: I will give you treasures kept in darkness, wealth hidden in secret places, so you may know that I am the **LORD**, Israel’s God, who calls you by name.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give you the treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, that you may know that it is I, the LORD, who call you by your name, even the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve Cyrus’s ignorance despite divine call.
verses.before: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel my chosen, I have called you by your name. I have surnamed you, though you have not known me.
verses.after: For the sake of Jacob my servant, Israel my chosen one, I call you by name and give you a title, though you do not know me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel my chosen, I have called you by your name. I have surnamed you, though you have not known me.

verses.rationale: Repeat ignorance and exclusive deity claim.
verses.before: I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides me there is no God. I equip you, though you have not known me,
verses.after: I am the **LORD**, and there is no other; apart from me there is no God. I equip you, though you do not know me,
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides me there is no God. I equip you, though you have not known me,

verses.rationale: Keep worldwide recognition and exact repeated declaration.
verses.before: that they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is none besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no one else.
verses.after: so people from the sun’s rising to its setting may know there is none besides me. I am the **LORD**, and there is no other.
verses.tsw_comparator: that they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is none besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no one else.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine agency over both opposites and note ra range.
verses.before: forming light and creating darkness, making well-being and creating calamity; I am the LORD, who does all these things.
verses.after: I form light and create darkness, make well-being and create disaster. I, the **LORD**, do all these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: forming light and creating darkness, making well-being and creating calamity; I am the LORD, who does all these things.

verses.rationale: Keep productive cosmic metaphor and repeated righteousness.
verses.before: Distil, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may bring forth salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
verses.after: Drip down, heavens above; let the skies rain righteousness. Let the earth open and salvation bear fruit, and let righteousness sprout with it. I, the **LORD**, have created it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Distil, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may bring forth salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up with it. I, the LORD, have created it.

verses.rationale: Retain shard/clay protest and odd hand denial.
verses.before: Woe to the one who strives with his Maker—a clay pot among the clay pots of the earth! Will the clay ask the one who fashions it, 'What are you making?' or your work, 'He has no hands?'
verses.after: Woe to one who quarrels with his Maker, a potsherd among earth’s potsherds! Does clay ask its potter, “What are you making?” Does your work say, “He has no hands”?
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who strives with his Maker—a clay pot among the clay pots of the earth! Will the clay ask the one who fashions it, 'What are you making?' or your work, 'He has no hands?'

verses.rationale: Keep gender-specific parental questions.
verses.before: Woe to the one who says to a father, 'What have you become the father of?' or to a mother, 'To what have you given birth?'"
verses.after: Woe to one who says to a father, “What are you begetting?” or to a woman, “What are you laboring to bring forth?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who says to a father, 'What have you become the father of?' or to a mother, 'To what have you given birth?'"

verses.rationale: Choose rhetorical challenge for second clause, noting imperative alternative.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker: "You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands!
verses.after: The **LORD**, Israel’s Holy One and Maker, says: “Ask me about things to come; would you command me about my children and the work of my hands?
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker: "You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands!

verses.rationale: Retain first-person creation and ordered celestial host.
verses.before: I have made the earth, and created man on it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens; and all their army have I commanded.
verses.after: I made the earth and created humanity upon it. My own hands stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have made the earth, and created man on it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens; and all their army have I commanded.

verses.rationale: Keep Cyrus’s task and absence of payment.
verses.before: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make straight all his ways: he will build my city, and he will let my exiles go free, not for price nor reward, says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: I stirred him up in righteousness and will make all his roads straight. He will build my city and release my exiles, without payment or bribe,” says the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make straight all his ways: he will build my city, and he will let my exiles go free, not for price nor reward, says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserve coerced tribute and feminine recipient without adding name.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: "The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you, and they will be yours. They will go after you. In chains they will come over; and they will fall down to you. They will make supplication to you: 'Surely God is in you; and there is none else, there is no other god.
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “Egypt’s labor and Cush’s trade, and the tall Sabeans, will come over to you and be yours. They will follow you, coming in chains, bowing before you and pleading with you: ‘Surely God is in you, and there is no other; there is no other God.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: "The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you, and they will be yours. They will go after you. In chains they will come over; and they will fall down to you. They will make supplication to you: 'Surely God is in you; and there is none else, there is no other god.

verses.rationale: Keep hiddenness beside saving identity.
verses.before: Most certainly you are a God who hid yourself, God of Israel, the Savior.'"
verses.after: Truly, you are a God who hides himself, Israel’s God, Savior.
verses.tsw_comparator: Most certainly you are a God who hid yourself, God of Israel, the Savior.'"

verses.rationale: Retain collective shame and artisan target.
verses.before: They will be disappointed, yes, confounded, all of them; they will go into confusion together who are makers of idols.
verses.after: All of them are ashamed and disgraced; the makers of images go away in disgrace together.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be disappointed, yes, confounded, all of them; they will go into confusion together who are makers of idols.

verses.rationale: Keep shift to direct address and enduring salvation.
verses.before: Yet Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation: you will not be disappointed nor confounded world without end.
verses.after: But Israel is saved by the **LORD** with everlasting salvation. You will not be ashamed or disgraced forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation: you will not be disappointed nor confounded world without end.

verses.rationale: Retain creation’s inhabited purpose and two names.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and did not create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is no one else.
verses.after: For the **LORD** says, the Creator of the heavens—he is God— the one who formed and made the earth, who established it, who did not create it as emptiness but formed it to be inhabited: “I am the **LORD**, and there is no other.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and did not create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is no one else.

verses.rationale: Keep emptiness echo from creation and transparent speech.
verses.before: I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the land of darkness; I did not say to the seed of Jacob, Seek you me in vain: I, the LORD, speak righteousness, I declare things that are right.
verses.after: I did not speak in secret, in a dark land; I did not tell Jacob’s offspring, ‘Seek me in emptiness.’ I, the **LORD**, speak righteousness, declare what is straight.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the land of darkness; I did not say to the seed of Jacob, Seek you me in vain: I, the LORD, speak righteousness, I declare things that are right.

verses.rationale: Preserve invitation to survivors and carried idols’ incapacity.
verses.before: Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations: they have no knowledge who carry the wood of their engraved image, and pray to a god that cannot save.
verses.after: Gather and come, draw near together, you survivors of the nations! Those who carry their wooden idols know nothing; they pray to a god who cannot save.
verses.tsw_comparator: Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations: they have no knowledge who carry the wood of their engraved image, and pray to a god that cannot save.

verses.rationale: Keep judicial summons and prediction proof.
verses.before: Declare you, and bring it forth; yes, let them take counsel together: who has shown this from ancient time? who has declared it of old? Haven't I, the LORD? and there is no God else besides me, a just God and a Savior; there is no one besides me.
verses.after: Declare your case; present it! Let them consult together. Who made this heard long ago, announced it in advance? Was it not I, the **LORD**? There is no other God beside me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none except me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare you, and bring it forth; yes, let them take counsel together: who has shown this from ancient time? who has declared it of old? Haven't I, the LORD? and there is no God else besides me, a just God and a Savior; there is no one besides me.

verses.rationale: Retain universal invitation and singular divine claim.
verses.before: Look to me, and be you saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is none else.
verses.after: Turn to me and be saved, all earth’s ends, for I am God, and there is no other.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look to me, and be you saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is none else.

verses.rationale: Preserve self-oath and every knee/tongue parallel.
verses.before: By myself have I sworn, the word is gone forth from my mouth in righteousness, and will not return, that to me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear.
verses.after: By myself I have sworn; a righteous word has gone from my mouth and will not return: to me every knee will bend, every tongue will swear allegiance.
verses.tsw_comparator: By myself have I sworn, the word is gone forth from my mouth in righteousness, and will not return, that to me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear.

verses.rationale: Keep reported speech and ambiguous pronoun transitions.
verses.before: Only in the LORD, it is said of me, is righteousness and strength; even to him will men come; and all people who were incensed against him will be disappointed.
verses.after: ‘Only in the **LORD**,’ people will say of me, ‘are righteousness and strength.’ To him all who rage against him will come and be ashamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only in the LORD, it is said of me, is righteousness and strength; even to him will men come; and all those who were incensed against him will be disappointed.

verses.rationale: Render justified juridically in context and retain all offspring.
verses.before: In the LORD will all the seed of Israel be justified, and will glory.
verses.after: In the **LORD** all Israel’s offspring will be vindicated and glory.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In the LORD will all the seed of Israel be justified, and will glory.

verses.rationale: Keep named Babylonian gods and burdened animals.
verses.before: Bel bows down, Nebo stoops; their idols are on the animals, and on the livestock: the things that you carried about are made a load, a burden to the weary animal.
verses.after: Bel bows, Nebo stoops; their idols are loaded onto animals and cattle. What you carried is now a load, a burden for weary beasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bel bows down, Nebo stoops; their idols are on the animals, and on the livestock: the things that you carried about are made a load, a burden to the weary animal.

verses.rationale: Preserve gods’ inability and shared deportation.
verses.before: They stoop, they bow down together; they could not deliver the burden, but themselves are gone into captivity.
verses.after: They stoop and bow together; they cannot rescue the burden, and they themselves go into captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: They stoop, they bow down together; they could not deliver the burden, but themselves are gone into captivity.

verses.rationale: Contrast carried people with carried idols.
verses.before: Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been borne by me from their birth, that have been carried from the womb;
verses.after: “Listen to me, Jacob’s house, all the remnant of Israel’s house, you whom I have borne from the womb, carried from birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been borne by me from their birth, that have been carried from the womb;

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated first-person carrying across life stages.
verses.before: Even to your old age I am the same; even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry and deliver you.
verses.after: Even to old age I am he; even when you are gray I will bear you. I made you, and I will carry you; I will bear you and rescue you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even to your old age I am the same; even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry and deliver you.

verses.rationale: Keep doubled comparison challenge.
verses.before: To whom will you liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, that we may be like?
verses.after: To whom will you liken me and make me equal? With whom will you compare me, that we should be alike?
verses.tsw_comparator: To whom will you liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, that we may be like?

verses.rationale: Retain economic production before worship.
verses.before: Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver in the balance. They hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god. They fall down—yes, they worship.
verses.after: People pour gold from a bag, weigh silver on a balance, hire a goldsmith, and he makes it into a god. Then they bow and worship.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver in the balance. They hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god. They fall down—yes, they worship.

verses.rationale: Keep immobility and failed rescue in carried-idol contrast.
verses.before: They bear it on the shoulder, they carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands, from its place it will not move: yes, one may cry to it, yet it can not answer, nor save him out of his trouble.
verses.after: They lift it onto a shoulder and carry it, set it in its place, and there it stands. It cannot move from that spot. Though someone cries to it, it does not answer; it cannot save him from his distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: They bear it on the shoulder, they carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands, from its place it will not move: yes, one may cry to it, yet it can not answer, nor save him out of his trouble.

verses.rationale: Choose composed-attention sense for rare imperative with note.
verses.before: Remember this, and show yourselves men; bring it again to mind, you transgressors.
verses.after: Remember this and take it to heart; bring it to mind, you rebels.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember this, and show yourselves men; bring it again to mind, you transgressors.

verses.rationale: Keep positive remember alongside43:18 negative.
verses.before: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me;
verses.after: Remember the former things from long ago: I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and none is like me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me;
