verses.rationale: Retain temporal reach and purpose.
verses.before: declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done; saying, My counsel will stand, and I will do all my pleasure;
verses.after: I announce the end from the beginning, from ancient times things not yet done. I say, ‘My counsel will stand; I will fulfill all my purpose.’
verses.tsw_comparator: declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done; saying, My counsel will stand, and I will do all my pleasure;

verses.rationale: Follow my-counsel read-form and preserve bird image.
verses.before: calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country; yes, I have spoken, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed, I will also do it.
verses.after: I call a bird of prey from the east, from a distant land the man of my counsel. I have spoken; I will bring it about. I have formed it; I will do it.
verses.tsw_comparator: calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country; yes, I have spoken, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed, I will also do it.

verses.rationale: Keep resistant hearts rather than emend to disheartened.
verses.before: Listen to me, you stout-hearted, who are far from righteousness:
verses.after: Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted, far from righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to me, you stout-hearted, who are far from righteousness:

verses.rationale: Preserve near/far response and righteousness/salvation pairing.
verses.before: I bring near my righteousness, it will not be far off, and my salvation will not wait; and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory.
verses.after: I bring my righteousness near; it is not far away. My salvation will not delay. I will grant salvation in Zion, my splendor to Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I bring near my righteousness, it will not be far off, and my salvation will not wait; and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory.

verses.rationale: Keep gendered city humiliation and lost throne.
verses.before: Come down, and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans: for you will no more be called tender and delicate.
verses.after: Come down and sit in the dust, virgin Daughter Babylon! Sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called tender and pampered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come down, and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans: for you will no more be called tender and delicate.

verses.rationale: Preserve forced labor and bodily exposure.
verses.before: Take the millstones, and grind meal; remove your veil, strip off the train, uncover the leg, pass through the rivers.
verses.after: Take millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, lift your skirt, bare your legs and cross rivers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take the millstones, and grind meal; remove your veil, strip off the train, uncover the leg, pass through the rivers.

verses.rationale: Choose spare sense for difficult encounter verb with note.
verses.before: Your nakedness will be uncovered, yes, your shame will be seen: I will take vengeance, and will spare no man.
verses.after: Your nakedness will be exposed, your disgrace seen. “I will take vengeance and spare no one.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your nakedness will be uncovered, yes, your shame will be seen: I will take vengeance, and will spare no man.

verses.rationale: Keep interjected communal confession.
verses.before: Our Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: Our Redeemer—the **LORD** of hosts is his name— is Israel’s Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated loss of title.
verses.before: Sit you silent, and get you into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans; for you will no more be called The mistress of kingdoms.
verses.after: Sit silent; enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called mistress of kingdoms.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sit you silent, and get you into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans; for you will no more be called The mistress of kingdoms.

verses.rationale: Retain divine agency and Babylon’s cruelty toward elderly.
verses.before: I was angry with my people, I profaned my inheritance, and gave them into your hand: you did show them no mercy; on the aged have you very heavily laid your yoke.
verses.after: “I was angry with my people; I profaned my inheritance and handed them over to you. You showed them no compassion; on the aged you laid an exceedingly heavy yoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was angry with my people, I profaned my inheritance, and gave them into your hand: you did show them no mercy; on the aged have you very heavily laid your yoke.

verses.rationale: Keep arrogant future and ignored consequence.
verses.before: You said, I will be mistress forever; so that you did not lay these things to your heart, neither did remember the latter end of it.
verses.after: You said, ‘I will be mistress forever.’ You did not take these things to heart or remember their outcome.
verses.tsw_comparator: You said, I will be mistress forever; so that you did not lay these things to your heart, neither did remember the latter end of it.

verses.rationale: Preserve quasi-divine boast and family-loss denial.
verses.before: Now therefore hear this, you who are given to pleasures, who sit securely, who say in your heart, I am, and there is none else besides me; I will not sit as a widow, neither will I know the loss of children:
verses.after: Now hear this, pleasure-loving one, sitting secure, saying in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no other. I will never sit as a widow nor know the loss of children.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore hear this, you who are given to pleasures, who sit securely, who say in your heart, I am, and there is none else besides me; I will not sit as a widow, neither will I know the loss of children:

verses.rationale: Keep two losses, one day, and ineffective magic.
verses.before: but these two things will come to you in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood; in their full measure will they come on you, in the multitude of your sorceries, and the great abundance of your enchantments.
verses.after: Both will come upon you in an instant, on one day: loss of children and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, despite your many sorceries and the great power of your spells.
verses.tsw_comparator: but these two things will come to you in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood; in their full measure will they come on you, in the multitude of your sorceries, and the great abundance of your enchantments.

verses.rationale: Repeat exact boast and corrupted wisdom.
verses.before: For you have trusted in your wickedness; you have said, None sees me; your wisdom and your knowledge, it has perverted you, and you have said in your heart, I am, and there is none else besides me.
verses.after: You trusted in your evil and said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray; you said in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no other.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have trusted in your wickedness; you have said, None sees me; your wisdom and your knowledge, it has perverted you, and you have said in your heart, I am, and there is none else besides me.

verses.rationale: Choose charm sense for uncertain dawn verb, note alternative.
verses.before: So will evil come on you; you will not know the dawning of it: and mischief will fall on you; you will not be able to put it away: and desolation will come on you suddenly, which you do not know.
verses.after: Evil will come upon you, and you will not know how to charm it away. Disaster will fall upon you, and you cannot avert it. Ruin you did not foresee will come suddenly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore will evil come on you; you will not know the dawning of it: and mischief will fall on you; you will not be able to put it away: and desolation will come on you suddenly, which you do not know.

verses.rationale: Keep ironic perhaps and lifelong labor.
verses.before: Stand now with your enchantments, and with the multitude of your sorceries, in which you have labored from your youth; if so be you will be able to profit, if so be you may prevail.
verses.after: Stand fast, then, in your spells and many sorceries, with which you have labored from youth. Perhaps you can gain some benefit; perhaps you can strike terror!
verses.tsw_comparator: Stand now with your enchantments, and with the multitude of your sorceries, in which you have labored from your youth; if so be you will be able to profit, if so be you may prevail.

verses.rationale: Follow participial read-form and retain ancient divination practices.
verses.before: You are wearied in the multitude of your counsels: let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save you from the things that will come on you.
verses.after: You are worn out with all your advisers. Let them stand up and save you— those who divide the heavens, gaze at stars, and tell you month by month what will happen to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are wearied in the multitude of your counsels: let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save you from the things that will come on you.

verses.rationale: Keep destructive versus warming fire distinction.
verses.before: Look, they will be as stubble; the fire will burn them; they will not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: it will not be a coal to warm at, nor a fire to sit before.
verses.after: Look, they are stubble; fire burns them. They cannot rescue themselves from the flame’s power. This is no coal for warmth, no fire to sit beside.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, they will be as stubble; the fire will burn them; they will not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: it will not be a coal to warm at, nor a fire to sit before.

verses.rationale: Preserve traders not silently astrologers and absent savior.
verses.before: Thus will the things be to you in which you have labored: people who have trafficked with you from your youth will wander everyone to his quarter; there will be none to save you.
verses.after: Such are those with whom you labored, your traders from youth. Each wanders his own way; there is no one to save you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus will the things be to you in which you have labored: those who have trafficked with you from your youth will wander everyone to his quarter; there will be none to save you.

verses.rationale: Retain waters text and note offspring euphemism rather than loins emendation.
verses.before: Hear you this, house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah; who swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness
verses.after: Hear this, Jacob’s house, you called by Israel’s name, who came from Judah’s waters, who swear by the **LORD**’s name and invoke Israel’s God, but not in truth or righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear you this, house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah; who swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness

verses.rationale: Make city affiliation clear without approving false reliance.
verses.before: (for they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves on the God of Israel; the LORD of Hosts is his name):
verses.after: They call themselves citizens of the holy city and lean on Israel’s God— the **LORD** of hosts is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: (for they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves on the God of Israel; the LORD of Hosts is his name):

verses.rationale: Preserve announcement before sudden fulfillment.
verses.before: I have declared the former things from of old; yes, they went forth out of my mouth, and I shown them: suddenly I did them, and they happened.
verses.after: “The former things I announced long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I made them heard. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have declared the former things from of old; yes, they went forth out of my mouth, and I shown them: suddenly I did them, and they happened.

verses.rationale: Keep two resistant body materials.
verses.before: Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your brow brass;
verses.after: I knew you were stubborn, your neck an iron sinew, your forehead bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your brow brass;

verses.rationale: Retain prediction’s anti-idolatry rationale.
verses.before: so I have declared it to you from of old; before it happened I shown it you; lest you should say, My idol has done them, and my engraved image, and my molten image, has commanded them.
verses.after: So I told you long ago; before it happened I made you hear, lest you say, ‘My idol did these things; my carved image and cast image commanded them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore I have declared it to you from of old; before it came to pass I shown it you; lest you should say, My idol has done them, and my engraved image, and my molten image, has commanded them.

verses.rationale: Preserve hearing/seeing/declaration sequence and newness.
verses.before: You have heard it; see all this; and you, will you not declare it? I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not known.
verses.after: You have heard; now look at it all. Will you not declare it? From now on I tell you new things, hidden things you have not known.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have heard it; see all this; and you, will you not declare it? I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not known.

verses.rationale: Retain created-now claim rather than simple disclosure.
verses.before: They are created now, and not from of old; and before this day you did not hear them; lest you should say, Look, I knew them.
verses.after: They are created now, not long ago; before today you had not heard of them, lest you say, ‘Look, I knew them already.’
verses.tsw_comparator: They are created now, and not from of old; and before this day you did not hear them; lest you should say, Look, I knew them.

verses.rationale: Keep three negatives and emphatic betrayal.
verses.before: Yes, you did not hear; yes, you did not know; yes, from of old your ear was not opened: for I knew that you did deal very treacherously, and was called a transgressor from the womb.
verses.after: You had not heard, you had not known; your ear had not been opened long ago. For I knew you would betray, betray; from the womb you were called a rebel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, you did not hear; yes, you did not know; yes, from of old your ear was not opened: for I knew that you did deal very treacherously, and was called a transgressor from the womb.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine motives and restrained wrath.
verses.before: For my name's sake will I defer my anger, and for my praise will I refrain for you, that I not cut you off.
verses.after: For my name’s sake I delay my anger; for my praise I restrain it toward you, so I do not cut you off.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my name's sake will I defer my anger, and for my praise will I refrain for you, that I not cut you off.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned chosen, note tested alternative.
verses.before: Look, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
verses.after: Look, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.

verses.rationale: Repeat motive and mark contextual name supply in note.
verses.before: For my own sake, for my own sake, will I do it; for how should my name be profaned? and my glory I will not give to another.
verses.after: For my own sake, for my own sake I act. How could my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my own sake, for my own sake, will I do it; for how should my name be profaned? and my glory I will not give to another.

verses.rationale: Retain called relation and first/last refrain.
verses.before: Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
verses.after: Listen to me, Jacob, Israel whom I called! I am he; I am first, and I am last.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.

verses.rationale: Keep embodied creation and obedient cosmic response.
verses.before: Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens: when I call to them, they stand up together.
verses.after: My hand founded the earth; my right hand spread out the heavens. When I call them, they stand together.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens: when I call to them, they stand up together.

verses.rationale: Preserve unnamed beloved agent and compressed arm clause.
verses.before: Assemble yourselves, all you, and hear; who among them has declared these things? He whom the LORD loves will perform his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm will be on the Chaldeans.
verses.after: Gather, all of you, and hear! Who among them announced these things? The **LORD** loves him; he will fulfill his purpose against Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.
verses.tsw_comparator: Assemble yourselves, all you, and hear; who among them has declared these things? He whom the LORD loves will perform his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm will be on the Chaldeans.

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic I and consecutive divine acts.
verses.before: I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him; I have brought him, and he will make his way prosperous.
verses.after: I, I have spoken; I have called him. I have brought him, and his way will succeed.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him; I have brought him, and he will make his way prosperous.

verses.rationale: Preserve new sending voice and ambiguous Spirit’s grammatical role.
verses.before: Come you near to me, hear you this; from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit.
verses.after: Come near me and hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it came to be, I was there.” And now the Lord **GOD** has sent me, and his Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come you near to me, hear you this; from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit.

verses.rationale: Keep two names and instructing/guiding roles.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your good, who leads you in the way you should go.
verses.after: The **LORD**, your Redeemer, Israel’s Holy One, says: “I am the **LORD** your God, teaching you what benefits you, guiding you in the way you should go.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your good, who leads you in the way you should go.

verses.rationale: Preserve unrealized condition and two water images.
verses.before: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! then had your peace been as a river, and your righteousness as the waves of the sea:
verses.after: If only you had listened to my commandments! Your peace would have been like a river, your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! then had your peace been as a river, and your righteousness as the waves of the sea:

verses.rationale: Keep descendants and corporate name with grain ambiguity noted.
verses.before: your seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of your body like the grains of it: his name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.
verses.after: Your offspring would have been like sand, your descendants like its grains; their name would never have been cut off or destroyed from my presence.”
verses.tsw_comparator: your seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of your body like the grains of it: his name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.

verses.rationale: Preserve double departure and public redemption announcement.
verses.before: Go you forth from Babylon, flee you from the Chaldeans; with a voice of singing declare you, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth: say you, the LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob.
verses.after: Go out from Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With a joyful shout declare this, make it heard; carry it to earth’s ends: “The **LORD** has redeemed his servant Jacob!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Go you forth from Babylon, flee you from the Chaldeans; with a voice of singing declare you, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth: say you, the LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob.

verses.rationale: Keep exodus water miracle and repeated rock.
verses.before: They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts; he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them; he split the rock also, and the waters gushed out.
verses.after: They did not thirst when he led them through wastelands; he made water flow for them from rock. He split rock, and water gushed out.
verses.tsw_comparator: They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts; he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them; he split the rock also, and the waters gushed out.

verses.rationale: Retain sharp concluding limit and later refrain.
verses.before: There is no peace, says the LORD, to the wicked.
verses.after: “There is no peace for the wicked,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no peace, says the LORD, to the wicked.

verses.rationale: Retains prenatal calling and distant maritime audience without naming the speaker beyond the poem.
verses.before: Listen, islands, to me; and listen, you peoples, from far: the LORD has called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother has he made mention of my name:
verses.after: Listen to me, coastlands; hear me, peoples far away. The **LORD** called me from the womb; from inside my mother he spoke my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen, islands, to me; and listen, you peoples, from far: the LORD has called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother has he made mention of my name:

verses.rationale: Preserves both weapon metaphors and repeated concealment.
verses.before: and he has made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand has he hid me: and he has made me a polished shaft; in his quiver has he kept me close:
verses.after: He made my mouth a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me a polished arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he has made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand has he hid me: and he has made me a polished shaft; in his quiver has he kept me close:

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit identification Israel rather than substituting an interpreted individual.
verses.before: and he said to me, You are my servant; Israel, in whom I will be glorified.
verses.after: He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will display my glory.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and he said to me, You are my servant; Israel, in whom I will be glorified.

verses.rationale: Preserves servant discouragement alongside confidence, including vapor image.
verses.before: Yet I said, I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely the justice due to me is with the LORD, and my recompense with my God.
verses.after: But I said, “I have worked for nothing; I have spent my strength on emptiness and vapor. Yet my cause rests with the **LORD**, and my reward with my God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I said, I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely the justice due to me is with the LORD, and my recompense with my God.

verses.rationale: Follows read form to him rather than written not; preserves distinction between servant and restored Israel.
verses.before: Now says the LORD who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, and that Israel be gathered to him (for I am honorable in the eyes of the LORD, and my God is become my strength);
verses.after: And now the **LORD** speaks— he who formed me in the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him and gather Israel to him. I am honored in the **LORD**’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now says the LORD who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, and that Israel be gathered to him (for I am honorable in the eyes of the LORD, and my God is become my strength);

verses.rationale: Keeps restoration and worldwide salvation together; follows read survivors form.
verses.before: The LORD says, “It is too small a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and restore the preserved of Israel. I will also make you a light to the nations, so that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”
verses.after: He says, “It is too small a task for you to be my servant merely to raise up Jacob’s tribes and bring back Israel’s survivors. I will also make you a light for the nations, so my salvation may reach the ends of the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD says, “It is too small a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and restore the preserved of Israel. I will also make you a light to the nations, so that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”

verses.rationale: Retains singular nation and reversal from servant of rulers to honored figure.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers: Kings will see and arise; princes, and they will worship; because of the LORD who is faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD**, Israel’s Redeemer, his Holy One, says to one deeply despised, abhorred by the nation, a servant of rulers: “Kings will see and rise; princes will bow down, because the **LORD** is faithful, Israel’s Holy One has chosen you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers: Kings will see and arise; princes, and they will worship; because of the LORD who is faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.

verses.rationale: Preserves servant as covenant and concrete land allotment.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, In an acceptable time have I answered you, and in a day of salvation have I helped you; and I will preserve you, and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make them inherit the desolate heritage:
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “At a time of favor I answered you; on a day of salvation I helped you. I will guard you and give you as a covenant for the people, to restore the land and allot its desolate inheritances,
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, In an acceptable time have I answered you, and in a day of salvation have I helped you; and I will preserve you, and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make them inherit the desolate heritage:

verses.rationale: Links release commission to pastoral return imagery without replacing prisoners with an abstraction.
verses.before: saying to people who are bound, Go forth; to people who are in darkness, Show yourselves. They will feed in the ways, and on all bare heights will be their pasture.
verses.after: to say to prisoners, ‘Come out!’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves!’ They will graze along the roads and find pasture on every bare hill.
verses.tsw_comparator: saying to those who are bound, Go forth; to those who are in darkness, Show yourselves. They will feed in the ways, and on all bare heights will be their pasture.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily needs and compassionate guidance parallel.
verses.before: They will not hunger nor thirst; neither will the heat nor sun strike them: for the one who has mercy on them will lead them, even by springs of water he will guide them.
verses.after: They will neither hunger nor thirst; scorching heat and sun will not strike them. The one who has compassion on them will lead them and guide them beside springs of water.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not hunger nor thirst; neither will the heat nor sun strike them: for the one who has mercy on them will lead them, even by springs of water he will guide them.

verses.rationale: Retains mountains as road and possessive my.
verses.before: I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways will be exalted.
verses.after: I will turn all my mountains into a road, and my highways will be raised up.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways will be exalted.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncertain Sinim without asserting a modern country.
verses.before: Look, these will come from far; and look, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim.
verses.after: Look, these will come from far away; look, these from the north and the west, and these from the land of Sinim.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, these will come from far; and look, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim.

verses.rationale: Follows read imperative and carries comfort theme forward.
verses.before: Sing, heavens; and be joyful, earth; and break forth into singing, mountains: for the LORD has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
verses.after: Sing, heavens! Rejoice, earth! Mountains, break into song! For the **LORD** has comforted his people and will have compassion on his afflicted ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing, heavens; and be joyful, earth; and break forth into singing, mountains: for the LORD has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.

verses.rationale: Keeps Zion’s objection immediately after announced comfort and distinguishes divine titles.
verses.before: Yet Zion said, the LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.
verses.after: But Zion said, “The **LORD** has abandoned me; my Lord has forgotten me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Zion said, the LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal analogy, specific son and exceptional possibility.
verses.before: Can a woman forget her nursing child or have no compassion on the child of her womb? Even these may forget, but I will not forget you.
verses.after: “Can a woman forget her nursing child and feel no compassion for the son she bore? Even if these women forget, I will not forget you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Can a woman forget her nursing child or have no compassion on the child of her womb? Even these may forget, but I will not forget you.

verses.rationale: Keeps embodied engraving and actual city walls.
verses.before: Look, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me.
verses.after: Look, I have engraved you on my palms; your walls are always before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned children rather than repointing builders.
verses.before: Your children make haste; your destroyers and people who made you waste will go forth from you.
verses.after: Your children hurry back; those who tore you down and laid you waste depart from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your children make haste; your destroyers and those who made you waste will go forth from you.

verses.rationale: Keeps oath and children as bridal ornaments.
verses.before: Lift up your eyes round about, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live, says the LORD, you will surely clothe you with them all as with an ornament, and gird yourself with them, like a bride.
verses.after: Lift your eyes and look around: they have all gathered and come to you. As I live,” declares the **LORD**, “you will wear them all like jewelry and bind them on like a bride.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your eyes round about, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live, says the LORD, you will surely clothe you with them all as with an ornament, and gird yourself with them, like a bride.

verses.rationale: Preserves devouring image and crowding reversal.
verses.before: For, as for your waste and your desolate places, and your land that has been destroyed, surely now will you be too small for the inhabitants, and people who swallowed you up will be far away.
verses.after: Your ruins, your desolate places, your devastated land— now you will be too cramped for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you will be far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: For, as for your waste and your desolate places, and your land that has been destroyed, surely now will you be too small for the inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.

verses.rationale: Makes paradox of bereavement and children readable without erasing it.
verses.before: The children of your bereavement will yet say in your ears, The place is too small for me; give place to me that I may dwell.
verses.after: The children born after your bereavement will yet say within your hearing, ‘This place is too cramped for me; make room for me to live here.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of your bereavement will yet say in your ears, The place is too small for me; give place to me that I may dwell.

verses.rationale: Retains female city’s sequence of astonished questions.
verses.before: Then will you say in your heart, Who has conceived these for me, seeing I have been bereaved of my children, and am solitary, an exile, and wandering back and forth? and who has brought up these? Look, I was left alone; these, where were they?
verses.after: Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who bore these for me? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and cast aside. Who raised these? I was left all alone— where have these come from?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then will you say in your heart, Who has conceived these for me, seeing I have been bereaved of my children, and am solitary, an exile, and wandering back and forth? and who has brought up these? Look, I was left alone; these, where were they?

verses.rationale: Keeps sons and daughters and public gathering signals.
verses.before: Thus says the Lord GOD, Look, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and set up my banner to the peoples; and they will bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.
verses.after: This is what the Lord **GOD** says: “Look, I will lift my hand toward the nations and raise my banner for the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the Lord GOD, Look, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and set up my banner to the peoples; and they will bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.

verses.rationale: Preserves royal service and degrading dust image without softening power reversal.
verses.before: Kings will be your nursing fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers: they will bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet; and you will know that I am the LORD; and people who wait for me will not be disappointed.
verses.after: Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow before you, faces to the ground, and lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the **LORD**; those who wait for me will not be put to shame.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Kings will be your nursing fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers: they will bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet; and you will know that I am the LORD; and those who wait for me will not be disappointed.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned righteous rather than emending to tyrant; ambiguity noted.
verses.before: Will the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?
verses.after: Can plunder be taken from a warrior? Can the captives of someone in the right escape?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated contention and emphatic divine subject.
verses.before: But thus says the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the prey of the terrible will be delivered; for I will contend with the one who contends with you, and I will save your children.
verses.after: Yes, this is what the **LORD** says: “Even a warrior’s captives will be taken away; even a tyrant’s plunder will escape. I myself will contend with those who contend with you, and I myself will save your children.
verses.tsw_comparator: But thus says the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the prey of the terrible will be delivered; for I will contend with the one who contends with you, and I will save your children.

verses.rationale: Retains violent self-devouring image and all-flesh recognition.
verses.before: I will feed people who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
verses.after: I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will become drunk on their own blood as on new wine. Then all flesh will know that I am the **LORD**, your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserves both legal household metaphors and stated cause of expulsion.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorce, with which I have put her away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Look, for your iniquities were you sold, and for your transgressions was your mother put away.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Where is your mother’s divorce document by which I sent her away? Or to which of my creditors did I sell you? Look, you were sold because of your own offenses; your mother was sent away because of your rebellions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorce, with which I have put her away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Look, for your iniquities were you sold, and for your transgressions was your mother put away.

verses.rationale: Maintains questions and offensive physical consequences of dried water.
verses.before: Why, when I came, was there no man? when I called, was there none to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? Look, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stink, because there is no water, and die for thirst.
verses.after: Why, when I came, was no one there? Why, when I called, did no one answer? Is my hand too short to redeem? Have I no power to rescue? At my rebuke I dry up the sea and turn rivers into desert; their fish stink for lack of water and die of thirst.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why, when I came, was there no man? when I called, was there none to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? Look, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stink, because there is no water, and die for thirst.

verses.rationale: Retains heavens dressed for mourning.
verses.before: I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.
verses.after: I clothe the heavens in darkness and make sackcloth their covering.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.

verses.rationale: Links learned speaking to repeated listening; difficult sustain verb noted.
verses.before: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of people who are taught, so that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning the Lord GOD awakens; awakens my ear to listen as people who are taught.
verses.after: The Lord **GOD** has given me a learner’s tongue, so I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning after morning he awakens me; he awakens my ear to listen as learners do.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of those who are taught, so that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning the Lord GOD awakens; awakens my ear to listen as those who are taught.

verses.rationale: Preserves auditory image and two obedient responses.
verses.before: The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I did not turn backward.
verses.after: The Lord **GOD** opened my ear, and I did not rebel or turn back.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I did not turn backward.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily abuse and deliberate exposure.
verses.before: I gave my back to the strikers, and my cheeks to people who plucked off the hair; I did not hide my face from shame and spitting.
verses.after: I gave my back to those who beat me and my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard. I did not hide my face from insults and spit.
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave my back to the strikers, and my cheeks to those who plucked off the hair; I did not hide my face from shame and spitting.

verses.rationale: Keeps causal repetition and flint image despite humiliation already described.
verses.before: For the Lord GOD will help me; so I have not been confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I will not be disappointed.
verses.after: But the Lord **GOD** helps me, so I have not been disgraced. So I have set my face like flint, knowing I will not be put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore I have not been confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I will not be disappointed.

verses.rationale: Makes courtroom setting clear while retaining challenge sequence.
verses.before: He is near who justifies me; who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together: who is my adversary? Let him come near to me.
verses.after: The one who vindicates me is near. Who will bring a case against me? Let us stand together. Who is my accuser? Let him approach me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is near who justifies me; who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together: who is my adversary? Let him come near to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves condemnation question and textile decay image.
verses.before: Look, the Lord GOD will help me; who is the one who will condemn me? Look, all they will wax old as a garment, the moth will eat them up.
verses.after: Look, the Lord **GOD** helps me. Who can condemn me? They will all wear out like a garment; moths will eat them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the Lord GOD will help me; who is the one who will condemn me? Look, all they will wax old as a garment, the moth will eat them up.

verses.rationale: Keeps servant listener in darkness, not automatically morally wicked.
verses.before: Who is among you who fears the LORD, who obeys the voice of his servant? the one who walks in darkness, and has no light, let him trust in the name of the LORD, and rely on his God.
verses.after: Who among you fears the **LORD** and listens to his servant? Whoever walks in darkness and has no light should trust in the **LORD**’s name and lean on his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is among you who fears the LORD, who obeys the voice of his servant? the one who walks in darkness, and has no light, let him trust in the name of the LORD, and rely on his God.

verses.rationale: Preserves ironic command and divine responsibility for outcome.
verses.before: Look, all you who kindle a fire, who gird yourselves about with firebrands; walk you in the flame of your fire, and among the brands that you have kindled. This will you have of my hand; you will lie down in sorrow.
verses.after: Look, all you who kindle a fire and surround yourselves with flaming brands: walk by the light of your fire and the brands you have lit! This is what you receive from my hand: you will lie down in torment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, all you who kindle a fire, who gird yourselves about with firebrands; walk you in the flame of your fire, and among the brands that you have kindled. This will you have of my hand; you will lie down in sorrow.

verses.rationale: Retains rock and quarry ancestral images.
verses.before: Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn and to the quarry from which you were dug.
verses.after: “Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the **LORD**. Look to the rock from which you were cut and the quarry from which you were dug.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn and to the quarry from which you were dug.

verses.rationale: Names both ancestors and contrasts one with multiplication.
verses.before: Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him, and made him many.
verses.after: Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who gave you birth. He was only one when I called him, but I blessed him and made him many.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him, and made him many.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated comfort, Eden and garden rather than generic flourishing.
verses.before: For the LORD has comforted Zion; he has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in it, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.
verses.after: For the **LORD** has comforted Zion, comforted all her ruins. He will make her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the **LORD**’s garden. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of song.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has comforted Zion; he has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in it, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular possessive nation and outward instruction.
verses.before: Attend to me, my people; and give ear to me, my nation: for a law will go forth from me, and I will establish my justice for a light of the peoples.
verses.after: Pay attention to me, my people; my nation, listen to me. Instruction will go out from me, and I will establish my justice as a light for peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Attend to me, my people; and give ear to me, my nation: for a law will go forth from me, and I will establish my justice for a light of the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keeps plural arms and singular arm, righteousness-salvation pairing.
verses.before: My righteousness is near, my salvation is gone forth, and my arms will judge the peoples; the islands will wait for me, and on my arm will they trust.
verses.after: My righteousness is near; my salvation has gone out. My arms will judge the peoples. The coastlands wait for me; they put their hope in my arm.
verses.tsw_comparator: My righteousness is near, my salvation is gone forth, and my arms will judge the peoples; the islands will wait for me, and on my arm will they trust.

verses.rationale: Retains cosmic transience and pinned like-so comparison; gnat alternative noted.
verses.before: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish away like smoke, and the earth will wax old like a garment; and people who dwell in it will die in like manner: but my salvation will be forever, and my righteousness will not be abolished.
verses.after: Lift your eyes to the heavens; look at the earth below. The heavens will dissolve like smoke, the earth wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants die in the same way. But my salvation will last forever; my righteousness will never fail.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish away like smoke, and the earth will wax old like a garment; and those who dwell in it will die in like manner: but my salvation will be forever, and my righteousness will not be abolished.

verses.rationale: Keeps internal instruction and human hostility connected.
verses.before: Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; do not you fear the reproach of men, neither be you dismayed at their insults.
verses.after: Listen to me, you who know righteousness, people with my instruction in your hearts. Do not fear human insults or be shattered by their taunts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; do not you fear the reproach of men, neither be you dismayed at their insults.

verses.rationale: Maintains textile parallels and reversed righteousness-salvation order.
verses.before: For the moth will eat them up like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool; but my righteousness will be forever, and my salvation to all generations.
verses.after: For moths will eat them like a garment, and grubs will eat them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation through every generation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the moth will eat them up like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool; but my righteousness will be forever, and my salvation to all generations.

verses.rationale: Retains appeal to divine arm and mythic monster names without historic flattening.
verses.before: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD; awake, as in the days of old, the generations of ancient times. Isn't it you who did cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the monster?
verses.after: Awake, awake! Clothe yourself in strength, arm of the **LORD**! Awake as in days long past, generations of old. Was it not you who cut Rahab apart and pierced the sea monster?
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD; awake, as in the days of old, the generations of ancient times. Isn't it you who did cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the monster?

verses.rationale: Preserves connection between monster defeat and sea crossing.
verses.before: Isn't it you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep; who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?
verses.after: Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, and made the sea’s depths a road for the redeemed to cross?
verses.tsw_comparator: Isn't it you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep; who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?

verses.rationale: Repeats Isaiah 35:10 wording to preserve intentional refrain.
verses.before: The ransomed of the LORD will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads: they will obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
verses.after: Those ransomed by the **LORD** will return and come to Zion with singing, everlasting joy upon their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them; sorrow and sighing will flee.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ransomed of the LORD will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads: they will obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic I and grass mortality comparison.
verses.before: I, even I, am the one who comforts you: who are you, that you are afraid of man who will die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass;
verses.after: “I, I am the one who comforts you. Who are you to fear a mortal who dies, a human being who becomes grass,
verses.tsw_comparator: I, even I, am the one who comforts you: who are you, that you are afraid of man who will die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass;

verses.rationale: Keeps creation-memory argument and repeated fury question.
verses.before: and have forgotten the LORD your Maker, who stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and fear continually all the day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he makes ready to destroy? and where is the fury of the oppressor?
verses.after: and forget the **LORD**, your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth? All day long you tremble before the oppressor’s fury as he prepares to destroy. But where is the oppressor’s fury now?
verses.tsw_comparator: and have forgotten the LORD your Maker, who stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and fear continually all the day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he makes ready to destroy? and where is the fury of the oppressor?

verses.rationale: Makes captive posture intelligible and preserves death-food promises.
verses.before: The captive exile will speedily be freed; and he will not die and go down into the pit, neither will his bread fail.
verses.after: The one bent down in chains will soon be freed; he will not die in the pit nor run short of bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: The captive exile will speedily be freed; and he will not die and go down into the pit, neither will his bread fail.

verses.rationale: Keeps first-to-third person divine name formula.
verses.before: For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea, so that the waves of it roar: the LORD of Hosts is his name.
verses.after: I am the **LORD** your God, who stirs the sea so its waves roar; the **LORD** of hosts is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea, so that the waves of it roar: the LORD of Hosts is his name.

verses.rationale: Preserves unusual planting heavens and unnamed singular recipient.
verses.before: I have put my words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of my hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and tell Zion, You are my people.
verses.after: I have put my words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of my hand, to plant the heavens, to found the earth, and to say to Zion, ‘You are my people.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I have put my words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of my hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and tell Zion, You are my people.

verses.rationale: Retains repetition, divine fury and intoxication metaphor.
verses.before: Awake, awake, stand up, Jerusalem, that have drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his wrath; you have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.
verses.after: Rouse yourself, rouse yourself! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who drank from the **LORD**’s hand the cup of his fury. You drank the cup that makes people stagger and drained its bowl.
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, awake, stand up, Jerusalem, that have drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his wrath; you have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.

verses.rationale: Preserves paired maternal history and abandoned present.
verses.before: There is none to guide her among all the sons whom she has gave birth; neither is there any who takes her by the hand among all the sons who she has brought up.
verses.after: Of all the children she bore, not one guides her; of all the children she raised, not one takes her hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is none to guide her among all the sons whom she has gave birth; neither is there any who takes her by the hand among all the sons who she has brought up.

verses.rationale: Keeps two paired calamities and first-person comfort question.
verses.before: These two things have happened to you. Who will bemoan you? Desolation and destruction, and the famine and the sword; how will I comfort you?
verses.after: These two calamities have met you— who will mourn with you?— devastation and destruction, famine and sword. How can I comfort you?
verses.tsw_comparator: These two things have happened to you. Who will bemoan you? Desolation and destruction, and the famine and the sword; how will I comfort you?

verses.rationale: Retains trapped-animal simile and explicit divine agency.
verses.before: Your sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as an antelope in a net; they are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
verses.after: Your children faint; they lie at every street corner like antelope caught in a net, filled with the **LORD**’s fury, your God’s rebuke.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as an antelope in a net; they are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps address feminine through context and distinguishes metaphorical intoxication.
verses.before: So hear now this, you afflicted, and drunken, but now with wine:
verses.after: So hear this, afflicted one, drunk, but not with wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore hear now this, you afflicted, and drunken, but now with wine:

verses.rationale: Preserves advocate role and cup transfer rather than erasing wrath.
verses.before: Thus says your Lord GOD, and your God who pleads the cause of his people, Look, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath; you will no more drink it again:
verses.after: This is what your Lord, the **LORD**, says, your God who argues his people’s case: “Look, I have taken from your hand the cup that makes people stagger, the bowl of my fury. You will never drink from it again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says your Lord GOD, and your God who pleads the cause of his people, Look, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath; you will no more drink it again:

verses.rationale: Retains humiliating physical domination and coming reversal.
verses.before: and I will put it into the hand of people who afflict you, who have said to your soul, Bow down, that we may go over; and you have laid your back as the ground, and as the street, to people who go over.
verses.after: I will put it into the hands of your tormentors, who told you, ‘Lie face down so we can walk over you.’ You made your back like the ground, like a street for them to walk on.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and I will put it into the hand of those who afflict you, who have said to your soul, Bow down, that we may go over; and you have laid your back as the ground, and as the street, to those who go over.

verses.rationale: Keeps ritual boundary language and clothing reversal.
verses.before: Awake, awake—put on your strength, O Zion! Put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city; for the uncircumcised and the unclean will enter you no more.
verses.after: Awake, awake! Put on your strength, Zion! Put on your splendid clothes, Jerusalem, holy city. The uncircumcised and the unclean will no longer enter you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, awake—put on your strength, O Zion! Put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city; for the uncircumcised and the unclean shall enter you no more.

verses.rationale: Follows read feminine free-yourself and preserves captive city imagery.
verses.before: Shake yourself from the dust; rise up, sit enthroned, O Jerusalem. Loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter Zion.
verses.after: Shake off the dust; rise and take your seat, Jerusalem. Free yourself from the bonds around your neck, captive Daughter Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shake yourself from the dust; rise up, sit enthroned, O Jerusalem. Loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter Zion.

verses.rationale: Preserves sale-redemption contrast and money image.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without money.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without silver.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money.

verses.rationale: Retains residence as foreigners and causeless oppression.
verses.before: For thus says the Lord GOD: My people went down at first into Egypt to reside there as resident aliens, and Assyria oppressed them for nothing.
verses.after: For this is what the Lord **GOD** says: “My people first went down to Egypt to live there as foreigners; then Assyria oppressed them for nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the Lord GOD: My people went down at first into Egypt to reside there as resident aliens, and Assyria oppressed them for nothing.

verses.rationale: Follows both read forms and leaves rulers’ howling unexplained rather than assigning praise or mockery.
verses.before: Now therefore, what am I doing here, says the LORD, seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers howl, says the LORD, and my name is continually despised all day long.
verses.after: Now what do I have here?” declares the **LORD**. “My people have been taken for nothing; their rulers howl,” declares the **LORD**, “and my name is despised continually, all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, what am I doing here, says the LORD, seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers howl, says the LORD, and my name is continually despised all day long.

verses.rationale: Keeps name knowledge linked to direct self-presence.
verses.before: So my people will know my name; therefore on that day they will know that I am the one who speaks: Here am I.
verses.after: So my people will know my name; on that day they will know that I am the one speaking. Here I am!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore my people shall know my name; therefore in that day they shall know that I am the one who speaks: Here am I.

verses.rationale: Preserves feet image and repeated announcements in natural clauses.
verses.before: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news, who announces peace, who brings good news of good things, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
verses.after: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
verses.tsw_comparator: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news, who announces peace, who brings good news of good things, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”

verses.rationale: Renders eye-to-eye eyewitness sense and preserves returning divine subject.
verses.before: The voice of your watchmen—they lift up their voice; together they sing for joy, for eye to eye they see the return of the LORD to Zion.
verses.after: Listen! Your watchmen raise their voices; together they sing for joy. With their own eyes they see the **LORD** returning to Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: The voice of your watchmen—they lift up their voice; together they sing for joy, for eye to eye they see the return of the LORD to Zion.

verses.rationale: Keeps ruins addressed as singers and comfort-redemption link.
verses.before: Break forth together into singing, you ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted his people, the LORD has redeemed Jerusalem.
verses.after: Break into joyful song together, ruins of Jerusalem! For the **LORD** has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Break forth together into singing, you ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted his people, the LORD has redeemed Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains physical arm and universal witnesses.
verses.before: The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
verses.after: The **LORD** has bared his holy arm before all the nations. All the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.

verses.rationale: Keeps unnamed city and cultic vessel-bearers without adding place name.
verses.before: Depart, depart—go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of it; be clean, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
verses.after: Leave, leave! Go out from there! Touch nothing unclean. Go out from her midst; purify yourselves, you who carry the **LORD**’s vessels.
verses.tsw_comparator: Depart, depart—go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of it; be clean, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast with hurried departure and both protective positions.
verses.before: For you will not go out in haste, and you will not go in flight; for the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
verses.after: You will not leave in haste or go out in flight, for the **LORD** goes before you, and Israel’s God guards your rear.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you shall not go out in haste, and you shall not go in flight; for the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.

verses.rationale: Retains wisdom-success ambiguity and threefold exaltation.
verses.before: Look—my servant will act wisely; he will be high and lifted up, and will be greatly exalted.
verses.after: Look, my servant will act wisely; he will rise, be lifted up, and be very high.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look—my servant shall act wisely; he shall be high and lifted up, and shall be greatly exalted.

verses.rationale: Keeps you-to-his shift and extreme disfigurement without normalizing pronouns.
verses.before: Just as many were appalled at him— so marred was his appearance beyond mortals, and his form beyond the children of humanity—
verses.after: Just as many were appalled at you— so disfigured was his appearance beyond that of a man, his form beyond that of human beings—
verses.tsw_comparator: Just as many were appalled at him— so marred was his appearance beyond mortals, and his form beyond the children of humanity—

verses.rationale: Follows pinned sprinkle; notes debated startle alternative rather than silently substituting it.
verses.before: so he will startle many nations; kings will shut their mouths because of him. For what had not been told them they will see, and what they had not heard they will understand.
verses.after: so he will sprinkle many nations. Kings will shut their mouths because of him, for they will see what they had not been told and understand what they had not heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: so he shall startle many nations; kings shall shut their mouths because of him. For that which had not been told them they shall see, and that which they had not heard they shall understand.

verses.rationale: Preserves report-as-heard and unidentified communal voice.
verses.before: Who has trusted what we have heard? And to whom has the LORD’s arm been revealed?
verses.after: Who has believed what we have heard? To whom has the **LORD**’s arm been revealed?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has trusted what we have heard? And to whom has the LORD’s arm been revealed?

verses.rationale: Retains before-him ambiguity and unattractive plant image.
verses.before: For he grew up before the LORD like a young plant, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no form or majesty that we should look at him, and no appearance that we should desire him.
verses.after: He grew before him like a tender shoot, like a root from dry ground. He had no fine form or splendor to draw our gaze, no appearance to make us desire him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he grew up before the LORD like a young plant, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no form or majesty that we should look at him, and no appearance that we should desire him.

verses.rationale: Preserves physical sickness and repeated despised without doctrinal paraphrase.
verses.before: He was despised and rejected by mortals— a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief; and like one from whom people hide their faces, he was despised, and we held him as nothing.
verses.after: Despised and abandoned by people, a man of pains, acquainted with sickness, like someone from whom faces turn away— he was despised, and we gave him no regard.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was despised and rejected by mortals— a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief; and like one from whom people hide their faces, he was despised, and we held him as nothing.

verses.rationale: Keeps reversal of communal assessment and physical afflictions.
verses.before: Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we held him as stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
verses.after: Yet it was our sicknesses he carried, our pains he bore. We thought him stricken, struck by God and afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we held him as stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.

verses.rationale: Retains causal prepositions, peace and singular wound without prescribing a theory.
verses.before: But he was pierced because of our rebellions, crushed because of our iniquities; the discipline that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.
verses.after: But he was pierced because of our rebellions, crushed because of our offenses. The discipline that brought us peace was upon him; by his wound we were healed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he was pierced because of our rebellions, crushed because of our iniquities; the discipline that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.

verses.rationale: Keeps all-us frame and divine causative encounter.
verses.before: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—each to their own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
verses.after: All of us wandered like sheep; each of us turned to our own way. The **LORD** made the guilt of us all fall upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—each to their own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated silence and female ewe specifically.
verses.before: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
verses.after: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb led to slaughter, like a ewe silent before her shearers, he did not open his mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.

verses.rationale: Keeps ambiguous judicial removal, generation question and my-people shift; plural suffix alternative noted.
verses.before: By oppression and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who considered that he was cut off from the land of the living, struck because of the rebellion of my people?
verses.after: Through oppression and judgment he was taken away. Who considered his generation? For he was cut off from the land of the living; because of my people’s rebellion, the blow fell on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: By oppression and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who considered that he was cut off from the land of the living, struck because of the rebellion of my people?

verses.rationale: Retains rich singular and undeserved violence; notes unusual plural deaths form.
verses.before: They made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.
verses.after: They assigned his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death, though he had done no violence and no deceit was in his mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves disturbing divine agency, second-person possible subject and conditional offering clause.
verses.before: Yet it pleased the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief. When you make his life an offering for guilt, he will see offspring; he will prolong his days; the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
verses.after: Yet the **LORD** desired to crush him and make him sick. If you make his life a reparation offering, he will see offspring and prolong his days, and the **LORD**’s purpose will prosper in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet it pleased the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief. When you make his life an offering for guilt, he shall see offspring; he shall prolong his days; the will of the LORD shall prosper in his hand.

verses.rationale: Does not insert light absent from pinned text; preserves knowledge ambiguity and divine my-servant voice.
verses.before: Out of the anguish of his life he will see and be satisfied; by his knowledge my righteous servant will make many righteous, and he will bear their iniquities.
verses.after: After his life’s anguish he will see and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will bring righteousness to many, and he will bear their offenses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Out of the anguish of his life he shall see and be satisfied; by his knowledge my righteous servant shall make many righteous, and he shall bear their iniquities.

verses.rationale: Keeps victorious plunder alongside death and repeated rebels, without naming later identification.
verses.before: So I will allot him a portion with the many, and he will divide the spoil with the strong, because he poured out his life to death and was numbered with the rebels; yet he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the rebels.
verses.after: So I will give him a share among the many, and he will divide plunder with the strong, because he poured out his life to death and was counted among rebels. Yet he carried the sin of many and interceded for rebels.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will allot him a portion with the many, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong, because he poured out his life to death and was numbered with the rebels; yet he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the rebels.

verses.rationale: Preserves city-as-mother metaphor and comparison without general promise about infertility.
verses.before: Sing, barren, you who did not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, you who did not labor with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, says the LORD.
verses.after: “Sing, barren woman who has never given birth! Break into song and shout, you who have never labored in childbirth! For the desolate woman has more children than the married woman,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing, barren, you who did not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, you who did not labor with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps practical tent expansion sequence.
verses.before: Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of your habitations; do not spare: lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes.
verses.after: “Enlarge the space for your tent; let them stretch out your dwelling’s curtains. Do not hold back! Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of your habitations; do not spare: lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes.

verses.rationale: Retains nations dispossession claim rather than replacing with harmless influence.
verses.before: For you will spread aboard on the right hand and on the left; and your seed will possess the nations, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited.
verses.after: You will spread out to right and left. Your offspring will take possession of nations and settle deserted cities.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you will spread aboard on the right hand and on the left; and your seed will possess the nations, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited.

verses.rationale: Maintains parallel assurances and distinct youth-widowhood history.
verses.before: Don't be afraid; for you will not be ashamed: neither be confounded; for you will not be disappointed: for you will forget the shame of your youth; and the reproach of your widowhood will you remember no more.
verses.after: Do not fear: you will not be ashamed. Do not be humiliated: you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth and no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Don't be afraid; for you will not be ashamed: neither be confounded; for you will not be disappointed: for you will forget the shame of your youth; and the reproach of your widowhood will you remember no more.

verses.rationale: Keeps marriage metaphor and accumulating titles.
verses.before: For your Maker is your husband; the LORD of Hosts is his name: and the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; the God of the entire earth will he be called.
verses.after: For your Maker is your husband— the **LORD** of hosts is his name. Your Redeemer is Israel’s Holy One; he is called the God of all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your Maker is your husband; the LORD of Hosts is his name: and the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; the God of the whole earth will he be called.

verses.rationale: Retains distress of abandoned wife and divine recall.
verses.before: For the LORD has called you as a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit, even a wife of youth, when she is cast off, says your God.
verses.after: For the **LORD** has called you back like a wife abandoned and grieved in spirit, a wife married in youth and then rejected, says your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has called you as a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit, even a wife of youth, when she is cast off, says your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps first-person admission of abandonment.
verses.before: For a small moment have I forsaken you; but with great mercies will I gather you.
verses.after: “For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
