verses.tsw_comparator: For a small moment have I forsaken you; but with great mercies will I gather you.

verses.rationale: Preserves moment-everlasting contrast and hesed vocabulary.
verses.before: In overflowing wrath I hid my face from you for a moment; but with everlasting steadfast love will I have mercy on you, says the LORD your Redeemer.
verses.after: In a surge of anger I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting faithful love I will have compassion on you,” says your Redeemer, the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: In overflowing wrath I hid my face from you for a moment; but with everlasting steadfast love will I have mercy on you, says the LORD your Redeemer.

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned waters of Noah, not variant days, and explicit oath analogy.
verses.before: For this is as the waters of Noah to me; for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah will no more go over the earth, so have I sworn that I will not be angry with you, nor rebuke you.
verses.after: “This is like Noah’s waters to me. As I swore that Noah’s waters would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn not to be angry with you or rebuke you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is as the waters of Noah to me; for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah will no more go over the earth, so have I sworn that I will not be angry with you, nor rebuke you.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated move/shake vocabulary tying landscape to covenant.
verses.before: For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.
verses.after: Mountains may move away and hills may shake, but my faithful love will not move away from you, and my covenant of peace will not shake,” says the **LORD**, who has compassion on you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

verses.rationale: Retains addressed distressed city and precious construction; mineral terms approximate.
verses.before: You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, look, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires.
verses.after: “Afflicted one, storm-tossed and uncomforted, look, I will set your stones in dark mortar and lay your foundations with sapphires.
verses.tsw_comparator: You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, look, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires.

verses.rationale: Preserves architectural distinctions without overclaiming mineral identification.
verses.before: I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
verses.after: I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of sparkling stones, and all your boundary walls of precious stones.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated children rather than substituting builders.
verses.before: All your children will be taught of the LORD; and great will be the peace of your children.
verses.after: All your children will be taught by the **LORD**, and great will be your children’s peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: All your children will be taught of the LORD; and great will be the peace of your children.

verses.rationale: Retains imperative distancing within assurance.
verses.before: In righteousness will you be established: you will be far from oppression, for you will not be afraid; and from terror, for it will not come near you.
verses.after: You will be established in righteousness. Keep far from oppression, for you need not fear, and from terror, for it will not come near you.
verses.tsw_comparator: In righteousness will you be established: you will be far from oppression, for you will not be afraid; and from terror, for it will not come near you.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast between hostile gathering and divine agency.
verses.before: Look, they may gather together, but not by me: whoever will gather together against you will fall because of you.
verses.after: If anyone stirs up conflict, it is not from me. Whoever stirs up conflict with you will fall because of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, they may gather together, but not by me: whoever will gather together against you will fall because of you.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated creator claim including destructive agent.
verses.before: Look, I have created the smith who blows the fire of coals, and brings forth a weapon for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.
verses.after: Look, I myself created the smith who blows on the charcoal fire and produces a weapon for its work. I myself created the destroyer to ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I have created the smith who blows the fire of coals, and brings forth a weapon for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.

verses.rationale: Links weapon and courtroom assurances to plural servants, not universal individual immunity.
verses.before: No weapon that is formed against you will prosper; and every tongue that will rise against you in judgment you will condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness which is of me, says the LORD.
verses.after: No weapon formed against you will succeed, and you will condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the inheritance of the **LORD**’s servants; their vindication comes from me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: No weapon that is formed against you will prosper; and every tongue that will rise against you in judgment you will condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness which is of me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps paradoxical buying without payment and specific drinks.
verses.before: Ho! Everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you who have no money, come, buy and eat. Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
verses.after: “Come, all who thirst, come to the water! You who have no silver, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without silver, without a price.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ho! Everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you who have no money, come, buy and eat. Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

verses.rationale: Retains weighing money and repeated listening as food imagery.
verses.before: Why do you spend money for what is not bread? and your labor for what does not satisfy? listen diligently to me, and eat you what is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
verses.after: Why weigh out silver for what is not bread, and spend your labor on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me and eat what is good; delight yourselves in rich food.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you spend money for that which is not bread? and your labor for that which does not satisfy? listen diligently to me, and eat you that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.

verses.rationale: Preserves Davidic covenant connection and plural faithful mercies.
verses.before: Turn your ear, and come to me; hear, and your soul will live: and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
verses.after: Incline your ears and come to me; listen, so you may live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful acts of love promised to David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn your ear, and come to me; hear, and your soul will live: and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.

verses.rationale: Retains him referring back to David and repeated peoples.
verses.before: Look, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.
verses.after: Look, I made him a witness to peoples, a leader and commander of peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keeps shift to unnamed singular you rather than imposing an identity.
verses.before: Look, you will call a nation that you do not know; and a nation that did not know you will run to you, because of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has glorified you.
verses.after: Look, you will call a nation you do not know, and a nation that does not know you will run to you, because of the **LORD** your God, Israel’s Holy One, who has glorified you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you will call a nation that you do not know; and a nation that did not know you will run to you, because of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has glorified you.

verses.rationale: Retains opportunity framed by while.
verses.before: Seek you the LORD while he may be found; call you on him while he is near:
verses.after: Seek the **LORD** while he may be found; call to him while he is near.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seek you the LORD while he may be found; call you on him while he is near:

verses.rationale: Links ways and thoughts to following divine comparison.
verses.before: let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; and let him return to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.
verses.after: Let the wicked abandon their way and the wrongdoer their thoughts. Let them return to the **LORD**, who will have compassion, to our God, who abundantly forgives.
verses.tsw_comparator: let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; and let him return to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.

verses.rationale: Preserves inverse order of thoughts and ways.
verses.before: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the LORD.
verses.after: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains spatial analogy rather than generic unknowability.
verses.before: For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
verses.after: “As the heavens are higher than the earth, so my ways are higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.

verses.rationale: Preserves snow, growth stages and two recipients.
verses.before: For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and does not return there, but waters the earth, and makes it bring forth and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater;
verses.after: As rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return there without watering the earth, making it bear and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
verses.tsw_comparator: For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and does not return there, but waters the earth, and makes it bring forth and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater;

verses.rationale: Keeps sent word as effective agent.
verses.before: so will my word be that goes forth out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
verses.after: so will my word be that goes out from my mouth: it will not return to me empty. It will accomplish what I desire and succeed in what I sent it to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: so will my word be that goes forth out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.

verses.rationale: Preserves creation’s bodily celebration and guided departure.
verses.before: For you will go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills will break forth before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
verses.after: For you will go out with joy and be led in peace. Mountains and hills will break into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you will go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills will break forth before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired plant replacements and enduring sign.
verses.before: Instead of the thorn will come up the fir tree; and instead of the brier will come up the myrtle tree: and it will be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.
verses.after: Instead of thornbushes, cypress will grow; instead of nettles, myrtle will grow. This will bring the **LORD** renown, an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Instead of the thorn will come up the fir tree; and instead of the brier will come up the myrtle tree: and it will be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

verses.rationale: Keeps human righteousness and divine righteousness linked.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Keep justice and practice righteousness, for my salvation is near to come and my righteousness is about to be revealed.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Keep justice and do righteousness, for my salvation is near to coming and my righteousness to being revealed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Keep justice and practice righteousness, for my salvation is near to come and my righteousness is about to be revealed.

verses.rationale: Preserves Sabbath and conduct together; generic human terms inclusive.
verses.before: Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast; who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil.
verses.after: Happy is the person who does this, the human being who holds firmly to it, keeping the Sabbath from profanation and their hand from doing any evil.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast; who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit outsider categories and infertility image.
verses.before: Neither let the foreigner, who has joined himself to the LORD, speak, saying, the LORD will surely separate me from his people; neither let the eunuch say, Look, I am a dry tree.
verses.after: Let no foreigner who has joined the **LORD** say, “The **LORD** will surely separate me from his people.” And let no eunuch say, “Look, I am a dry tree.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Neither let the foreigner, who has joined himself to the LORD, speak, saying, the LORD will surely separate me from his people; neither let the eunuch say, Look, I am a dry tree.

verses.rationale: Keeps named recipients and three conditions.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and hold fast my covenant:
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose what pleases me and hold firmly to my covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and hold fast my covenant:

verses.rationale: Preserves sons-daughters comparison and cut-off wordplay.
verses.before: To them will I give in my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, that will not be cut off.
verses.after: I will give within my house and my walls a memorial and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give each one an everlasting name that will not be cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: To them will I give in my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, that will not be cut off.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated LORD and foreigners’ positive service.
verses.before: Also the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD, to minister to him, and to love the name of the LORD, to be his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and holds fast my covenant;
verses.after: And the foreigners who join the **LORD** to serve him, to love the **LORD**’s name and become his servants, all who keep the Sabbath from profanation and hold firmly to my covenant—
verses.tsw_comparator: Also the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD, to minister to him, and to love the name of the LORD, to be his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and holds fast my covenant;

verses.rationale: Preserves sacrificial inclusion alongside universal prayer.
verses.before: these I will bring to my holy mountain and make joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
verses.after: I will bring them to my holy mountain and give them joy in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”
verses.tsw_comparator: these I will bring to my holy mountain and make joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.

verses.rationale: Keeps Israel and additional gathered groups without replacing either.
verses.before: The Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, says, Yet will I gather others to him, besides his own who are gathered.
verses.after: The Lord **GOD**, who gathers Israel’s outcasts, declares, “I will gather still others to him, besides those already gathered.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, says, Yet will I gather others to him, besides his own who are gathered.

verses.rationale: Preserves abrupt threatening summons after inclusion.
verses.before: All you animals of the field, come to devour, yes, all you animals in the forest.
verses.after: All you beasts of the field, come and eat, all you beasts in the forest!
verses.tsw_comparator: All you animals of the field, come to devour, yes, all you animals in the forest.

verses.rationale: Follows read his-watchmen and keeps dog metaphor.
verses.before: His watchmen are blind, they are all without knowledge; they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark; dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.
verses.after: His watchmen are blind; all of them lack knowledge. They are all silent dogs, unable to bark, dreaming, lying down, loving sleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: His watchmen are blind, they are all without knowledge; they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark; dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.

verses.rationale: Keeps combined dogs-shepherds imagery and universal indictment.
verses.before: Yes, the dogs are greedy, they can never have enough; and these are shepherds who cannot understand: they have all turned to their own way, each person to his gain, from every quarter.
verses.after: These dogs have fierce appetites; they never know satisfaction. They are shepherds without understanding. All have turned to their own way, each seeking gain, every last one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, the dogs are greedy, they can never have enough; and these are shepherds who cannot understand: they have all turned to their own way, each one to his gain, from every quarter.

verses.rationale: Marks complacent leaders’ quoted voice and escalating boast.
verses.before: Come you, say they, I will get wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and tomorrow will be as this day, a day great beyond measure.
verses.after: “Come, let me get wine; let us fill ourselves with strong drink! Tomorrow will be like today, only much, much better.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Come you, say they, I will get wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and tomorrow will be as this day, a day great beyond measure.

verses.rationale: Preserves neglected deaths and ambiguous removal from/because of evil.
verses.before: The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart; faithful people are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous are taken away from the presence of evil.
verses.after: The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart. People of faithful love are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous are taken away from evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart; faithful people are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous are taken away from the presence of evil.

verses.rationale: Keeps death-rest image without expanding afterlife claims.
verses.before: He enters into peace; they rest in their beds, each person who walks in his uprightness.
verses.after: They enter peace; those who walk uprightly rest upon their beds.
verses.tsw_comparator: He enters into peace; they rest in their beds, each one who walks in his uprightness.

verses.rationale: Retains accusatory parentage and sexual language.
verses.before: But draw near here, you sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the prostitute.
verses.after: “But you, come here, children of a sorceress, offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute!
verses.tsw_comparator: But draw near here, you sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the prostitute.

verses.rationale: Preserves taunting gestures and repeated offspring accusation.
verses.before: Against whom do you sport yourselves? against whom make you a wide mouth, and put out the tongue? Aren't you children of disobedience, a seed of falsehood,
verses.after: Whom are you mocking? At whom do you open your mouths and stick out your tongues? Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of falsehood,
verses.tsw_comparator: Against whom do you sport yourselves? against whom make you a wide mouth, and put out the tongue? Aren't you children of disobedience, a seed of falsehood,

verses.rationale: Keeps child killing explicit, with ritual landscape.
verses.before: you who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every green tree; who kill the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?
verses.after: you who burn with passion among the oaks, under every green tree, who slaughter children in the ravines, beneath the clefts of the rocks?
verses.tsw_comparator: you who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every green tree; who kill the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?

verses.rationale: Preserves portion-stone wordplay as far as English permits and double they.
verses.before: Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion; they, they are your lot; even to them have you poured a drink offering, you have offered an offering. Will I be appeased for these things?
verses.after: Your portion is among the ravine’s smooth stones; they, they are your lot. To them you poured drink offerings and brought grain offerings. Should I relent over these things?
verses.tsw_comparator: Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion; they, they are your lot; even to them have you poured a drink offering, you have offered an offering. Will I be appeased for these things?

verses.rationale: Keeps bed-sacrifice juxtaposition.
verses.before: On a high and lofty mountain have you set your bed; there also you went up to offer sacrifice.
verses.after: On a high and lofty mountain you placed your bed; there too you went up to offer sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: On a high and lofty mountain have you set your bed; there also you went up to offer sacrifice.

verses.rationale: Retains sexualized covenant infidelity; literal hand euphemism documented.
verses.before: Behind the doors and the posts have you set up your memorial: for you have uncovered yourself to another than me, and are gone up; you have enlarged your bed, and made you a covenant with them: you loved their bed where you saw it.
verses.after: Behind the door and doorpost you placed your memorial. Leaving me, you uncovered yourself and climbed up; you widened your bed and made a pact with them. You loved their bed; you gazed on their nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behind the doors and the posts have you set up your memorial: for you have uncovered yourself to another than me, and are gone up; you have enlarged your bed, and made you a covenant with them: you loved their bed where you saw it.

verses.rationale: Keeps king reading rather than silently substituting Molek.
verses.before: You went to the king with oil, and did increase your perfumes, and did send your ambassadors far off, and did debase yourself even to Sheol.
verses.after: You went to the king with oil and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your envoys far away and sank as low as Sheol.
verses.tsw_comparator: You went to the king with oil, and did increase your perfumes, and did send your ambassadors far off, and did debase yourself even to Sheol.

verses.rationale: Retains persistence in condemned activity and idiomatic life-of-hand.
verses.before: You were wearied with the length of your way; yet you did not say, It is in vain: you found a reviving of your strength; so you were not faint.
verses.after: Your long journey wearied you, but you did not say, ‘It is hopeless.’ You found fresh strength, so you did not grow faint.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were wearied with the length of your way; yet you did not say, It is in vain: you found a reviving of your strength; therefore you were not faint.

verses.rationale: Preserves direct questions and divine silence explanation.
verses.before: Of whom have you been afraid and in fear, that you lie, and have not remembered me, nor laid it to your heart? Haven't I held my peace even of long time, and you do not fear me?
verses.after: Whom did you dread and fear that you lied, forgot me and gave me no thought? Was it because I kept silent so long that you did not fear me?
verses.tsw_comparator: Of whom have you been afraid and in fear, that you lie, and have not remembered me, nor laid it to your heart? Haven't I held my peace even of long time, and you do not fear me?

verses.rationale: Keeps ironic righteousness rather than replacing accusation with a different noun.
verses.before: I will declare your righteousness; and as for your works, they will not profit you.
verses.after: I will expose your righteousness and your deeds; they will not help you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will declare your righteousness; and as for your works, they will not profit you.

verses.rationale: Leaves collection’s idol referent contextual; preserves wind-breath contrast.
verses.before: When you cry, let people who you have gathered deliver you; but the wind will take them, a breath will carry them all away: but the one who takes refuge in me will possess the land, and will inherit my holy mountain.
verses.after: When you cry out, let your collection rescue you! A wind will carry them all away; a breath will take them. But whoever takes refuge in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When you cry, let those who you have gathered deliver you; but the wind will take them, a breath will carry them all away: but the one who takes refuge in me will possess the land, and will inherit my holy mountain.

verses.rationale: Keeps unnamed he and repeated road-building command.
verses.before: He will say, Cast up, cast up, prepare the way, take up the stumbling-block out of the way of my people.
verses.after: And he will say, “Build up, build up! Clear the way! Remove every obstacle from my people’s road.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He will say, Cast up, cast up, prepare the way, take up the stumbling-block out of the way of my people.

verses.rationale: Preserves transcendence and presence with afflicted, repeated revive.
verses.before: For thus says the high and exalted One, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with the crushed and lowly in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the crushed.
verses.after: For this is what the high and exalted one says, who dwells forever, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the crushed and lowly in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the crushed.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the high and exalted One, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with the crushed and lowly in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the crushed.

verses.rationale: Keeps finite creature’s vulnerability as stated reason.
verses.before: For I will not contend forever, neither will I be always angry; for the spirit would faint before me, and the souls who I have made.
verses.after: I will not contend forever nor remain angry always, for the spirit would faint before me, the living breath of those I made.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will not contend forever, neither will I be always angry; for the spirit would faint before me, and the souls who I have made.

verses.rationale: Retains divine striking and singular corporate subject.
verses.before: For the iniquity of his covetousness was I angry, and struck him; I hid my face and was angry; and he went on backsliding in the way of his heart.
verses.after: His sinful greed angered me, and I struck him; I hid myself in anger. Yet he turned away and followed his own heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the iniquity of his covetousness was I angry, and struck him; I hid my face and was angry; and he went on backsliding in the way of his heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves healing despite observed ways and mourners included.
verses.before: I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
verses.after: I have seen his ways, but I will heal him; I will lead him and restore comfort to him and to those who mourn for him,
verses.tsw_comparator: I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.

verses.rationale: Keeps fruit-of-lips image and doubled peace.
verses.before: I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to the one who is far off and to the one who is near, says the LORD; and I will heal him.
verses.after: creating the fruit of lips. Peace, peace, to the far and the near,” says the **LORD**, “and I will heal him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to the one who is far off and to the one who is near, says the LORD; and I will heal him.

verses.rationale: Retains literal turbulent sea image.
verses.before: But the wicked are like the troubled sea; for it cannot rest, and its waters cast up mire and dirt.
verses.after: But the wicked are like a restless sea that cannot be still, whose waters toss up mud and mire.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the wicked are like the troubled sea; for it cannot rest, and its waters cast up mire and dirt.

verses.rationale: Echoes 48:22 while preserving different divine designation.
verses.before: There is no peace, says my God, to the wicked.
verses.after: “There is no peace for the wicked,” says my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no peace, says my God, to the wicked.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily shouting and shofar sound.
verses.before: Cry aloud, do not spare, lift up your voice like a trumpet, and declare to my people their disobedience, and to the house of Jacob their sins.
verses.after: “Cry out with a full throat; do not hold back! Raise your voice like a ram’s horn. Tell my people their rebellion, the house of Jacob their sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cry aloud, do not spare, lift up your voice like a trumpet, and declare to my people their disobedience, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves as-though exposure of apparent devotion.
verses.before: Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways: as a nation that did righteousness, and did not forsake the ordinance of their God, they ask of me righteous judgments; they delight to draw near to God.
verses.after: Day after day they seek me and delight in knowing my ways, as though they were a nation that did righteousness and had not abandoned its God’s justice. They ask me for righteous judgments and delight in drawing near to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways: as a nation that did righteousness, and did not forsake the ordinance of their God, they ask of me righteous judgments; they delight to draw near to God.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes people’s complaint from response and keeps labor exploitation explicit.
verses.before: Why have we fasted, say they, and you do not see? why have we afflicted our soul, and you take no knowledge? Look, in the day of your fast you find your own pleasure, and exact all your labors.
verses.after: ‘Why have we fasted, and you have not seen? Why humbled ourselves, and you have not noticed?’ Look, on your fast day you pursue your own interests and drive all your workers hard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why have we fasted, say they, and you do not see? why have we afflicted our soul, and you take no knowledge? Look, in the day of your fast you find your own pleasure, and exact all your labors.

verses.rationale: Preserves physical violence rather than general disagreement.
verses.before: Look, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wickedness: you do not fast this day so as to make your voice to be heard on high.
verses.after: Look, you fast only to quarrel and fight and strike with a wicked fist. Fasting as you do today will not make your voice heard on high.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wickedness: you do not fast this day so as to make your voice to be heard on high.

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical questions and tangible penitential acts.
verses.before: Is such the fast that I have chosen? the day for a man to afflict his soul? Is it to bow down his head as a rush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?
verses.after: Is this the fast I choose, a day for people to humble themselves? Is it bowing the head like a reed and spreading sackcloth and ashes? Do you call this a fast, a day acceptable to the **LORD**?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is such the fast that I have chosen? the day for a man to afflict his soul? Is it to bow down his head as a rush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?

verses.rationale: Retains bondage-release sequence and repeated every-yoke breadth.
verses.before: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness, undo the straps of the yoke, let the oppressed go free, and break every yoke?
verses.after: Is not this the fast I choose: to loosen the bonds of wickedness, undo the straps of the yoke, release the oppressed, and break every yoke?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness, undo the straps of the yoke, let the oppressed go free, and break every yoke?

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete aid and kin obligation rather than generic kindness.
verses.before: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, bring the homeless poor into your house, when you see the naked, cover them, and not hide yourself from your own flesh?
verses.after: Is it not sharing your bread with the hungry, bringing the homeless poor into your house, clothing the naked when you see them, and not hiding from your own flesh and blood?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, bring the homeless poor into your house, when you see the naked, cover them, and not hide yourself from your own flesh?

verses.rationale: Preserves healing-growth image and front-rear protection.
verses.before: Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly; your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will guard your rear.
verses.after: Then your light will break out like dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly. Your righteousness will go before you; the **LORD**’s glory will guard your rear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly; your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will guard your rear.

verses.rationale: Keeps promised response followed by continuing conditions.
verses.before: Then will you call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry, and he will say, Here I am. If you take away from the midst of you the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking wickedly;
verses.after: Then you will call, and the **LORD** will answer; you will cry for help, and he will say, ‘Here I am.’ If you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing finger and harmful speech,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then will you call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry, and he will say, Here I am. If you take away from the midst of you the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking wickedly;

verses.rationale: Follows pinned self/life rather than substituting bread, with explanatory idiom.
verses.before: and if you draw out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then will your light rise in darkness, and your obscurity be as the noonday;
verses.after: if you pour yourself out for the hungry and satisfy the afflicted, your light will rise in darkness, and your gloom will be like noon.
verses.tsw_comparator: and if you draw out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then will your light rise in darkness, and your obscurity be as the noonday;

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily bones and reliable-water imagery.
verses.before: and the LORD will guide you continually, and satisfy your soul in dry places, and make strong your bones; and you will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail.
verses.after: The **LORD** will guide you continually, satisfy you in parched places and strengthen your bones. You will be like a watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the LORD will guide you continually, and satisfy your soul in dry places, and make strong your bones; and you will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail.

verses.rationale: Preserves civic restoration and two descriptive names.
verses.before: People who will be of you will build the old waste places; you will raise up the foundations of many generations; and you will be called The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.
verses.after: Your people will rebuild ancient ruins; you will raise foundations laid generations ago. You will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of Streets to Live In.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who will be of you will build the old waste places; you will raise up the foundations of many generations; and you will be called The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated own-interests language; final speech idiom interpretation noted.
verses.before: If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day; and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the LORD honorable; and will honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words:
verses.after: If you restrain your foot on the Sabbath from pursuing your own interests on my holy day, if you call the Sabbath a delight and the **LORD**’s holy day honorable, if you honor it by not following your own ways, pursuing your own interests or talking business,
verses.tsw_comparator: If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day; and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the LORD honorable; and will honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words:

verses.rationale: Keeps delight echo and ancestral land inheritance.
verses.before: then will you delight yourself in the LORD; and I will make you to ride on the high places of the earth; and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father: for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it.
verses.after: then you will delight in the **LORD**. I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father.” For the **LORD**’s mouth has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: then will you delight yourself in the LORD; and I will make you to ride on the high places of the earth; and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father: for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it.

verses.rationale: Links bodily images to 50:2 without adding inability claim.
verses.before: Look, the LORD’s hand is not too short to save, nor the LORD’s ear too heavy to hear.
verses.after: Look, the **LORD**’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the LORD’s hand is not too short to save, nor the LORD’s ear too heavy to hear.

verses.rationale: Preserves moral cause and hidden-face image.
verses.before: but your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he will not hear.
verses.after: Rather, your offenses have separated you from your God; your sins have hidden his face from you, so he does not hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: but your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he will not hear.

verses.rationale: Keeps four body parts and bloodguilt specificity.
verses.before: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, your tongue mutters wickedness.
verses.after: Your palms are stained with blood, your fingers with guilt. Your lips speak lies; your tongue mutters injustice.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, your tongue mutters wickedness.

verses.rationale: Preserves courtroom setting and conception metaphor.
verses.before: None sues in righteousness, and none pleads in truth: they trust in vanity, and speak lies; they conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity.
verses.after: No one brings a case justly; no one pleads honestly. They trust in emptiness and speak falsehood, conceive trouble and give birth to wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: None sues in righteousness, and none pleads in truth: they trust in vanity, and speak lies; they conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired dangerous and useless products.
verses.before: They hatch adders' eggs, and weave the spider's web: the one who eats of their eggs dies; and what is crushed breaks out into a viper.
verses.after: They hatch vipers’ eggs and weave spiders’ webs. Whoever eats their eggs dies; when one is crushed, a snake hatches.
verses.tsw_comparator: They hatch adders' eggs, and weave the spider's web: the one who eats of their eggs dies; and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper.

verses.rationale: Retains work repetition and failed clothing image.
verses.before: Their webs will not become garments, neither will they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.
verses.after: Their webs cannot become clothing; they cannot cover themselves with what they make. Their works are works of wrongdoing; acts of violence are in their hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their webs will not become garments, neither will they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps innocent victims and repeated wrongdoing from previous verse.
verses.before: Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; desolation and destruction are in their paths.
verses.after: Their feet run to evil; they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of wrongdoing; devastation and destruction mark their highways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; desolation and destruction are in their paths.

verses.rationale: Preserves peace frame and path metaphor throughout.
verses.before: The way of peace they do not know; and there is no justice in their goings: they have made them crooked paths; whoever goes in it does not know peace.
verses.after: They do not know the way of peace; there is no justice in their tracks. They have made their paths crooked; no one walking them knows peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: The way of peace they do not know; and there is no justice in their goings: they have made them crooked paths; whoever goes in it does not know peace.

verses.rationale: Retains shift from they to confessing we.
verses.before: So is justice far from us, neither does righteousness overtake us: we look for light, but, look, darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity.
verses.after: So justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We wait for light, but there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore is justice far from us, neither does righteousness overtake us: we look for light, but, look, darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult vigorous/dead contrast; lexical uncertainty noted.
verses.before: We grope for the wall like the blind; yes, we grope as people who have no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the twilight; among people who are lusty we are as dead men.
verses.after: We grope along a wall like the blind, groping like people without eyes. We stumble at noon as at dusk; among the vigorous we are like the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: We grope for the wall like the blind; yes, we grope as those who have no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the twilight; among those who are lusty we are as dead men.

verses.rationale: Keeps two animal sounds and repeated moaning.
verses.before: We roar all like bears, and moan sore like doves: we look for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us.
verses.after: We all growl like bears and moan and moan like doves. We wait for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far from us.
verses.tsw_comparator: We roar all like bears, and moan sore like doves: we look for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us.

verses.rationale: Preserves courtroom testimony and self-knowledge.
verses.before: For our transgressions are multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and as for our iniquities, we know them:
verses.after: For our rebellions before you are many, and our sins testify against us. Our rebellions are with us; we know our offenses:
verses.tsw_comparator: For our transgressions are multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and as for our iniquities, we know them:

verses.rationale: Keeps confession’s concrete verbal and relational failures.
verses.before: transgressing and denying the LORD, and turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.
verses.after: rebelling and denying the **LORD**, turning back from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering lying words from the heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: transgressing and denying the LORD, and turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.

verses.rationale: Retains personified virtues excluded from civic space.
verses.before: Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands afar off; for truth is fallen in the street, and uprightness cannot enter.
verses.after: Justice is driven backward, and righteousness stands far away. Truth stumbles in the public square, and honesty cannot enter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands afar off; for truth is fallen in the street, and uprightness cannot enter.

verses.rationale: Keeps risk borne by those rejecting evil and divine observation.
verses.before: Yes, truth is lacking; and the one who departs from evil makes himself a prey. the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.
verses.after: Truth is missing, and whoever turns from evil becomes prey. The **LORD** saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, truth is lacking; and the one who departs from evil makes himself a prey. the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine astonishment and his own saving arm.
verses.before: He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his own arm brought salvation to him; and his righteousness, it upheld him.
verses.after: He saw that there was no one and was appalled that no one intervened. So his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness sustained him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his own arm brought salvation to him; and his righteousness, it upheld him.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four items of divine warrior clothing.
verses.before: He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head; and he put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle.
verses.after: He put on righteousness as a breastplate and a helmet of salvation on his head. He dressed in garments of vengeance and wrapped himself in zeal like a cloak.
verses.tsw_comparator: He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head; and he put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle.

verses.rationale: Preserves repetitive repayment and geographic reach.
verses.before: According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay, wrath to his adversaries, recompense to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompense.
verses.after: He will repay according to their deeds: fury to his adversaries, repayment to his enemies; to the coastlands he will repay what is due.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay, wrath to his adversaries, recompense to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompense.

verses.rationale: Chooses divine rushing-stream syntax; enemy-and-banner alternative documented.
verses.before: So will they fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come as a rushing stream, which the breath of the LORD drives.
verses.after: From the west they will fear the **LORD**’s name, and from the sunrise his glory. For he will come like a rushing river driven by the **LORD**’s wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: So will they fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come as a rushing stream, which the breath of the LORD drives.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned to-Zion and repentant recipients without importing another textual form.
verses.before: A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression, says the LORD.
verses.after: “A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from rebellion,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains three generations and shift from them to singular you.
verses.before: As for me, this is my covenant with them, says the LORD: my Spirit who is on you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, will not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your seed, nor out of the mouth of your seed's seed, says the LORD, from henceforth and forever.
verses.after: “As for me, this is my covenant with them,” says the **LORD**. “My Spirit upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, from your offspring’s mouths, or from the mouths of their offspring,” says the **LORD**, “from now and forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As for me, this is my covenant with them, says the LORD: my Spirit who is on you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, will not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your seed, nor out of the mouth of your seed's seed, says the LORD, from henceforth and forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps feminine city addressed through context and dawn image.
verses.before: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
verses.after: Rise, shine, for your light has come! The **LORD**’s glory has risen upon you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrasting illumination without erasing global darkness.
verses.before: For look, darkness covers the earth and deep darkness the peoples, but the LORD rises upon you, and the LORD’s glory appears over you.
verses.after: Look, darkness covers the earth and thick gloom the peoples, but the **LORD** rises upon you, and his glory appears over you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, darkness covers the earth and deep darkness the peoples, but the LORD rises upon you, and the LORD’s glory appears over you.

verses.rationale: Keeps nations and kings distinct.
verses.before: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
verses.after: Nations will walk toward your light, and kings toward the brightness of your dawn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.

verses.rationale: Preserves reunion formula and gendered children with carrying posture.
verses.before: Lift up your eyes round about, and see: they all gather themselves together, they come to you; your sons will come from far, and your daughters will be carried in the arms.
verses.after: Lift your eyes and look around: they have all gathered and come to you. Your sons come from far away; your daughters are carried on the hip.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your eyes round about, and see: they all gather themselves together, they come to you; your sons will come from far, and your daughters will be carried in the arms.

verses.rationale: Keeps physical heart reaction and maritime wealth.
verses.before: Then you will see and be radiant, and your heart will thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea will be turned to you, the wealth of the nations will come to you.
verses.after: Then you will see and beam with joy; your heart will tremble and open wide. For the sea’s abundance will turn toward you; the nations’ wealth will come to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will see and be radiant, and your heart will thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea will be turned to you, the wealth of the nations will come to you.

verses.rationale: Retains named trading peoples, animals and gifts.
verses.before: The multitude of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba will come; they will bring gold and frankincense, and will proclaim the praises of the LORD.
verses.after: A flood of camels will cover you, young camels from Midian and Ephah. They will all come from Sheba, carrying gold and frankincense and proclaiming the **LORD**’s praises.
verses.tsw_comparator: The multitude of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba will come; they will bring gold and frankincense, and will proclaim the praises of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps sacrificial purpose and repeated glory-root.
verses.before: All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered together to you, the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you; they will come up with acceptance on my altar; and I will glorify the house of my glory.
verses.after: All Kedar’s flocks will gather to you; Nebaioth’s rams will serve you. They will rise as acceptable offerings on my altar, and I will glorify my glorious house.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered together to you, the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you; they will come up with acceptance on my altar; and I will glorify the house of my glory.

verses.rationale: Preserves simile and question before ships named.
verses.before: Who are these who fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?
verses.after: Who are these flying like a cloud, like doves to their windows?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who are these who fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?

verses.rationale: Keeps divine first-person speaker and destination’s honor.
verses.before: Surely the islands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
verses.after: For the coastlands wait for me, with Tarshish’s ships in the lead, to bring your sons from far away, their silver and gold with them, for the name of the **LORD** your God, Israel’s Holy One, who has glorified you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely the islands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.

verses.rationale: Preserves subservience and divine striking rather than generic reconciliation.
verses.before: Foreigners will build up your walls, and their kings will minister to you: for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favor have I had mercy on you.
verses.after: Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. In my anger I struck you, but in my favor I have compassion on you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Foreigners will build up your walls, and their kings will minister to you: for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favor have I had mercy on you.

verses.rationale: Keeps continuous opening and led kings ambiguity.
verses.before: Your gates also will be open continually; they will not be shut day nor night; that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations, and their kings led captive.
verses.after: Your gates will always stand open; day and night they will not close, so the nations’ wealth may be brought to you, with their kings led in procession.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your gates also will be open continually; they will not be shut day nor night; that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations, and their kings led captive.

verses.rationale: Retains coercive threat in restoration vision.
verses.before: For that nation and kingdom that will not serve you will perish; yes, those nations will be utterly wasted.
verses.after: For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will perish; those nations will be utterly devastated.
verses.tsw_comparator: For that nation and kingdom that will not serve you will perish; yes, those nations will be utterly wasted.

verses.rationale: Maintains three tree terms consistently with 41:19 and temple-foot image.
verses.before: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir tree, the pine, and the box tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.
verses.after: Lebanon’s glory will come to you, cypress, plane and pine together, to beautify my sanctuary’s place. I will glorify the place of my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir tree, the pine, and the box tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.

verses.rationale: Keeps offspring of oppressors and city’s two titles.
verses.before: The sons of people who afflicted you will come bending to you; and all people who despised you will bow themselves down at the soles of your feet; and they will call you The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: The children of those who afflicted you will come bowing before you. All who despised you will bow at your feet and call you the **LORD**’s City, Zion of Israel’s Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of those who afflicted you will come bending to you; and all those who despised you will bow themselves down at the soles of your feet; and they will call you The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves deserted city reversal and durable joy.
verses.before: Whereas you have been forsaken and hated, so that no man passed through you, I will make you an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.
verses.after: Once abandoned and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from generation to generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whereas you have been forsaken and hated, so that no man passed through you, I will make you an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.

verses.rationale: Retains startling male royal nursing image rather than financial paraphrase.
verses.before: You will also suck the milk of the nations, and will suck the breast of kings; and you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
verses.after: You will suck the milk of nations and nurse at kings’ breasts. Then you will know that I am the **LORD**, your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will also suck the milk of the nations, and will suck the breast of kings; and you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four substitutions and transformed authority titles.
verses.before: For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron. I will also make your officers peace, and righteousness your ruler.
verses.after: Instead of bronze I will bring gold; instead of iron, silver; instead of wood, bronze; instead of stone, iron. I will appoint Peace as your overseer and Righteousness as your taskmaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron. I will also make your officers peace, and righteousness your ruler.

verses.rationale: Keeps civic naming and end of violence.
verses.before: Violence will no more be heard in your land, desolation nor destruction within your borders; but you will call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise.
verses.after: Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor devastation and destruction within your borders. You will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Violence will no more be heard in your land, desolation nor destruction within your borders; but you will call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise.

verses.rationale: Retains replacement of luminaries by divine light.
verses.before: The sun will be no more your light by day; neither for brightness will the moon give light to you: but the LORD will be to you an everlasting light, and your God your glory.
verses.after: The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor the moon give you brightness. The **LORD** will be your everlasting light, and your God your glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sun will be no more your light by day; neither for brightness will the moon give light to you: but the LORD will be to you an everlasting light, and your God your glory.

verses.rationale: Preserves sun-moon imagery even after previous replacement claim.
verses.before: Your sun will no more go down, neither will your moon withdraw itself; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be ended.
verses.after: Your sun will never again set, nor your moon withdraw, for the **LORD** will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will end.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your sun will no more go down, neither will your moon withdraw itself; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be ended.

verses.rationale: Follows read my planting and retains corporate shoot image.
verses.before: Your people also will be all righteous; they will inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.
verses.after: All your people will be righteous; they will possess the land forever— a shoot I planted, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your people also will be all righteous; they will inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.

verses.rationale: Preserves thousand and appointed-time/hasten tension.
verses.before: The little one will become a thousand, and the small one a strong nation; I, the LORD, will hasten it in its time.
verses.after: The smallest will become a thousand, the least a mighty nation. I am the **LORD**; at its time I will hasten it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The little one will become a thousand, and the small one a strong nation; I, the LORD, will hasten it in its time.

verses.rationale: Keeps anointed unnamed speaker, afflicted recipients and difficult release expression without importing Greek additions.
verses.before: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the oppressed; the LORD has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to captives and release to prisoners,
verses.after: The Spirit of the Lord **GOD** is upon me, because the **LORD** has anointed me to bring good news to the afflicted. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom to captives and release to prisoners,
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the oppressed; the LORD has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to captives and release to prisoners,

verses.rationale: Preserves vengeance alongside favor and differing year/day units.
verses.before: to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort everyone who mourn,
verses.after: to proclaim the **LORD**’s year of favor and our God’s day of vengeance, to comfort all who mourn,
verses.tsw_comparator: to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,

verses.rationale: Keeps three exchanges and oak image; headdress-ashes wordplay noted.
verses.before: to appoint to people who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may be glorified.
verses.after: to provide for those who mourn in Zion: to give them a splendid headdress instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a faint spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, the **LORD**’s planting, to display his glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: to appoint to those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may be glorified.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated ruin terms across restoration actions.
verses.before: They will build the old wastes, they will raise up the former desolations, and they will repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.
verses.after: They will rebuild ancient ruins, raise places devastated long ago, and renew ruined cities, places desolate for generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will build the old wastes, they will raise up the former desolations, and they will repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.

verses.rationale: Keeps foreign labor relationship rather than generic cooperation.
verses.before: Strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and your vinedressers.
verses.after: Strangers will stand and tend your flocks; foreigners will be your farmers and vine growers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and your vinedressers.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast of roles and nations’ resources.
verses.before: But you will be named the priests of the LORD; men will call you the ministers of our God: you will eat the wealth of the nations, and in their glory will you boast yourselves.
verses.after: But you will be called the **LORD**’s priests; you will be named ministers of our God. You will eat the nations’ wealth and take pride in their splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you will be named the priests of the LORD; men will call you the ministers of our God: you will eat the wealth of the nations, and in their glory will you boast yourselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps second-to-third person shift and repeated double.
verses.before: Instead of your shame you will have double; and instead of dishonor they will rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they will possess double; everlasting joy will be to them.
verses.after: Instead of your shame, a double portion; instead of humiliation, they will shout for joy over their share. So they will inherit a double portion in their land, and everlasting joy will be theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Instead of your shame you will have double; and instead of dishonor they will rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they will possess double; everlasting joy will be to them.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned burnt-offering vocalization; alternative wrongdoing noted.
verses.before: For I, the LORD, love justice, I hate robbery with iniquity; and I will give them their recompense in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
verses.after: “For I, the **LORD**, love justice; I hate robbery in a burnt offering. I will faithfully give them their reward and make an everlasting covenant with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I, the LORD, love justice, I hate robbery with iniquity; and I will give them their recompense in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.

verses.rationale: Preserves recognition of descendants as blessed.
verses.before: Their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples; everyone who see them will acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD has blessed.
verses.after: Their offspring will be known among the nations, their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will recognize that they are offspring the **LORD** has blessed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples; all who see them will acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD has blessed.

verses.rationale: Retains both bridegroom and bride and priestly verb nuance.
verses.before: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
verses.after: I rejoice greatly in the **LORD**; my whole being exults in my God. He has clothed me in garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom wearing a priestly headdress, like a bride adorning herself with jewels.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

verses.rationale: Keeps growth repetition and worldwide witness.
verses.before: For as the earth brings forth its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.
verses.after: As the earth brings out its shoots and a garden makes its seeds sprout, so the Lord **GOD** will make righteousness and praise sprout before all the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as the earth brings forth its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.

verses.rationale: Leaves first-person speaker unnamed and keeps two light images.
verses.before: For Zion’s sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness goes out like brightness and her salvation like a burning torch.
verses.after: For Zion’s sake I will not be silent; for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness shines like dawn and her salvation burns like a torch.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Zion’s sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness goes out like brightness and her salvation like a burning torch.

verses.rationale: Preserves name given by divine mouth.
verses.before: The nations will see your righteousness and all kings your glory; you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give.
verses.after: Nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the **LORD**’s mouth will pronounce.
verses.tsw_comparator: The nations will see your righteousness and all kings your glory; you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give.

verses.rationale: Keeps crown held rather than worn and hand/palm pairing.
verses.before: You will also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
verses.after: You will be a splendid crown in the **LORD**’s hand, a royal diadem in your God’s palm.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.

verses.rationale: Translates meaningful names and repeats marriage verb.
verses.before: You will no more be termed Forsaken; neither will your land any more be termed Desolate: but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
verses.after: You will no longer be called Abandoned, nor your land Desolate. You will be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married, for the **LORD** delights in you, and your land will be married.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will no more be termed Forsaken; neither will your land any more be termed Desolate: but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned sons and startling city-marriage metaphor; builders alternative noted.
verses.before: For as a young man marries a virgin, so will your sons marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so will your God rejoice over you.
verses.after: As a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you. As a bridegroom rejoices over a bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as a young man marries a virgin, so will your sons marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so will your God rejoice over you.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine-reminder role and unceasing watch.
verses.before: I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem; they will never hold their peace day nor night: you who call on the LORD, take no rest,
verses.after: On your walls, Jerusalem, I have stationed watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who remind the **LORD**, take no rest,
verses.tsw_comparator: I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem; they will never hold their peace day nor night: you who call on the LORD, take no rest,

verses.rationale: Preserves striking command to deny God rest.
verses.before: and give him no rest, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
verses.after: and give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her a praise in the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and give him no rest, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps oath limbs and protection of labor’s products.
verses.before: The LORD has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give your grain to be food for your enemies; and foreigners will not drink your new wine, for which you have labored:
verses.after: The **LORD** has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: “I will never again give your grain as food to your enemies, nor will foreigners drink the new wine you worked for.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give your grain to be food for your enemies; and foreigners will not drink your new wine, for which you have labored:

verses.rationale: Clarifies crop referents while retaining first-person courts.
verses.before: but people who have garnered it will eat it, and praise the LORD; and people who have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.
verses.after: Those who gather the grain will eat it and praise the **LORD**; those who gather the grapes will drink their wine in my holy courts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but those who have garnered it will eat it, and praise the LORD; and those who have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated movement and construction commands.
verses.before: Go through, go through the gates; prepare you the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a banner for the peoples.
verses.after: Pass through, pass through the gates! Prepare the people’s road. Build up, build up the highway; clear away the stones. Raise a banner over the peoples!
verses.tsw_comparator: Go through, go through the gates; prepare you the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a banner for the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keeps salvation personified and echoes 40:10.
verses.before: Look, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth, Say you to the daughter of Zion, Look, your salvation comes; look, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
verses.after: Look, the **LORD** has announced to the ends of the earth: “Say to Daughter Zion, ‘Look, your salvation is coming! Look, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth, Say you to the daughter of Zion, Look, your salvation comes; look, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural people and singular city’s distinct names.
verses.before: They will call them The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and you will be called Sought out, A city not forsaken.
