verses.after: They will call them Holy People, Redeemed of the **LORD**. And you will be called Sought Out, A City Not Abandoned.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will call them The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and you will be called Sought out, A city not forsaken.

verses.rationale: Marks question and divine answer while keeping Edom and Bozrah.
verses.before: Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this who is glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save.
verses.after: Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah in crimson-stained clothes, splendid in his garments, striding in his great strength? “It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this who is glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save.

verses.rationale: Retains question that exposes wine-blood metaphor.
verses.before: Why are you red in your clothing, and your garments like the one who treads in the wine vat?
verses.after: Why are your clothes red, your garments like those of someone treading a winepress?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why are you red in your clothing, and your garments like the one who treads in the wine vat?

verses.rationale: Preserves violent agency and alone emphasis.
verses.before: I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the peoples there was no man with me: yes, I trod them in my anger, and trampled them in my wrath; and their lifeblood is sprinkled on my garments, and I have stained all my clothing.
verses.after: “I have trodden the press alone; no one from the peoples was with me. I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their lifeblood spattered my clothes; I stained all my garments.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the peoples there was no man with me: yes, I trod them in my anger, and trampled them in my wrath; and their lifeblood is sprinkled on my garments, and I have stained all my clothing.

verses.rationale: Keeps redemption tied to vengeance, with distinct time units.
verses.before: For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.
verses.after: For a day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed had come.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.

verses.rationale: Echoes 59:16 but preserves fury rather than righteousness.
verses.before: I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: therefore my own arm brought salvation to me; and my wrath, it upheld me.
verses.after: I looked, but there was no helper; I was appalled, but there was no supporter. So my own arm brought me salvation, and my fury sustained me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: therefore my own arm brought salvation to me; and my wrath, it upheld me.

verses.rationale: Keeps intoxication and slaughter imagery together.
verses.before: I trod down the peoples in my anger, and made them drunk in my wrath, and I poured out their lifeblood on the earth.
verses.after: I trampled peoples in my anger, made them drunk in my fury, and poured their lifeblood onto the ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I trod down the peoples in my anger, and made them drunk in my wrath, and I poured out their lifeblood on the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves three divine names and hesed framing.
verses.before: I will recount the steadfast love of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has done for us, and the great goodness to the house of Israel shown according to compassion and the abundance of steadfast love.
verses.after: I will recount the **LORD**’s faithful acts of love, the **LORD**’s praiseworthy deeds, for all the **LORD** has done for us— his great goodness to the house of Israel, shown according to his compassion and his abundant faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will recount the steadfast love of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has done for us, and the great goodness to the house of Israel shown according to compassion and the abundance of steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine expectation that following rebellion contradicts.
verses.before: For he said, Surely, they are my people, children who will not deal falsely: so he was their Savior.
verses.after: He said, “Surely they are my people, children who will not deal falsely.” So he became their Savior.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he said, Surely, they are my people, children who will not deal falsely: so he was their Savior.

verses.rationale: Follows read to-him distress; written not and messenger interpretations noted.
verses.before: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
verses.after: In all their distress he was distressed, and the messenger of his presence saved them. In his love and pity he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
verses.tsw_comparator: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them, and carried them all the days of old.

verses.rationale: Retains reversal and direct divine hostility.
verses.before: But they rebelled, and grieved his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and himself fought against them.
verses.after: But they rebelled and grieved his holy Spirit. So he turned into their enemy; he himself fought against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they rebelled, and grieved his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and himself fought against them.

verses.rationale: Chooses people as ambiguous remembering subject; preserves plural shepherds.
verses.before: Then he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, Where is the one who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? where is the one who put his holy Spirit among them?
verses.after: Then his people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: “Where is the one who brought them up from the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is the one who put his holy Spirit among them,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, Where is the one who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? where is the one who put his holy Spirit in the midst of them?

verses.rationale: Keeps arm beside Moses and purpose of name.
verses.before: who caused his glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses? who divided the waters before them, to make himself an everlasting name?
verses.after: who sent his glorious arm at Moses’ right hand, who split the waters before them to make an everlasting name for himself,
verses.tsw_comparator: who caused his glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses? who divided the waters before them, to make himself an everlasting name?

verses.rationale: Preserves dry-ground horse simile in water crossing.
verses.before: who led them through the depths, as a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble?
verses.after: who led them through the depths? Like a horse in open country, they did not stumble.
verses.tsw_comparator: who led them through the depths, as a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble?

verses.rationale: Keeps animal comparison and shift from he to you.
verses.before: As the livestock that go down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused them to rest; so did you lead your people, to make yourself a glorious name.
verses.after: Like cattle going down into a valley, the **LORD**’s Spirit gave them rest. So you led your people to make yourself a glorious name.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As the livestock that go down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused them to rest; so did you lead your people, to make yourself a glorious name.

verses.rationale: Retains singular me within communal lament and bodily compassion.
verses.before: Look down from heaven, and see from the habitation of your holiness and of your glory: where are your zeal and your mighty acts? the yearning of your heart and your compassion is restrained toward me.
verses.after: Look down from heaven and see, from your holy and glorious dwelling. Where are your zeal and your mighty deeds? Your deep stirring and compassion are withheld from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look down from heaven, and see from the habitation of your holiness and of your glory: where are your zeal and your mighty acts? the yearning of your heart and your compassion is restrained toward me.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancestral nonrecognition and repeated Father.
verses.before: For you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us, and Israel does not acknowledge us: you, the LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from everlasting is your name.
verses.after: For you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not recognize us. You, **LORD**, are our Father; Our Redeemer from of Old is your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us, and Israel does not acknowledge us: you, the LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from everlasting is your name.

verses.rationale: Keeps accusatory divine causatives instead of softening to mere permission.
verses.before: O the LORD, why do you make us to err from your ways, and harden our heart from your fear? Return for your servants' sake, the tribes of your inheritance.
verses.after: Why, **LORD**, do you make us wander from your ways and harden our hearts so we do not fear you? Return for your servants’ sake, the tribes of your inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: O the LORD, why do you make us to err from your ways, and harden our heart from your fear? Return for your servants' sake, the tribes of your inheritance.

verses.rationale: Preserves unspecified possession object and sanctuary harm.
verses.before: Your holy people possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary.
verses.after: Your holy people possessed it only a little while; our adversaries have trampled your sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your holy people possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Maps first part of Hebrew 63:19 to public label without duplicating following plea.
verses.before: We are become as they over whom you never bear rule, as people who were not called by your name.
verses.after: We have become like those you never ruled, those over whom your name was never called.
verses.tsw_comparator: We are become as they over whom you never bear rule, as those who were not called by your name.

source_partition.reason: Existing public numbering splits original Isa 63:19 between the identity lament and the wish for divine descent. Full original record hash retained for each part.

verses.rationale: Maps latter part of Hebrew 63:19 to public 64:1; keeps wish and divine descent.
verses.before: Oh, that you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains might quake at your presence—
verses.after: If only you would tear open the heavens and come down, so the mountains would quake before you!
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh, that you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains might quake at your presence—

source_partition.reason: Existing public numbering splits original Isa 63:19 between the identity lament and the wish for divine descent. Full original record hash retained for each part.

verses.rationale: Maps Hebrew 64:1; preserves two fire similes and purpose.
verses.before: as when fire kindles the brushwood, and the fire causes the waters to boil; to make your name known to your adversaries, that the nations may tremble at your presence!
verses.after: As fire ignites brushwood, as fire makes water boil, make your name known to your adversaries, so nations tremble before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: as when fire kindles the brushwood, and the fire causes the waters to boil; to make your name known to your adversaries, that the nations may tremble at your presence!

verses.rationale: Keeps recalled descent and repetition from plea.
verses.before: When you did terrible things which we did not look for, you came down, the mountains quaked at your presence.
verses.after: When you did awesome things we did not expect, you came down, and mountains quaked before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you did terrible things which we did not look for, you came down, the mountains quaked at your presence.

verses.rationale: Preserves hearing/seeing sequence and waiting recipients.
verses.before: For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the eye seen a God besides you, who works for the one who waits for him.
verses.after: From ancient times no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen a God besides you who acts for those who wait for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the eye seen a God besides you, who works for the one who waits for him.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult in-them clause rather than silently reconstructing certainty.
verses.before: You meet the one who rejoices and works righteousness, people who remember you in your ways: look, you were angry, and we sinned: in them have we been of long time; and will we be saved?
verses.after: You meet those who rejoice and do righteousness, who remember you in your ways. Look, you were angry, and we sinned; we have long been in them—can we be saved?
verses.tsw_comparator: You meet the one who rejoices and works righteousness, those who remember you in your ways: look, you were angry, and we sinned: in them have we been of long time; and will we be saved?

verses.rationale: Preserves ritual bodily image and repeated all-us confession.
verses.before: For we have all become as one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is as a polluted garment: and we all fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
verses.after: All of us have become like someone unclean; all our righteous deeds are like a menstrual cloth. All of us wither like a leaf, and our offenses carry us away like wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we have all become as one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is as a polluted garment: and we all fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine causative and literal melting image in idiomatic context.
verses.before: There is none who calls on your name, who stirs up himself to take hold of you; for you have hid your face from us, and have consumed us by means of our iniquities.
verses.after: No one calls on your name or stirs themselves to take hold of you, for you have hidden your face from us and made us melt under the power of our offenses.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is none who calls on your name, who stirs up himself to take hold of you; for you have hid your face from us, and have consumed us by means of our iniquities.

verses.rationale: Preserves father and artisan metaphors together.
verses.before: But now, the LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.
verses.after: Yet now, **LORD**, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you are our potter; all of us are the work of your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now, the LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps petition’s repeated all-us claim.
verses.before: Don't be furious, the LORD, neither remember iniquity forever: see, look, we beg you, we are all your people.
verses.after: Do not be so deeply angry, **LORD**; do not remember guilt forever. Please look: all of us are your people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Don't be furious, the LORD, neither remember iniquity forever: see, look, we beg you, we are all your people.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated wilderness and named city.
verses.before: Your holy cities are become a wilderness, Zion is become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
verses.after: Your holy cities have become wilderness; Zion has become wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your holy cities are become a wilderness, Zion is become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete destroyed temple and wider treasured places.
verses.before: Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised you, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant places are laid waste.
verses.after: Our holy and glorious house, where our ancestors praised you, has been burned with fire; all we treasured lies in ruins.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised you, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant places are laid waste.

verses.rationale: Ends lament in unresolved questions, not supplied reassurance.
verses.before: Will you refrain yourself for these things, the LORD? will you hold your peace, and afflict us very sore?
verses.after: In the face of all this, will you hold back, **LORD**? Will you stay silent and afflict us so deeply?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you refrain yourself for these things, the LORD? will you hold your peace, and afflict us very sore?

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled availability and unidentified nation.
verses.before: I was ready to be sought by people who did not ask; I was ready to be found by people who did not seek me. I said, “Here I am, here I am,” to a nation that did not call on my name.
verses.after: “I made myself available to those who did not ask; I let myself be found by those who did not seek me. I said, ‘Here I am, here I am,’ to a nation that did not call on my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was ready to be sought by those who did not ask; I was ready to be found by those who did not seek me. I said, “Here I am, here I am,” to a nation that did not call on my name.

verses.rationale: Keeps extended divine gesture and moral path.
verses.before: I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;
verses.after: All day long I spread out my hands to a rebellious people walking a way that is not good, following their own thoughts.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;

verses.rationale: Preserves specific ritual settings without invented deity.
verses.before: a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks;
verses.after: These people continually provoke me to my face, sacrificing in gardens and burning offerings on bricks,
verses.tsw_comparator: a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks;

verses.rationale: Follows read broth and retains prohibited food and grave rites.
verses.before: who sit among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat pig's flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
verses.after: sitting among graves, spending the night in secret places, eating pig’s flesh, with broth of offensive things in their pots.
verses.tsw_comparator: who sit among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat pig's flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;

verses.rationale: Preserves holiness claim and divine bodily irritation.
verses.before: who say, Stand by yourself, do not come near to me, for I am holier than you. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all the day.
verses.after: They say, ‘Keep to yourself! Do not come near me, for I am too holy for you.’ These are smoke in my nostrils, a fire burning all day.
verses.tsw_comparator: who say, Stand by yourself, do not come near to me, for I am holier than you. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all the day.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated repayment and ledger-like image.
verses.before: Look, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, yes, I will recompense into their bosom,
verses.after: Look, it is written before me. I will not be silent; I will repay, repay right into their laps
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, yes, I will recompense into their bosom,

verses.rationale: Retains you/their shift and inherited plus current offenses.
verses.before: your own iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the LORD, who have burned incense on the mountains, and blasphemed me on the hills; so will I first measure their work into their bosom.
verses.after: your offenses and your ancestors’ offenses together,” says the **LORD**. “They burned offerings on mountains and insulted me on hills. I will first measure their payment into their laps.”
verses.tsw_comparator: your own iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the LORD, who have burned incense on the mountains, and blasphemed me on the hills; therefore will I first measure their work into their bosom.

verses.rationale: Keeps saved grape cluster as limited preservation image.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, Don't destroy it, for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sake, that I may not destroy them all.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “As when new wine is found in a cluster and someone says, ‘Do not destroy it; there is a blessing in it,’ so I will act for my servants’ sake and not destroy them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, Don't destroy it, for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sake, that I may not destroy them all.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancestral names and specific mountain inheritance.
verses.before: I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains; and my chosen will inherit it, and my servants will dwell there.
verses.after: I will bring offspring out of Jacob, and from Judah an heir to my mountains. My chosen ones will possess the land, and my servants will live there.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains; and my chosen will inherit it, and my servants will dwell there.

verses.rationale: Keeps two places and animal uses.
verses.before: Sharon will be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down in, for my people who have sought me.
verses.after: Sharon will become pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for my people who seek me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sharon will be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down in, for my people who have sought me.

verses.rationale: Translates deity names with capitals and preserves ritual meal.
verses.before: But you who forsake the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune, and who fill up mixed wine to Destiny;
verses.after: But you who abandon the **LORD**, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny—
verses.tsw_comparator: But you who forsake the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune, and who fill up mixed wine to Destiny;

verses.rationale: Preserves Destiny/destine pun and repeated failed response.
verses.before: I will destine you to the sword, and you will all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not hear; but you did what was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I did not delight.
verses.after: I will destine you for the sword; all of you will bow down for slaughter, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen. You did what was evil in my eyes and chose what did not please me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will destine you to the sword, and you will all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not hear; but you did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I did not delight.

verses.rationale: Keeps three repeated look-servants contrasts.
verses.before: So thus says the Lord GOD, Look, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; look, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty; look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed;
verses.after: So this is what the Lord **GOD** says: “Look, my servants will eat, but you will hunger. Look, my servants will drink, but you will thirst. Look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be ashamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD, Look, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; look, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty; look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed;

verses.rationale: Retains bodily emotional contrast and howling intensity.
verses.before: look, my servants will sing for joy of heart, but you will cry for sorrow of heart, and will wail for vexation of spirit.
verses.after: Look, my servants will sing from glad hearts, but you will cry out from aching hearts and howl from broken spirits.
verses.tsw_comparator: look, my servants will sing for joy of heart, but you will cry for sorrow of heart, and will wail for vexation of spirit.

verses.rationale: Marks curse-formula interpretation; alternative direct prediction noted.
verses.before: You will leave your name for a curse to my chosen; and the Lord GOD will kill you; and he will call his servants by another name:
verses.after: You will leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones: ‘May the Lord **GOD** put you to death!’ But he will call his servants by another name.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will leave your name for a curse to my chosen; and the Lord GOD will kill you; and he will call his servants by another name:

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated Hebrew Amen title with vocabulary explanation.
verses.before: so that the one who blesses himself in the earth will bless himself in the God of truth; and the one who swears in the earth will swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hid from my eyes.
verses.after: Whoever seeks a blessing in the land will seek it by the God of Amen, and whoever swears in the land will swear by the God of Amen. For the former troubles are forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that the one who blesses himself in the earth will bless himself in the God of truth; and the one who swears in the earth will swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hid from my eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps creation claim without importing later cosmology.
verses.before: For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth; the former things will not be remembered or come to mind.
verses.after: For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered nor come to mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth; the former things will not be remembered or come to mind.

verses.rationale: Retains city created as joy, not merely given joy.
verses.before: But be you glad and rejoice forever in what I create; for, look, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.
verses.after: Instead, rejoice and be glad forever in what I create, for look, I am creating Jerusalem as gladness and her people as joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: But be you glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, look, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine joy and abolished lament sounds.
verses.before: I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people; and there will be heard in her no more the voice of weeping and the voice of crying.
verses.after: I will be glad in Jerusalem and rejoice in my people. No sound of weeping or cry of distress will be heard in her again.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people; and there will be heard in her no more the voice of weeping and the voice of crying.

verses.rationale: Keeps death within renewed-world vision; sinner alternative noted.
verses.before: There will be no more there an infant of days, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the child will die one hundred years old, and the sinner being one hundred years old will be accursed.
verses.after: No infant there will live only a few days, no old person fail to complete their years. Someone dying at a hundred will be a youth; someone falling short of a hundred will be considered cursed.
verses.tsw_comparator: There will be no more there an infant of days, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the child will die one hundred years old, and the sinner being one hundred years old will be accursed.

verses.rationale: Retains enjoyment of own labor.
verses.before: They will build houses, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.
verses.after: They will build houses and live in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will build houses, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.

verses.rationale: Keeps tree longevity and reversal of dispossession.
verses.before: They will not build, and another inhabit; they will not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree will be the days of my people, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands.
verses.after: They will not build for another to inhabit nor plant for another to eat. My people’s days will be like a tree’s days; my chosen ones will long enjoy the work of their hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not build, and another inhabit; they will not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree will be the days of my people, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands.

verses.rationale: Preserves childbirth free of calamity, not generic success promise.
verses.before: They will not labor in vain, nor bring forth for calamity; for they are the seed of the blessed of the LORD, and their offspring with them.
verses.after: They will not labor for nothing nor bear children for terror, for they are offspring blessed by the **LORD**, and their descendants are with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not labor in vain, nor bring forth for calamity; for they are the seed of the blessed of the LORD, and their offspring with them.

verses.rationale: Retains temporal reversal of earlier unanswered prayer.
verses.before: It will happen that, before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
verses.after: Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen that, before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.

verses.rationale: Keeps serpent’s dust exception and echoes 11:9.
verses.before: The wolf and the lamb will feed together; the lion will eat straw like the ox, and dust will be the serpent’s food. They will not hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain, says the LORD.
verses.after: Wolf and lamb will graze together; the lion will eat straw like cattle, and dust will be the serpent’s food. They will neither harm nor destroy on all my holy mountain,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wolf and the lamb will feed together; the lion will eat straw like the ox, and dust will be the serpent’s food. They will not hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves temple question rather than categorical denial of worship.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me, and what place will be my resting place?
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Heaven is my throne, and earth my footstool. What kind of house could you build for me? What place could be my resting place?
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me, and what place will be my resting place?

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated all-these and favored vulnerable hearer.
verses.before: My hand made all these things, and so all these things came to be, says the LORD. But this is the one to whom I will look: one who is poor and crushed in spirit and trembles at my word.
verses.after: My hand made all these things, and so all these things came to be,” declares the **LORD**. “But this is the one I look toward: the afflicted and crushed in spirit, who trembles at my word.
verses.tsw_comparator: My hand made all these things, and so all these things came to be, says the LORD. But this is the one to whom I will look: one who is poor and crushed in spirit and trembles at my word.

verses.rationale: Preserves terse paired acts; equivalence versus combined practices noted.
verses.before: The one who slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person; the one who sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog’s neck; the one who presents a grain offering, like one who presents pig’s blood; the one who makes a memorial offering of frankincense, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.
verses.after: One slaughters an ox—and kills a person; one sacrifices a lamb—and breaks a dog’s neck; one brings a grain offering—and pig’s blood; one burns memorial incense—and blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways and delight in their offensive things.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person; the one who sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog’s neck; the one who presents a grain offering, like one who presents pig’s blood; the one who makes a memorial offering of frankincense, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.

verses.rationale: Echoes 65:12 and repeated choosing on both sides.
verses.before: So I also will choose their delusions and bring upon them what they dread, because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they did not listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I did not delight in.”
verses.after: So I too will choose harsh treatment for them and bring upon them what they dread, because I called and no one answered, I spoke and they did not listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what did not please me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I also will choose their delusions and bring upon them what they dread, because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they did not listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I did not delight in.”

verses.rationale: Retains hostile brothers’ religious taunt and ambiguous tone.
verses.before: Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at the LORD’s word: “Your brothers who hate you and cast you out because of my name have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified, so that we may see your joy!’ But they are the ones who will be put to shame.”
verses.after: Hear the **LORD**’s word, you who tremble at his word: “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of my name say, ‘Let the **LORD** be glorified, so we may see your joy!’ But they will be put to shame.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at the LORD’s word: “Your brothers who hate you and cast you out because of my name have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified, so that we may see your joy!’ But they are the ones who will be put to shame.”

verses.rationale: Keeps threefold sound build-up.
verses.before: A sound of tumult from the city! A sound from the temple! The sound of the LORD repaying enemies what is due.
verses.after: A sound of uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! The sound of the **LORD** repaying his enemies what they deserve!
verses.tsw_comparator: A sound of tumult from the city! A sound from the temple! The sound of the LORD repaying enemies what is due.

verses.rationale: Preserves miraculous chronology and male child.
verses.before: Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before her pain came upon her, she delivered a son.
verses.after: Before she labored, she gave birth; before pain came upon her, she delivered a son.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before her pain came upon her, she delivered a son.

verses.rationale: Keeps four questions and mother-city identification.
verses.before: Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen things like these? Can a land be born in one day? Can a nation be brought forth in one moment? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.
verses.after: Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen anything like it? Can a land be brought forth in one day, a nation born in a moment? Yet as soon as Zion labored, she gave birth to her children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen things like these? Can a land be born in one day? Can a nation be brought forth in one moment? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.

verses.rationale: Preserves both childbirth questions and divine titles.
verses.before: “Will I bring to the point of birth and not cause delivery?” says the LORD. “Will I, who cause birth, close the womb?” says your God.
verses.after: “Would I bring to the point of birth and not deliver?” says the **LORD**. “Would I, who bring about birth, close the womb?” says your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Will I bring to the point of birth and not cause delivery?” says the LORD. “Will I, who cause birth, close the womb?” says your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps mourners invited into joy.
verses.before: Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her; rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her,
verses.after: Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad in her, all who love her. Rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn over her,
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her; rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her,

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal bodily nourishment.
verses.before: so that you may nurse and be satisfied from her comforting breast, so that you may drink deeply and delight in the abundance of her glory.
verses.after: so you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breast, so you may drink deeply and delight in her overflowing glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may nurse and be satisfied from her comforting breast, so that you may drink deeply and delight in the abundance of her glory.

verses.rationale: Keeps water and nursing images side by side.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “Look, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream. You will nurse; you will be carried on the hip and bounced upon the knees.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “Look, I will extend peace to her like a river and the nations’ glory like an overflowing stream. You will nurse, be carried on the hip, and be dandled on the knees.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “Look, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream. You will nurse; you will be carried on the hip and bounced upon the knees.

verses.rationale: Preserves direct maternal divine comparison and repeated comfort.
verses.before: As one whom a mother comforts, so I will comfort you; in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
verses.after: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; in Jerusalem you will be comforted.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As one whom a mother comforts, so I will comfort you; in Jerusalem you will be comforted.

verses.rationale: Keeps bones-growth image and contrasting divine responses.
verses.before: You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will flourish like new grass. The hand of the LORD will be known toward the LORD’s servants, and indignation toward the LORD’s enemies.
verses.after: You will see, and your hearts will rejoice; your bones will flourish like grass. The **LORD**’s hand will be known among his servants, and his indignation among his enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will flourish like new grass. The hand of the LORD will be known toward the LORD’s servants, and indignation toward the LORD’s enemies.

verses.rationale: Retains fiery warrior arrival.
verses.before: For look, the LORD will come in fire, and the LORD’s chariots like the whirlwind, to render anger in fury and rebuke with flames of fire.
verses.after: For look, the **LORD** will come in fire, his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger in fury and his rebuke in flames of fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, the LORD will come in fire, and the LORD’s chariots like the whirlwind, to render anger in fury and rebuke with flames of fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit deaths and repeated divine name.
verses.before: For by fire the LORD will execute judgment, and by the LORD’s sword, upon all flesh; and many will be those slain by the LORD.
verses.after: For with fire and his sword the **LORD** will judge all flesh, and many will be slain by the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by fire the LORD will execute judgment, and by the LORD’s sword, upon all flesh; and many will be those slain by the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps ritual purification used in condemned worship and all foods; read feminine one noted.
verses.before: People who sanctify and purify themselves to enter the gardens, following one in the midst, eating pig flesh, the abomination, and the mouse, will come to an end together, says the LORD.
verses.after: “Those who consecrate and purify themselves to enter the gardens, following the one in the middle, eating pig’s flesh, offensive things and mice—they will come to an end together,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who sanctify and purify themselves to enter the gardens, following one in the midst, eating pig flesh, the abomination, and the mouse, will come to an end together, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves incomplete opening rather than silently adding know; supplied time clarifies following feminine participle.
verses.before: For I know their works and their thoughts. The time is coming to gather all nations and languages; they will come and see my glory.
verses.after: “And I—their deeds and their thoughts! The time is coming to gather all nations and languages; they will come and see my glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know their works and their thoughts. The time is coming to gather all nations and languages; they will come and see my glory.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Pul rather than Put and complete geographical list.
verses.before: I will set a sign among them, and from them I will send survivors to the nations—to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, and to distant coastlands that have not heard my fame or seen my glory. They will declare my glory among the nations.
verses.after: I will set a sign among them and send survivors from them to the nations: Tarshish, Pul, Lud—those who draw the bow—Tubal, Javan and distant coastlands that have not heard of me or seen my glory. They will tell of my glory among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set a sign among them, and from them I will send survivors to the nations—to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, and to distant coastlands that have not heard my fame or seen my glory. They will declare my glory among the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves transport list and human-offering comparison; final animal term uncertain.
verses.before: They will bring all your brothers and sisters from all the nations as an offering to the LORD—on horses, in chariots, in wagons, on mules, and on dromedaries—to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the people of Israel bring a grain offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD.
verses.after: They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the **LORD**—on horses, in chariots and wagons, on mules and swift beasts—to my holy mountain, Jerusalem,” says the **LORD**, “just as the Israelites bring a grain offering in a clean vessel to the **LORD**’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will bring all your brothers and sisters from all the nations as an offering to the LORD—on horses, in chariots, in wagons, on mules, and on dromedaries—to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the people of Israel bring a grain offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Leaves them’s antecedent unresolved rather than restricting inclusion.
verses.before: And from among them I will also take some as priests and Levites, says the LORD.
verses.after: And I will also take some of them as priests and Levites,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: And from among them I will also take some as priests and Levites, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps creation’s endurance as analogy for people’s continuity.
verses.before: For as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will remain before me, says the LORD, so your offspring and your name will remain.
verses.after: “For as the new heavens and new earth I am making will endure before me,” declares the **LORD**, “so your offspring and your name will endure.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will remain before me, says the LORD, so your offspring and your name will remain.

verses.rationale: Retains calendar observances and universal bodily worship.
verses.before: From new moon to new moon and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before me, says the LORD.
verses.after: From new moon to new moon and Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh will come to bow before me,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: From new moon to new moon and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves corpses, unending worm/fire and disturbing final word without importing later doctrine.
verses.before: They will go out and look upon the corpses of people who rebelled against me, for their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched; they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.
verses.after: “They will go out and look at the corpses of those who rebelled against me. Their worm will not die, and their fire will not go out. They will be an abhorrence to all flesh.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They will go out and look upon the corpses of those who rebelled against me, for their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched; they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.

comparative_references.scope: All 851 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
